entries.title: Node-editor palette specs drift from the sidecar handlers: 7 of 10 built-in nodes wire ports/config keys the handler never reads, so composed graphs return None/0/'' as status ok or fail on the UI's own option values
entries.repro: [COD-workflow-engine-1] Proof run (scratchpad wf/proof.py) of a spec shaped exactly as the palette builds it: json_path wired on targetPort 'input' -> {extracted: None}; logic.branch wired on 'condition' -> {true_path: None, false_path: None}; flow.sleep config {duration_ms: 1000} -> slept 0.0; logic.compare op 'ne' (the palette's option) -> 'unknown op ne'; notify_desktop wired on 'message' -> message ''. Every node except compare reports status ok.
entries.evidence: [COD-workflow-engine-1] src/modules/node-editor/node-registry.ts:102-165 (ports: compute.indicator out 'values', agent_invoke out 'response', branch in 'condition' out 'true'/'false', compare in 'left'/'right', notify in 'message', json_path in 'input' out 'value', sleep in 'trigger' out 'done'), node-registry.ts:438-509 (config keys 'indicator'+'period', 'prompt', op option 'ne', 'duration_ms'); vs sidecar/services/workflow_nodes/builtin.py:109 ('indicator_id'), :122 (out 'result'), :167 ('prompt_template'), :207 (out 'content'), :235,249-250 ('value' -> 'true_path'/'false_path'), :258-265,281-282 ('a'/'b', 'neq'), :335 ('message_template' default '{value}'), :391-392 ('value' -> 'extracted'), :406,414 ('seconds' -> 'value'/'slept'); node-registry.ts:162 says 'milliseconds', handler clamps seconds -- refuter admitted_with_correction (high->high): The palette/handler drift is real and there is no translation layer: graph-state.flowToSpec copies handle ids verbatim into sourcePort/targetPort and config keys verbatim, and the engine wires inputs[target_port] = upstream[source_port]. Every mismatch reproduced (json_path 'input' -> extracted None, sleep duration_ms -> slept 0.0, compare 'ne' -> unknown op, indicator -> missing indicator_id, notify 'message' -> message ''). Correction: it is 7 of 10 built-ins, not 9 - data.fetch_quote, data.fetch_history and action.log ports/config match their handlers.
entries.root_cause: The node contract (ports + config schema) is hand-copied into TS with no parity test; graph-state.flowToSpec copies handle ids and config keys verbatim, so every name mismatch silently wires nothing.
entries.fix_shape: Make handler registration carry its port/config spec (register_node_type(type_id, handler, spec)), expose GET /workflow/node-types and derive the palette from it; interim: correct the 7 TS specs to the handler keys (indicator_id, prompt_template, value/true_path/false_path, a/b + 'neq', message_template, value/extracted, seconds) and add a pytest+vitest parity test that diffs palette ports/config against the registered specs.

entries.title: Workflow agent node launders every failure (bad agent id, 401, rate limit, network) into the literal '(no provider key configured)' with status ok, which downstream nodes consume as the agent's answer
entries.repro: [COD-workflow-engine-2] Any ai.agent_invoke failure (bad agent_id, rate limit, 401, network) -> handler catches it (builtin.py:197), content is replaced with the literal '(no provider key configured)' (builtin.py:205-206) and the node returns normally -> engine records status 'ok' and downstream nodes consume the sentinel string as the agent's answer.
entries.evidence: [COD-workflow-engine-2] sidecar/services/workflow_nodes/builtin.py:20-23 (CI motive stated), :156-162 (docstring claims env VYSTED_<PROV>_API_KEY fallback), :170 (api_key from node config), :183-206; sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py:1229-1239 (no env-key read; on_round_usage defaults None); src/modules/node-editor/node-registry.ts:448-463 (UI offers no provider/key field) -- refuter admitted_with_correction (high->high): Core claim holds: any exception or LLMErrorEvent with no streamed text becomes content '(no provider key configured)' and the handler returns normally, so the engine records status ok and downstream nodes consume the sentinel; the docstring's VYSTED_<PROV>_API_KEY env fallback does not exist anywhere in the sidecar. Corrections: the real error string is kept in outputs['error'] (not fully erased), and the BudgetGuard point is overstated - the foreground POST /agents/{id}/invoke route also omits on_round_usage; only durable Delegate runs are metered, so workflows are not a unique leak.
entries.root_cause: A CI-motivated special case in the handler catches every exception/LLMErrorEvent and substitutes a sentinel string; the docstring's VYSTED_<PROV>_API_KEY env fallback does not exist and the node editor supplies no provider/key, so in-app the node realistically always hits the sentinel. A config api_key (documented override, reachable via MCP save_workflow) is persisted plaintext in workflows.db spec_json.
entries.fix_shape: Raise on LLMErrorEvent/exception (the engine already turns raises into node-error); drop config api_key and thread the foreground BYOK creds from the run request like agents.invoke does; pass a BudgetGuard on_round_usage callback; move the CI stub into the test fixture. Pin: a test that an adapter error yields node status 'error', and that a spec carrying api_key is rejected on save.

entries.title: logic.branch does not branch: both downstream subgraphs always run (side effects such as notify or LLM spend fire on the un-taken path), and the strings 'false'/'no'/'0'/'off' route TRUE

entries.title: Concurrent quant pricings corrupt each other through QuantLib's process-global evaluation date (a valid call priced at 0.0 in 1413 of 3000 overlapping runs), and the async quant agent tools price synchronously on the event loop
entries.repro: [COD-macro-quant-2] Two threads call services.quant._common.set_evaluation_date with different dates then read ql.Settings.instance().evaluationDate: thread A set 2026-05-16, thread B set 2030-01-02, both observe 'January 2nd, 2030'. The four /quant routes are plain sync `def`, so FastAPI runs them concurrently in the anyio worker threadpool -> two simultaneous pricing calls with different valuation_date can each be served the other's date.
entries.evidence: [COD-macro-quant-2] sidecar/services/quant/_common.py:34-41 (set_evaluation_date writes the process global), _common.py:57 (build_bsm_process calls it on every price), sidecar/services/quant/bonds.py:52 and sidecar/services/quant/yield_curve.py:70 (write it directly), sidecar/routers/quant.py:37,46,55,64 (all four routes are sync `def`, unlike routers/macro.py:47,60,72 which are async def) -- refuter admitted_with_correction (critical->high): Mechanism is real and worse than a date mix-up: the four /quant routes are sync def (threadpool) and every engine writes the process-global ql.Settings evaluationDate before a lazy NPV(); a two-thread probe returned price 0.0 (option judged already expired) for 1413 of 3000 pricings of a valid ITM-ish call when a second thread priced with a later valuation date. Severity corrected critical->high only because the trigger needs two overlapping quant computations with DIFFERENT valuation dates in a single-user desktop (panel computes are click-driven; the async agent tools call options.price synchronously on the event loop, quant_tools.py:54, which also blocks the loop for large binomial_steps).
entries.root_cause: ql.Settings.instance().evaluationDate is a process singleton; the four /quant routes are sync def (anyio threadpool) and every engine writes the global before a lazy NPV(), so two overlapping pricings with different valuation dates read each other's date.
entries.fix_shape: Module-level threading.Lock in _common.py wrapping set-date-through-NPV as one critical section (used by options, greeks, bonds, yield_curve), plus await asyncio.to_thread(...) in the four quant_tools handlers. Pin with the two-thread probe as a pytest. Must land before/with R15-CODE-PLATFORM entry for quant workflow nodes (moving those to to_thread without the lock makes this race reachable from workflows too).

entries.evidence: COD-portfolio-5: src/modules/portfolio/PortfolioPanel.tsx:486-497 (weight written unconditionally at 495), 474-485 (header row: no Currency column); contrast 400-411 (the Wt column is dropped when mixedCurrencies, with the rationale at 400-401) and src/modules/portfolio/metrics.ts:26-32,144-147 (weight divides by the cross-currency... || refuter (COD-portfolio-5, admitted): Confirmed. handleExport writes Weight % whenever weight !== null, and weight is marketValue / totalMarketValue, a cross-currency sum when currencies are mixed. entries.root_cause: handleExport writes weight = marketValue/totalMarketValue unconditionally and has no Currency column.
entries.fix_shape: Add a Currency column from quote.currency and emit '' for Weight % when summary.mixedCurrencies; pin with a RELIANCE+AAPL export test.

entries.title: The research page fetcher follows redirects without re-checking the target, so a public URL that 302s to loopback/link-local/LAN is fetched and its HTML/text/PDF body lands in the brief (SSRF guard checks only the input URL)
entries.repro: A search result URL on a public host answers 302 -> http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ (or http://127.0.0.1:<sidecar port>/agents, or a LAN host). fetch_page calls is_public_http_url ONCE on the input URL (extract.py:593), which passes; httpx_fetch opens its client with follow_redirects=True (transport.py:108); the redirected body is main-content-extracted and returned as `content`, then wrapped into the synthesis prompt and the published brief. The post-redirect URL is available as fetched.url and is stored as `final_url` (extract.py:635) but never re-validated. Same hole on the PDF lane: extract.py:307 follow_redirects=True and the curl_cffi lane at extract.py:293-294 (follows redirects by default).
entries.evidence: COD-research-extraction-synthesis-1: sidecar/services/search/extract.py:593, sidecar/services/search/extract.py:635, sidecar/services/search/extract.py:307, sidecar/services/search/extract.py:293, sidecar/services/search/transport.py:108, sidecar/services/search/extract.py:12 || refuter (COD-research-extraction-synthesis-1, admitted_with_correction): The bypass is real and I reproduced it live. fetch_page checks is_public_http_url once, on the input URL only (extract.py:593). httpx_fetch then follows redirects (transport.py:108), the PDF lane does too (extract.py:307), and nothing re-checks fetched.url. Two corrections: the sidecar's own loopback JSON endpoints (the raw finding's /agents example) are rejected by the content-type filter at extract.py:620-621, s... || refuter severity_final: COD-research-extraction-synthesis-1=high
entries.root_cause: fetch_page calls is_public_http_url once on the input; httpx_fetch (follow_redirects=True), the PDF lane and the curl_cffi lane follow redirects and nothing re-validates fetched.url; DNS rebinding is a second TOCTOU.
entries.fix_shape: Set follow_redirects=False and walk redirects through is_public_http_url inside the transport (or an httpx response hook), so every lane inherits it; pin with a 302->127.0.0.1 test server.

entries.title: A full S&P 500 screen misses SC-034: from a Yahoo-throttled IP a cold run returns 0 of 506 symbols evaluated (100% 'rate_limited' skips, target <5%) and meets the 'single-digit seconds' bar only by failing fast; the pre-budget measurement was 329.8 s cold / 2.84 s warm (target sub-second)
entries.repro: Live on the isolated sidecar :52152 (refuter, 23 Sep): cold full S&P 500 screen -> returns in 7.6 s with evaluated_count=0, skipped_count=506, every skip reason 'rate_limited' (honestly itemized); repeat -> 0.1 s, same empty result. nifty50 answers 49/50 from cache but valuation_as_of is ~70 days old. Earlier session measurement (REBUILD_R4_SESSION2_REPORT.md perf table): warm 2.84 s, cold 329.8 s (v7 batch 429-throttled -> per-symbol fallback).
entries.evidence: specs/001-agent-native-redesign/spec.md:1452 (SC-034: cold <= single-digit seconds / warm sub-second / <5% skips, all itemized); docs/redesign/REBUILD_R4_SESSION2_REPORT.md 'Screener perf numbers' table (row filed under flagged/BUILT, not VERIFIED); sidecar/services/screener.py:12,125 (DEFAULT_WALL_BUDGET_SECONDS = 120.0 now bounds a run, so the 329.8 s run cannot recur), sidecar/services/screener.py:833-889 (budgeted v7 batch sweep, Yahoo-only). refuter (INT-spec-180-214, admitted_with_correction, severity_final high): timing now 'met' only because the run fails fast; the skip-rate target flips from met to 100% failed. Related but distinct: R15-DATA-072 (Yahoo breaker cannot close on success, prolongs the empty window), R15-DATA-093 (custom-universe key mismatch).
entries.root_cause: The screener's only live source for a US universe is Yahoo (v7 batch + per-symbol fallback); an IP-level Yahoo 429 (reproduced even via system curl per the session report) leaves no second provider and no seeded/persisted valuation snapshot for sp500, so the run itemizes every symbol as rate_limited. Warm-path latency above sub-second is unexplained by the raw findings.
entries.fix_shape: Give the screener a non-Yahoo fallback for evaluation fields (a persisted last-good valuation snapshot per universe, served with its as_of and a stale badge, plus an optional BYOK provider lane) so a throttled cold run evaluates from the snapshot instead of skipping 100%; surface the snapshot age in the result header. Pin with a test where the Yahoo batch and per-symbol calls raise rate_limited and a seeded snapshot exists, asserting skipped_count/total < 5% and every evaluated row carries as_of; add a perf check asserting warm < 1 s on the seeded store.

entries.title: SEC filing viewer 404s a 10-K it just listed: get_filing resolves metadata from only the last 40 filings with no form_type filter, so a heavy Form-4/144 filer's annual reports fall outside the window
entries.repro: AAPL's 10-Ks (accessions ...-25-000079, ...-24-000123, listed via form_type=10-K in the filings list) 404 'filing metadata unavailable' when opened. get_filing calls get_recent_filings with limit=40 and no form_type filter, then matches the accession against that unfiltered window; a heavy Form-4/144 filer pushes every annual report out of the 40-filing window before the match ever happens.
entries.evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/stage-c/batch-4/VERDICTS.md issue 3 (verifier batch-4); sidecar/services/sec_filings_provider.py:585-591 (get_recent_filings called with limit=40, no form_type) and :591-592 (match = next(...) over that unfiltered window).
entries.root_cause: get_filing's metadata lookup re-lists only the issuer's last 40 filings across all form types (not the form_type-filtered list the panel showed), so any filing outside that raw recency window is unreachable regardless of what the user clicked.
entries.fix_shape: Pass the target form_type (or widen/paginate the recent-filings lookup) so a filing visible in a form-filtered list is always resolvable by accession; pin with a test using an issuer whose 10-K falls outside the unfiltered 40-most-recent window.
entries.note: verify-only: Batch-5 (1574ed8) verifier found this a REGRESSION (not_certified): the no-hint get_filing lookup widened to a 1,000-row unfiltered window that sec-edgar-mcp cannot serve (limit >=200 times out or 'cannot unpack non-iterable NoneType'; 40/60/100 succeed), so sec_filing_content now fails for every filing outside a 40-recent window (AAPL Form 4, MSFT 10-Q both broke). Fixed before the batch-5 merge closed: 7ae5117 forwards form_type from sec_tools.py and tries a small window first; 7ae5117 is an ancestor of the batch-5 merge commit 1574ed8, so the regression never shipped on 004. || rc1 refutation audit @6741387b: partial — root cause: sidecar/services/agent_tools/catalog.py:741-746 marks sec_filing_content.form_type optional and says it only speeds up the lookup. Without that hint, sidecar/services/sec_filings_provider.py:579 and :618-632 search only the latest 40, then 100, filings of any form; for MSFT, 100 rows reach back only to 2026-03-24. sec_filings_provider.py:650-662 get_filing_sections and sidecar/routers/sec_filings.py:124-131 do not accept or forward form_type at all.; acceptance: In sidecar/tests/test_sec_filings_provider.py, use a recorder whose unfiltered get_recent_filings windows (limit 40 and 100, both full) never contain 0000320193-21-000105, but whose form_type=10-K list does. Assert (await get_filing('0000320193-21-000105', cik_or_symbol='AAPL')).filing.form_type == '10-K' with no ProviderError not_found, and that get_filing_sections(acc, cik_or_symbol='AAPL', form_type='10-K') resolves. In sidecar/tests/test_sec_tools.py, assert (await _sec_filing_content({'accession': acc, 'identifier': 'AAPL'}))['ok'] is True on the same recorder. Add a router test that /sections forwards form_type, unless R15-CODE-DATA-013 deletes that route.

entries.title: ^NSEI (Nifty 50) and other caret-prefixed Yahoo index symbols get wrongly suffixed .NS by _yahoo_symbol's IN bare-ticker path, so index history returns 0 bars
entries.repro: GET /history/%5ENSEI in an IN session -> 0 bars, reason in_eod_only. _yahoo_symbol('^NSEI'): s='^NSEI' does not end .NS/.BO; region IN and no dot in s, so is_nse_symbol/is_bse_symbol both return False for the index and the function falls through to return f'{s}.NS' = '^NSEI.NS', which Yahoo does not serve -- the real Yahoo symbol is '^NSEI' unchanged. The same in_eod_only reason string also mislabels DAL's no-trade year as an EOD-only cause.
entries.evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/stage-c/batch-4/VERDICTS.md issue 6 (verifier batch-4); sidecar/services/yfinance_provider.py:97-131 (_yahoo_symbol's IN bare-ticker branch has no exemption for a caret-prefixed index symbol); sidecar/routers/history.py:21,28 (in_eod_only reason).
entries.root_cause: _yahoo_symbol treats any dot-free symbol in an IN session as a bare equity ticker and appends .NS, with no case for a Yahoo index symbol (^NSEI, ^BSESN, etc.), which Yahoo serves unsuffixed.
entries.fix_shape: Exempt a leading '^' from the IN bare-ticker suffix branch in _yahoo_symbol (return the symbol unchanged); pin with a test that _yahoo_symbol('^NSEI') under region IN returns '^NSEI', not '^NSEI.NS'.
entries.note: source: verifier batch-4

entries.title: _yahoo_symbol rewrites every non-Indian foreign exchange suffix with a dash (BHP.AX -> BHP-AX, 0700.HK -> 0700-HK, 7203.T -> 7203-T, VOD.L -> VOD-L), so Yahoo answers 'possibly delisted' and every non-US, non-IN listing is unquotable
entries.repro: Quote any non-US, non-IN foreign listing, e.g. BHP.AX, 0700.HK, 7203.T, VOD.L -> _yahoo_symbol dash-rewrites the suffix, Yahoo reports the resulting ticker as 'possibly delisted', and the new error classifier maps that to 404 'check the symbol' for every such listing.
entries.evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/stage-c/batch-8/VERDICTS.md 'Issues (outside the entries; not in any diff)' #4 (batch-8 verifier).
entries.root_cause: _yahoo_symbol's suffix rewrite was built for the Indian NSE/BSE dash convention (.NS/.BO stay untouched, a bare ticker gets one added) and was never scoped away from other exchange suffixes, which Yahoo expects unchanged (dot form).
entries.fix_shape: Scope the dash rewrite to the Indian suffix set only; pass every other recognised exchange suffix (.AX, .HK, .T, .L, ...) through unchanged. Pin with a test quoting one symbol per non-Indian suffix in the resolver's known exchange list.

entries.title: Every launch freezes the app's main event loop for the whole MCP bind window (about 25 s warm, 34 s+ cold, up to 90 s), and the data sidecar is not even spawned until both MCP binds return
entries.repro: Cold launch of the packaged app (after a reboot, no warm _MEI dirs). setup() spawns the openbb-mcp and sec-edgar-mcp supervisors, joins both inline (each waits up to 45 s x 2 attempts), and only then calls start_main_sidecar. The window is built but the main event loop is blocked for the whole join. Measured by the code's own comments: 34.2 s / 33.6 s cold, 13.6 s / 24.6 s warm. A child that overruns is killed and its env var removed, so a late bind is lost for the session (/sec -> 501).
entries.evidence: src-tauri/src/lib.rs:66-83, src-tauri/src/lib.rs:472-493 (spawn, join, then start_main_sidecar), src-tauri/src/openbb_mcp.rs:149-171 (supervisor consumes the full budget; timeout kills the child and removes the env var), tauri app.rs:1414-1417 + 2513-2526 (setup hook runs inside the RuntimeRunEvent::Ready callback on the main thread), src/lib/sidecar-client.ts:105-110 (frontend documents the effect), scripts/ensure-openbb-mcp-sidecar.mjs:172 + scripts/ensure-sec-edgar-mcp-sidecar.mjs:152 (--onefile still), docs/redesign/DECISIONS.md D76; refuters: COD-rust-core-1 admitted high, INT-deferred-0-1 admitted_with_correction high (mechanism corrected to a main-thread freeze, not a live-but-disconnected UI)
entries.root_cause: The joins that make MCP env vars settle before the sidecar reads them sit inside Tauri's setup() closure, which runs on the main thread inside the event loop's Ready callback. The join only needs to precede the sidecar SPAWN, not the event loop. The --onedir fix that would remove per-launch extraction was never taken.
entries.fix_shape: Move both MCP joins AND start_main_sidecar into one background thread (start_main_sidecar takes &AppHandle instead of &App) and return from setup() immediately; resolve MCP ports late in the sidecar (a port file or Tauri command instead of an env var read once at import in openbb_mcp_provider.py:131-141) so a late MCP bind attaches instead of being lost. Pin with a Rust test that setup() returns within a small bound with stub supervisors that sleep, and a sidecar test that a late-written MCP port is picked up. The --onedir conversion is the separate, Tier-1 (tauri.conf.json externalBin) follow-up for the operator.

entries.title: A layout-level restore failure discards ALL non-layout state (portfolio holdings, watchlist, notes, settings, research memory) and the next autosave overwrites the user's blob; the scheduled trading-panel removal triggers it deterministically for any user whose last autosave had a broker panel docked
entries.repro: Scratch vitest: register every first-party module except broker-connect (the post-removal build) and stub the autosave GET to return a historical blob whose layout holds broker-connect + broker-order-entry -> restoreLastSessionOrDefault returns false, api.fromJSON is called 0 times, the default layout is applied, deserializeWorkspace never runs, and the page/PanelHost autosave subscriptions then persist default stores over __autosave__. Same outcome from any renamed component id, a late-registering plugin panel, an api.fromJSON throw (it aborts before the other 15 store restores) or a failed GET.
entries.evidence: src/lib/workspace.ts:512-515 (unknown-component skip returns before deserializeWorkspace, applies default without api.clear()), src/lib/workspace.ts:262-270 (layout restored FIRST; a throw aborts every later slice), src/lib/workspace.ts:522-533, src/lib/workspace.ts:417-433 (loadWorkspace has no unknown-component guard at all), src/components/PanelHost.tsx:180-193, src/app/page.tsx:108-181, src/modules/broker-connect/index.ts:51; docs/redesign/verification/r15/census/code/evidence/workspace-layout-repro.test.ts.txt (repro #2); $ISO/seat-l4-upgrade/evidence/workspace-upgrade-vitest.txt (GATE lines). Refuters: COD-workspace-layout-4 admitted high; LIFE-L4-UPGRADE-1 admitted_with_correction high (the measured blob carried 0 holdings and empty notes, so the measured loss was one watchlist symbol + prefs; holdings loss is inferred for a blob that combines holdings with a docked broker panel, and the trigger is deterministic once the removal ships)
entries.root_cause: Restore order makes user data hostage to the most fragile step: dockview fromJSON (and the unknown-component gate) runs before, and gates, every non-layout slice, and autosave is not gated on a successful restore.
entries.fix_shape: In deserializeWorkspace restore the non-layout slices first (or in a finally), call it from the skip path too, and strip unknown panel ids from the serialized layout (restoring the rest) instead of abandoning the whole blob; move the unknown-component guard inside deserializeWorkspace so loadWorkspace gets it too; have workspace_store keep one .bak on overwrite. Ship it WITH the trading-removal change. Pin with a vitest feeding a blob containing an unregistered broker panel plus holdings/notes/watchlist and asserting every non-layout slice is restored and no default-state POST is issued.
entries.note: The broker-connect-panel trigger condition is moot post-removal (a122dbf6 feat(d81)), but any unregistered panel in an old layout reproduces the same failure. Core defect stays open: a layout-restore failure silently discards the surviving portfolio holdings, watchlist, notes, settings and research memory, then autosaves the loss, pending verification of the workspace.ts restore-order fix.

entries.title: Autosave is neither gated on restore nor serialized: every launch fires a burst of PARTIAL full-blob POSTs mid-restore, and the last one drops researchSymbol and the research-memory archive
entries.repro: pnpm exec vitest run on docs/redesign/verification/r15/census/code/evidence/workspace-layout-repro.test.ts.txt (copied into src/lib/*.test.ts; passed 2/2): with the page.tsx subscriptions installed, deserializeWorkspace(blob) issues more than one POST during the restore; POST[0] has 0 holdings; the LAST POST has no researchSymbol and researchSpaces.byName == {} although the blob carried both. Launch -> read -> quit with no further autosave trigger => research memory wiped on disk.
entries.evidence: src/app/page.tsx:108-181 (10 subscriptions live from mount, each `void autosaveLayout()`), src/app/page.tsx:171-172 (false 'autosaveLayout is debounced' comment), src/lib/workspace.ts:541-556 (no restore gate, no debounce, no single-flight), src/lib/workspace.ts:351-370 (researchSpaces.replaceAll / setResearchSymbol run after the last subscribed store), src/components/PanelHost.tsx:147,164-166 (stated intent: autosave only after restore), src/lib/sidecar-client.ts:125-127 (up-to-120 s pre-restore window), sidecar/services/workspace_store.py:72-79 (last-writer-wins); refuter admitted high (a later full autosave repairs the disk copy, so loss needs a session with no further trigger)
entries.root_cause: Temporal coupling held by a comment: the restore-then-autosave ordering lives in PanelHost's private timer while ten store subscriptions call autosaveLayout directly from mount, and buildWorkspacePayload runs synchronously inside each call.
entries.fix_shape: A module flag restoreSettled (set in restoreLastSessionOrDefault's finally) that makes autosaveLayout a no-op until then, plus trailing-edge debounce and single-flight INSIDE autosaveLayout; delete PanelHost's private timer and fix the page.tsx comment. entries.title: Exchange payload field drift is served as fabricated data: a renamed open/high/low/volume field yields open=high=low=close candles with zero volume under the exchange's own provider label, and the correctness gate passes them
entries.repro: In-process (harness/parser_drift.py): take one real NSE historicalOR window for RELIANCE (8-22 Sep, 10 rows), rename CH_OPENING_PRICE / CH_TRADE_HIGH_PRICE / CH_TRADE_LOW_PRICE / CH_TOT_TRADED_QTY, stub nse_provider._get_json to return it, call provider_registry.get_history('RELIANCE.NS','1d','1mo') -> served with provider nse_direct, 10/10 bars flat (open=high=low=close), 10/10 volume 0.0. Renaming the close field instead -> honest ProviderError and fall-through.
entries.evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/lifecycle/L2-rot/30-parser-drift.txt (A0-A4), sidecar/services/nse_provider.py:405-409 ('or close' / 'or 0.0'), sidecar/services/bse_provider.py:240-244 (same pattern), sidecar/services/correctness_gate.py:118-140 (checks only non-empty bars, last close > 0, symbol match); refuter admitted high (latent: needs an upstream rename that has not happened yet; when it does it is wrong money-relevant data shown as true)
entries.root_cause: The parsers substitute close for a missing open/high/low and 0.0 for a missing volume (only close is required), and validate_series has no shape check that would catch a whole series of flat zero-volume bars.
entries.fix_shape: Treat a missing O/H/L/V key as a parse failure (raise ProviderError so the registry falls through) or map it to None with optional OHLCVBar fields; additionally make validate_series reject a series where every bar is flat and zero-volume. Pin with a parametrized test per exchange parser that renames each of O/H/L/V in a captured payload and asserts ProviderError / fall-through, never flat bars.

entries.title: When the openbb-mcp child dies, /fundamentals 500s and the research SSE stream ends mid-run with no done/error frame, while /openbb-mcp/status still reports available with no lastError
entries.repro: Kill the openbb-mcp child on its configured port -> GET /openbb-mcp/status {available:true,lastError:null}; GET /fundamentals/MAZDOCK and /fundamentals/KPITTECH -> 500; a research prompt on /agents/copilot/invoke is cut at 63.8 s right after 'pulling market data for MAZDOCK' with no done/error frame (uvicorn 'ASGI callable returned without completing response'; traceback httpx.ConnectError -> CancelledError via cancel scope -> RuntimeError 'Attempted to exit cancel scope in a different task'). /quotes still 200 via nse_direct; restarting the child restores 200s.
entries.evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/research-briefs/35-openbb-mcp-down-stream-dies.txt, docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/research-briefs/34-staleack-run2-rerun.jsonl, sidecar/services/mcp_client.py:102-119 (except Exception around _open cannot catch the anyio CancelledError; exit_stack.aclose() in another task), sidecar/services/openbb_mcp_provider.py:147-157 ('available' = endpoint configured, never liveness), :239-248 (maps Exception, not BaseException, to ProviderError), sidecar/services/provider_registry.py:410 (fallback catches ProviderError only), src/modules/chat/streaming.ts:225-249 (clean EOF breaks without onError); refuter admitted_with_correction high (escape is a BaseException from the streamable-http open; UI end state NEEDS-GUI)
entries.root_cause: A failed streamable-http MCP open raises an anyio CancelledError / cancel-scope RuntimeError (BaseException) that bypasses every `except Exception`, so it neither becomes a ProviderError (no registry fall-through, lastError stays null) nor stays inside the request task; it tears down the whole agent stream.
entries.fix_shape: In mcp_client._open/_call_tool, run the open in its own task/cancel scope and convert a connect failure (including the anyio cancellation it produces) to ProviderError, set available=false + lastError; make 'available' a liveness result; have streaming.ts treat EOF without a done frame as an error. Pin with a test that points the MCP client at a closed port and asserts get_fundamentals falls through to the next provider and the agent SSE ends with an error or done frame.

entries.title: DEEP/ULTRA brief [n] citations point at unrelated documents: markers minted against one round's source numbering survive into a brief published under a re-ranked, longer list (price/P&E chips open 'Change in Directorate' PDFs)
entries.repro: vy.py invoke copilot 'Deep research on Blue Star (BLUESTARCO): ... Cite sources.' --provider openai --model gpt-4o-mini --autonomy auto, research_depth=deep -> brief cites 'Closing Price Rs 1,525.0 [6]', 'P/E 61.67 [7]'; rail [7] = nsearchives BLUESTARCO ... change in directors PDF, [6] = Q1FY27 shareholder communication; figures actually came from [11] vysted://price / [12] vysted://fundamentals. Same on ULTRA HAL (13-ultra-hal-4omini.jsonl); absent on the control run whose list never changed (12-deep-bdl-4omini.jsonl).
entries.evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/research-briefs/r4-deep-bluestar-4omini.jsonl, replay-r4-deep-bluestar-4omini.json, 13-ultra-hal-4omini.jsonl, 12-deep-bdl-4omini.jsonl, EVIDENCE.md 'Finding 1'; sidecar/services/research/deep.py:356-373 (all_sources ranks web/filings ahead of structured), sidecar/services/research/iter.py:127-129 (_numbered_sources renumbers every round), iter.py:223-260 (synthesis reuses working-report markers). Refuter: admitted, high (transcript proves the mismatch; line-level mechanism corroborated, not traced statement-by-statement).
entries.root_cause: Source numbering is recomputed from a re-ranked, growing list each round while the evolving report text keeps markers minted under the earlier numbering; citecheck only strips out-of-range markers, so in-range stale ones ship.
entries.fix_shape: Give every source a stable id at first sight (append-only numbering; rank only for display/priority, never renumber after a marker exists), or rewrite report markers by URL whenever the list is re-ranked. Pin with a multi-round iter test where round 2 inserts sources ahead of round 1's and the final brief's [n] still resolves to the round-1 URL.

entries.title: ULTRA cross-check mangles every figure that starts a claim line ('40.5%' -> '5%', '-0.4%' -> '4%', '67.13953' -> '13953') and its step reports 'verified 5 numeric claim(s), 0 disagreement(s)' over five UNVERIFIED rows
entries.repro: vy.py invoke copilot 'Research Kaynes Technology in depth: ...' --provider ollama --model llama3.1:8b --autonomy auto, research_depth=ultra -> body: revenue growth +40.5%, P/E 67.13953; '## Cross-check' renders 'UNVERIFIED - 5%', 'UNVERIFIED - 4%', 'UNVERIFIED - 13953'; trace: 'cross-check: verified 5 numeric claim(s), 0 disagreement(s)'. Same on gpt-4o-mini HAL ('P/E 34.42' -> '42', 'Gross Margin 51.70%' -> '70%').
entries.evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/research-briefs/r3-ultra-kaynes.jsonl + .stdout.txt, replay-r3-ultra-kaynes.json, 13-ultra-hal-4omini.jsonl; sidecar/services/research/verify.py:137-158 (_extract_claims routes claims through _split_subquestions), sidecar/services/research/deep.py:179-202 (strips leading '<digits>.'/'-' with no following-space requirement), verify.py:412-418 (label counts checks, not verified). Refuter: admitted, high (reproduced in-process).
entries.root_cause: Claim extraction reuses the sub-question splitter, whose ordered-list/bullet stripping eats the integer part of a leading decimal and a leading minus sign; the step label interpolates len(checks).
entries.fix_shape: Give claims their own splitter that strips '<digits>. ' only when followed by whitespace + non-digit and never strips a sign; make the step label state verified/unverified/disagree counts separately. Pin with a test over '40.5% revenue growth', '-0.4% earnings growth', '67.13953 P/E' asserting the extracted claim text is unchanged.

entries.title: On the local (zero-setup) lane DEEP/ULTRA synthesis hits the 60 s per-call cap and silently ships the structured floor, labelled 'web coverage for this name is thin' while 13+ web sources were captured, with raw floats and no degraded_reason
entries.repro: vy.py invoke copilot 'Do a deep research brief on CG Power ... order book, margins, valuation vs peers' --provider ollama --model llama3.1:8b --autonomy auto, research_depth=deep -> step 'synthesize | wrote brief from evolving report | 60014 ms'; published markdown = '_Web coverage for this name is thin; ..._' + filings list + 'change % -1.527472527472525' + 'market cap 1411777036288.0' while the brief carries 13 http web sources; panel header 'DEEP - 21 sources', no note, execution.degraded_reason null. Also 11-deep-bdl-llama (60007 ms) and r3-ultra-kaynes (all three angle syntheses 60001-60012 ms).
entries.evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/research-briefs/r2-deep-cgpower.jsonl + .stdout.txt, 11-deep-bdl-llama.jsonl, r3-ultra-kaynes.stdout.txt, replay-r2-deep-cgpower.json; sidecar/services/research/deep.py:165 (_LLM_CALL_TIMEOUT_SECS=60.0), deep.py:173 (_safe_llm -> '' on timeout), sidecar/services/research/iter.py:260-272 (empty synthesis + empty report -> floor), deep.py:459-505 (raw f'{label} {val}'), deep.py:523-556 (floor copy). Refuter: admitted, high.
entries.root_cause: A fixed 60 s per-LLM-call cap sized for hosted models degrades every local-lane distill/synthesis to empty; the floor fallback hardcodes a 'thin web coverage' explanation regardless of why it fired and records no degraded reason.
entries.fix_shape: Scale the per-call cap by provider class (local vs hosted) or stream synthesis against a progress deadline; when the floor fires because synthesis returned empty, set execution.degraded_reason='synthesis_timeout' and a brief.note naming it; only claim thin coverage when web sources are actually empty; format floor numbers through the percent/INR-crore formatters. Pin with a test where the LLM stub times out and web sources exist, asserting degraded_reason and the absence of the thin-coverage copy.
entries.note: Batch-3 (c81d879) not certified: The writers did not mark this fixed. CHANGELOG batch 3 calls it partial and open, because the execution record's degraded_reason is not yet copied by agent_tools/research.py. Live on llama3.1:8b ('Do a deep research brief on CG Power…', DEEP), synthesis finished in 27.8 s under the new 150 s local cap. The brief showed no thin-coverage copy, market cap as '₹141,004 cr', and degraded_reason null. The timeout path did not fire, so the degraded_reason half was not exercised. It stays open as the writers declared.

entries.title: ULTRA cross-check runs unmetered after its entry check: up to 1 extract + 5 sequential 60 s verdict calls inside a '90 s' BudgetGuard, which can push the whole ULTRA brief past the runtime dispatch guard and lose it as a timeout
entries.repro: ULTRA run whose 5 extracted claims each take a slow verdict turn: cross_check() calls budget.breach() once at entry, then extract + parallel searches/native calls + a SEQUENTIAL loop of up to 5 _verdict_for calls each capped only at 60 s by _safe_llm -> ~360 s inside BudgetGuard(max_wall_seconds=90); only bound is the agent-runtime research dispatch guard (570 s for ULTRA), whose breach discards the whole brief.
entries.evidence: sidecar/services/research/verify.py:37-41 (docstring claims 'SAME BudgetGuard' - false), verify.py:304, verify.py:319, verify.py:357-394, sidecar/services/research/deep.py:165, sidecar/services/agent_tools/deep_research.py:78, deep_research.py:231-236, deep_research.py:272 (fresh guard); sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py:579-615,652-667 (refuter context). Refuter: admitted, high.
entries.root_cause: The cross-check round builds its own BudgetGuard and checks it once; the per-claim loop has no breach re-check and no asyncio.timeout.
entries.fix_shape: Wrap the claim loop in asyncio.timeout(budget.max_wall_seconds) and re-check budget.breach() before each _verdict_for, degrading the remaining claims to UNVERIFIED with the existing out-of-budget reason; fix the docstring. Pin with a test whose verdict stub sleeps past the budget and asserts the round returns within budget with the tail marked UNVERIFIED.
entries.note: Verifier batch-3 residual: the claim extract and parallel re-check searches still run BEFORE the wall-bounded verdict loop, so a slow extract can carry the round past its wall (5s extract under a 0.5s wall took 5.01s); on the local lane the per-call cap is now 150s so the 90s cross-check reserve can still be overrun. Suggested fix: wrap the whole round in asyncio.timeout(remaining_wall).

entries.title: Any URL with '/investor' in its path or an 'ir.' host is ranked PRIMARY (exchange/regulator grade), so a Medium or WordPress post outranks Reuters, owns marker [1], and the synthesis prompt tells the model [1] is the primary record
entries.repro: sidecar/.venv/bin/python: domain_tier('https://medium.com/investor-diary/why-i-bought-xyz') -> 1 (TIER_PRIMARY); domain_tier('https://someblog.wordpress.com/ir/2024/hot-tip') -> 1; domain_tier('https://reuters.com/markets/x') -> 2; rank_sources([Reuters, Medium]) -> ['Blog','Reuters']; priority_note -> 'primary record (exchange/regulator/filings/IR): [1]'.
entries.evidence: sidecar/services/research/finance.py:72, finance.py:127-132, finance.py:140, finance.py:173; sidecar/services/research/deep.py:368, sidecar/services/research/iter.py:845. Refuter: admitted, high (reproduced; also '/markets/investors-rush' news paths).
entries.root_cause: _looks_like_ir is a substring/prefix heuristic ('/investor' anywhere in the path, any 'ir.' host) guarding the table that decides source authority.
entries.fix_shape: Require a corroborated IR signal (ir./investors. host prefix AND host not on a publishing-platform denylist - medium.com, *.wordpress.com, substack.com, seekingalpha.com, reddit.com) or give IR its own tier between PRIMARY and PRESS. Pin with a table test of the reproduced URLs asserting none reaches TIER_PRIMARY and Reuters outranks them.
entries.closure_evidence: a217a529 merge(r15): Stage C batch 13 — RESEARCH-007 PSL check, DOCS-017 live universe counts, AGENT-090 ratio guard (partial)
entries.note: Verifier batch-3 residual: certifying this fix demoted first-party IR pages (tcs.com/investor-relations, reliance.com/investors, infosys.com/investors) from PRIMARY to GENERAL, below press, since a path marker alone is no longer PRIMARY. Expected side effect of the shipped fix shape; giving IR its own tier would avoid it. || rc1 refutation audit @6741387b: partial — root cause: sidecar/services/research/finance.py:146. _looks_like_ir matches host.startswith('investors.'/'investor.'/'ir.') without requiring that label to be a subdomain. After the www. strip, the news site investors.com (IBD) therefore ranks PRIMARY. finance.py:79-89: _IR_PLATFORM_DENYLIST lacks github.io, wixsite.com, netlify.app and hubpages.com, and matches blogspot only on .com. So ir.blogspot.in, investors.github.io, investors.wixsite.com and ir.netlify.app rank PRIMARY.; acceptance: Add sidecar/tests/test_research_finance.py::test_ir_host_prefix_never_promotes_news_or_platform_hosts. Assert domain_tier(u) != TIER_PRIMARY for https://www.investors.com/news/technology/nvidia-stock-buy-now/, https://investors.github.io/pump, https://ir.blogspot.in/post, https://investors.wixsite.com/x, https://ir.netlify.app/x and https://investors.hubpages.com/x. Assert rank_sources([IBD, GH, Reuters])[0].title == 'Reuters', and that priority_note does not name IBD or GH as a primary record. The controls ir.nvidia.com, investors.infosys.com, investor.apple.com and ir.tatamotors.com must stay TIER_PRIMARY. || batch-12 verifier @3d588a29: Acceptance cases pass, but the class fix fails fresh cases. The fix enumerates nine platforms in a denylist, so other free-hosting platforms still rank TIER_PRIMARY: ir.firebaseapp.com, investors.web.app, ir.azurewebsites.net, ir.onrender.com, ir.fly.dev, ir.glitch.me, investors.notion.site, ir.webflow.io, ir.herokuapp.com. The three-label 'IR label is a subdomain' check also misses ccSLD registrable domains: https://www.investors.co.uk/news/x, https://ir.co.in/x and https://investors.com.au/x rank 1, which is the original investors.com mechanism on a two-part TLD. Root fix: decide 'IR label sits on a registrable domain' from the Public Suffix List, including its private section (github.io, web.app, herokuapp.com, blogspot.* etc. are PSL private suffixes). No PSL package is in the venv today. || batch-14: certified by batch-13 verifier @e02073bd — the PSL-backed domain_tier check holds on all fresh cases (rank_sources/priority_note correct, controls unaffected, PSL bundled in the built binary); status -> fixed.

entries.title: On the keyless search tier (no Docker/SearXNG, the default for most users) chat web_search times out at its 25 s tool cap because DuckDuckGo, first in the fixed chain, burns ~41 s of nested retries before a healthy Brave (0.9 s) is tried; the model then blames the network and suggests 'a lighter depth'
entries.repro: Sidecar booted without Docker (/search/status t1_keyless, all engines 'available'); vy.py invoke copilot 'Use your web_search tool to find recent news about Dixon Technologies and cite the sources' --provider ollama --model llama3.1:8b -> tool timeout; model: 'there was a timeout error ... try again ... at a lighter depth' (2/2 runs). Direct handler timing: ddg FAIL 20.5 s, ddg FAIL 20.4 s, brave ok 0.9 s -> 42.5 s total.
entries.evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/failure-inducer/44-keyless-engine-timing.txt, 42-websearch-direct.txt, 41-deadsearxng-nodocker-websearch.txt, 43-nodocker-websearch-2nd.txt, 40-nodocker-status.txt; sidecar/services/agent_tools/catalog.py:313 (25 s), catalog.py:1572 (research-domain timeout hint), sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py:652-666 (wait_for), sidecar/services/search/keyless.py:53 (fixed ddg->brave->mojeek), keyless.py:150-190, keyless.py:201-232, sidecar/services/search/pacing.py:42 (2 attempts/engine), sidecar/services/search/ddg.py:60 (2 inner attempts), ddg.py:84 (12 s timeout). Refuters: SURF admitted high; COD-6 admitted_with_correction medium (outer 25 s bound exists, but DDG's nested budget exceeds it so failover never happens) - the live repro makes that corrected mechanism a core-flow failure, high kept.
entries.root_cause: Three independently reasonable retry layers (keyless 2 attempts x ddg 2 attempts x 12 s timeouts) with no per-engine deadline exceed the 25 s outer tool cap, so wait_for cancels before rotation reaches the next engine; the timeout hint is the research tool's copy.
entries.fix_shape: Give keyless.search a per-engine deadline that fits inside the tool cap (e.g. 6 s, no second attempt after a transport timeout), drop ddg.py's private retry loop now that keyless owns retry, and give web_search its own timeout hint naming the search tier. Pin with a test where the ddg stub hangs and brave answers, asserting web_search returns brave rows inside the catalog timeout.

entries.title: DEEP/ULTRA research never meters tokens or spend: the BudgetGuard has no token/spend ceiling, every loop site records usage=None, and the brief header shows no cost although dozens of paid LLM calls were billed
entries.repro: Run any DEEP brief on an OpenRouter paid model: deep_research._run_native builds BudgetGuard(max_steps=..., max_wall_seconds=...) only; oneshot.complete returns bare str; every loop site calls budget.record(None, model, provider) -> brief.cost carries zero tokens/spend and BriefPanel omits the segments.
entries.evidence: sidecar/services/agent_tools/deep_research.py:232-236, deep_research.py:322-325; sidecar/services/research/iter.py:585, iter.py:962, iter.py:1023, iter.py:1146; sidecar/services/research/deep.py:19-25, deep.py:1214; sidecar/services/research/verify.py:319; sidecar/services/budget_guard.py:95-107, budget_guard.py:116; src/modules/research/BriefPanel.tsx:113-146; spec FR-072/074/075. Refuter: admitted, high. Cross-cluster: same defect as R15-AGENT-012 (COD-research-extraction-synthesis-2, agent cluster) - the lead should fold the two at build time.
entries.root_cause: oneshot.complete drops the adapter's LLMUsage and returns text only, so research loops have nothing to record; the guard is built without the agent-invoke budget's token/spend ceilings.
entries.fix_shape: Make oneshot.complete return (text, usage), pass usage into budget.record at every research site, construct the research guard with the invoking run's token/spend ceilings so the existing breach path forces synthesis. Pin with a test that a stubbed-usage DEEP run reports non-zero brief.cost and breaches on a tiny max_spend_usd.

entries.title: Settings certifies any string as a working OpenRouter key ('research bills to it'), and when hosted Tier B research then 401s the trace shows only ok steps and 'done' - the failure reaches only the model, which answers with unfetched 'sources'
entries.repro: Settings -> AI Providers -> OpenRouter -> paste 'sk-or-v1-R15CANARY-this-is-not-a-real-key' -> POST /llm/keys/validate {ok:true}; Tier B card: 'OpenRouter key configured - research bills to it.' Then Tier B research with that key (vy.py invoke copilot ... --provider ollama --model llama3.1:8b --tier tier_b): stream = 2 research_step frames both 'ok', then 'done'; no error step/frame; llama3.1:8b answered with 'Brief sources: Wikipedia, Forbes, Bloomberg' (none fetched).
entries.evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/settings-plugins/10-settings-panel-replay.json (S2), G01-tierb-fake-openrouter-key.jsonl + .stdout.txt, http-log.jsonl B01/B12; sidecar/services/llm/openai.py:842-849 (validate = models.list()), sidecar/services/llm/openrouter_catalog.py:15 (/api/v1/models is unauthenticated), sidecar/services/agent_tools/deep_research.py:682, deep_research.py:723-724 (HTTP error returns ok:false without a _step), src/components/SettingsPanel.tsx:1103-1105. Refuter: admitted_with_correction, high (model did disclose it could not fetch; no brief was published; fabrication is the chat-text source list). Validation half's code root cause is R15-CODE-AGENT-003 (COD-llm-adapters-2-4, code-agent cluster).
entries.root_cause: OpenRouter key validation calls a public endpoint, so it cannot fail on a bad key; run_research_model_brief returns ok:false on HTTPStatusError without emitting an error step, so the trace and panel never show the failure.
entries.fix_shape: Validate OpenRouter against an authenticated endpoint (GET /api/v1/auth/key with the key; 401 -> invalid); in run_research_model_brief emit _step('error', <humanised 401 message>) before returning ok:false. Pin with a test that a 401 from the hosted research call produces an error research_step on the stream.

entries.title: A BSE-XBRL institutional-holding figure is shown in the brief labelled 'NSE shareholding filing, <NSE quarter>' - the service's honest split_source/split_as_of stamp is discarded one layer up
entries.repro: Dual-listed Indian name whose latest NSE quarterly master row has no matching BSE XBRL quarter (nearest-quarter branch, corporate_disclosures.py:530): _merge_bse_split stamps split_source='BSE', split_as_of=<BSE quarter>; ownership_check._fetch_latest copies institutions_percent but sets as_of_quarter=latest.quarter_end and source=latest.source (NSE) -> semantics renders basis 'NSE shareholding filing, <NSE quarter>' on institutions_percent_exchange.
entries.evidence: sidecar/services/corporate_disclosures.py:507, corporate_disclosures.py:538, sidecar/services/ownership_check.py:126-132, sidecar/services/research/semantics.py:555, semantics.py:559, semantics.py:578, sidecar/models/announcements.py:133. Refuter: admitted_with_correction critical -> high (live RELIANCE/SIL/TCS have split_as_of == quarter_end, so the wrong-QUARTER label fires only in the nearest-quarter branch; the 'NSE' source label on a BSE figure is always-on; both exchanges carry the same SEBI SHP filing).
entries.root_cause: split_source/split_as_of have no production reader; _fetch_latest re-derives provenance from the NSE master row.

entries.title: Notes editor and notes store drift apart and the editor overwrites the store: an agent write_note into the open note is invisible and clobbered by the next keystroke, clearing a note never persists, and edits within 600 ms of a scope switch or tab close are lost
entries.repro: (1) Notes open on General; agent write_note appends to General (host-actions.ts:1176-1191) -> editor still shows the old body (scope effect early-returns when prevScopeRef===scope) -> type one char -> 600 ms later the stale body + char replaces the agent's text in store and .md, while chat said 'Appended'. (2) Select-all + Delete -> editorMarkdown '' and debouncedMd '' -> guard at NotesPanel.tsx:169 returns -> old note resurrects on scope switch/relaunch. (3) Type in AAPL, switch to MSFT within 600 ms -> Tiptap setContent emits an update (emitUpdate defaults true) -> AAPL's last burst never written. (4) Close the Notes tab within 600 ms of typing -> debounce cleared, no flush.
entries.evidence: src/modules/notes/NotesPanel.tsx:45-52, :139-148, :150-178, :169; src/lib/host-actions.ts:1176-1191; src/store/notes.ts:58-65, :91-96; node_modules/@tiptap/core/src/commands/setContent.ts:51. Refuter: -1 admitted_with_correction high (workspace-load half refuted: fromJSON remounts the panel), -2 admitted high.
entries.root_cause: Two owners of the note body (Tiptap doc and useNotesStore) reconciled only on a scope-change edge; the debounced save is keyed to the scope current when the timer fires, an empty-guard meant for mount also swallows a real empty save, programmatic setContent emits user-update events, and unmount does not flush.
entries.fix_shape: Make the store authoritative: subscribe the editor to noteFor(scope) and setContent(value, {emitUpdate:false}) when it differs from lastWrittenRef; capture {scope, md} at update time and flush synchronously on scope change/unmount; replace the empty-guard with a 'user has edited' flag. Pin with vitest+jsdom: store write while editor open is shown and survives a keystroke; clear-all persists ''; type-then-switch within 600 ms persists the first scope's text.

entries.title: Cmd-K ticker pick does nothing to the chart: the palette writes the opt-in chart-sync bus (off by default, no possible peer for the singleton chart) instead of the always-consumed chart-command channel
entries.repro: Default settings: Cmd-K -> type RELIANCE -> pick the Tickers row (or a recent) -> palette closes, chart unchanged. CommandPalette.tsx:200/:384 call useChartSyncBus.setSymbol('palette', sym); ChartPanel consumes it only when syncSubscriptions.symbol is true and DEFAULT_SUBS.symbol=false (chart-sync.ts:66).
entries.evidence: src/components/CommandPalette.tsx:162, :198-201, :384; src/store/chart-sync.ts:66; src/modules/chart/ChartPanel.tsx:314-325, :761-799 (comment at :775-777 claims the command channel serves palette picks); src/modules/chart/index.ts:30; src/lib/host-actions.ts:259-265. Refuter: admitted high.
entries.root_cause: The chart symbol lives in four places (local state, chart-command.activeSymbol, chart-sync.symbol, panel-context) and each caller picked a different inbox; the sync bus lost its only purpose when the chart became a singleton.
entries.fix_shape: Route both palette ticker paths through loadSymbolIntoChart (host-actions.ts:259) and delete the chart-sync symbol bus + Sync popover (or scope it to real multi-chart). Pin with a vitest that a palette ticker pick changes the chart's active symbol under default settings.

entries.title: Agent Builder hard-codes stale copies of sidecar vocabularies: only 20 of 50 selectable tools can be granted (no research, web_search, publish_brief, news, terminal/portfolio reads), editing an agent silently strips every other tool, and an unknown provider such as openrouter is silently rewritten to anthropic on save

(2) POST /custom-agents tools:[research, web_search, price_data] (accepted) -> Edit in builder -> change Name -> Save -> PUT sends tools:[price_data]. (3) Edit an agent with default_provider 'openrouter' -> formStateFromAgent falls back to 'anthropic' -> Save writes anthropic; openrouter (the provider onboarding recommends) cannot be selected at all.
entries.evidence: src/modules/agent-builder/form.tsx:16-54, :139-141; src/modules/agent-builder/AgentBuilderPanel.tsx:51-67, :141-170, :319-337; sidecar/services/agent_tools/catalog.py:1520-1528; sidecar/models/custom_agent.py:28-43, :56-63; types/ai.ts:43-51. The form.tsx:16-17 claim 'verified by test_capability_catalog.py' is false. Refuter: -1 admitted high, -2 admitted high, -3 admitted_with_correction medium.

entries.fix_shape: Serve the selectable tool ids and provider ids from the sidecar (GET /agents/tool-ids or extend GET /llm/providers) and render from the response; keep the agent's full tool set and provider in form state (unknown ids as read-only chips), delete the form.tsx:139-141 filter, keep static arrays only as a pre-sidecar fallback. Pin with a vitest that edit+save round-trips an agent holding research/web_search/openrouter unchanged, plus a parity test against the catalog's derived list.

entries.title: Portfolio live-quote failure is indistinguishable from 'symbol not found': fetchPositionQuote swallows every error to null, so the failure banner and its Retry (the panel's only recovery) can never render
entries.repro: Stop the sidecar or break /quotes with holdings present -> every Price/Mkt val/P&L cell shows '—' and the footer says 'N without a live quote'; the warning banner never appears and Retry is unreachable, so the panel stays dashed until the holding set changes or it remounts.
entries.evidence: src/modules/portfolio/api.ts:23-32 (try/catch -> null), :35-45 (Promise.all over non-rejecting promises); src/modules/portfolio/PortfolioPanel.tsx:109-113, :153-159 (dead .catch), :794-808 (dead banner + Retry); PortfolioPanel.test.tsx:62,94,113,132 (only mockResolvedValue). Refuter: admitted high.
entries.root_cause: An exception masked at the per-symbol level erases the failure signal the panel-level handler needs; no test exercises a rejected fetch.

entries.title: A provider that accepts the request and never streams (or a hung planner pre-pass) leaves the chat on a silent spinner for up to 600 s: no client timeout, no heartbeat and no stall watchdog
entries.repro: Sidecar :52224 with OPENAI_BASE_URL -> junk stub. vy.py invoke copilot 'What is the price of RELIANCE?' --provider openai --bad-key --model junk-hang (stub sends 200 + SSE headers, then nothing) --timeout 150 -> zero SSE events of any kind in 150 s; client gave up (TRANSPORT TimeoutError). || [COD-agent-runtime-3] mode='agent' + a capable provider + a compound prompt (classify_intent(prompt).compound) -> invoke_agent awaits oneshot.complete(...) BEFORE the first token of the turn streams, with no timeout= argument. oneshot.py:60-73 states adapters carry no per-stream timeout (OpenAI SDK default ~600 s) and that timeout= exists for exactly this case. A hung provider socket is not an exception, so the 'except Exception -> best-effort' guard at agent_runtime.py:1412 does not fire: the composer sits dead with no frames.
entries.evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/failure-inducer/52-junk-hang.txt, sidecar/services/llm/openai.py:440-445, sidecar/.venv openai 2.36.0 DEFAULT_TIMEOUT = Timeout(connect=5.0, read=600, write=600, pool=600), src/modules/chat/streaming.ts (no timer/stall logic: grep timeout|stall|watchdog|setTimeout -> 0 hits), sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py:1396, sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py:1401, sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py:1412, sidecar/services/llm/oneshot.py:60, sidecar/services/agent_tools/deep_research.py:323, sidecar/services/company_narrative.py:468 || refuter corrections: COD-agent-runtime-3: The planner pre-pass does call oneshot.complete with no timeout before the first streamed frame, and deep_research/company_narrative pass one. Corrected on two points: it is not 'the only' user-facing caller without a timeout (the OpenAI adapter's tool-arg repair at openai.py:626 also omits it), and a hung socket is not unique to the planner - the main streaming round has no per-stream timeout either (the OpenAI client is built with only max_retries=0), so the marginal harm is an unbounded extra pre-stream latency on compound prompts, not a distinct dead-composer failure mode.
entries.root_cause: AsyncOpenAI is built with max_retries=0 but no timeout so the SDK's 600 s read timeout governs; the planner pre-pass awaits oneshot.complete with no timeout before the first frame; the runtime emits no heartbeat and streaming.ts has no idle timer.
entries.fix_shape: Set an explicit first-byte/idle timeout on adapter clients and timeout=15 on the planner call, emit a heartbeat frame while waiting, and add a frontend stall watchdog that surfaces 'the provider went quiet' with Retry. Test: the junk-hang stub yields an error frame within the idle budget.
entries.note: Batch-5 (1574ed8) certified: against a silent stub the run emits 17 heartbeats then an error frame at 200s (20s planner timeout + 180s adapter idle); base emitted zero events in 150s. Copy nit noted by the verifier: the idle-timeout error still reads 'Could not reach OpenAI -- check your network', which is wrong for a connection that opened and then went silent ('stopped responding' would be accurate); follow-up copy fix, not re-opened as a new defect.

entries.title: A truncated or empty answer is shown as a complete one: max_tokens/length finishes (Anthropic hard-capped at 4096), streams that end with no finish_reason, and rounds with zero text and zero tool calls all settle as success with no notice or Retry
entries.repro: design + code trace: an Anthropic turn whose answer exceeds DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS=4096 (nothing on the agent/chat path raises it) ends with stop_reason 'max_tokens'; the adapter yields LLMDoneEvent(finish_reason='max_tokens'). OpenAI/Groq/Gemini/Ollama likewise carry 'length'. normalizeEvent maps it to event.finishReason, but makeHandlers' done branch passes only usage to onDone, and agent_runtime special-cases only 'content_filter'. The bubble finalises normally, mid-sentence or mid-table, with no notice. || [SURF-FAILURE-INDUCER-1] Sidecar :52224 booted with OPENAI_BASE_URL -> loopback junk stub (harness/junk_provider.py). vy.py invoke copilot 'What is the price of RELIANCE?' --provider openai --bad-key --model junk-truncated -> one delta 'RELIANCE closed at Rs 1,4', socket closed, then {kind:done, finish_reason:null}, no error. --model junk-html (HTTP 200 text/html captive-portal page) -> only {kind:done}, zero text. --model junk-emptychoices (choices:[] then [DONE]) -> only {kind:done}. Same junk through the Ollama adapter (OLLAMA_HOST) -> honest parse_error frames.
entries.evidence: sidecar/services/llm/anthropic.py:36-37 (DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS = 4_096), sidecar/services/llm/anthropic.py:110 and :142-146 (stop_reason forwarded as finish_reason), sidecar/services/llm/openai.py:785-787, sidecar/services/llm/groq.py:166-168,184, sidecar/services/llm/ollama.py:216-218, sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py:1485-1495 (only content_filter becomes an error frame), src/modules/chat/streaming.ts:338-342 (finishReason parsed), src/modules/chat/ChatSidebar.tsx:2025-2030 (done -> onDone(usage) only; finishReason discarded), docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/failure-inducer/50-junk-truncated.txt, docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/failure-inducer/50-junk-html.txt, docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/failure-inducer/50-junk-emptychoices.txt, docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/failure-inducer/51-ollama-junk-ndjson-truncated.txt, sidecar/services/llm/openai.py:751, sidecar/services/llm/openai.py:830, sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py:1485, sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py:1499, src/modules/chat/ChatSidebar.tsx:914-919, src/store/chat-history.ts:213-219, src/modules/chat/ChatSidebar.tsx:1239-1250 || refuter corrections: SURF-FAILURE-INDUCER-1: Real but narrower than titled: driving the adapter directly shows the REALISTIC mid-stream failures are surfaced honestly - a chunked-transfer cut raises and is humanized to 'Could not reach <provider>', and an OpenRouter-style error chunk (error field + finish_reason 'error') becomes '<provider> returned a server error' (53-adapter-direct-stream-ends.txt). What stays silent is (a) a clean close-delimited EOF with no finish_reason (the 'Rs 1,4' case), (b) a 200 non-SSE body, and (c) any round with zero text and zero tool calls - (c) is the one users actually hit (empty free-model completions; qwen3 think-only rounds in LOCAL_LANE_PROOF.md), and it is runtime/frontend-wide, not OpenAI-adapter-only: agent_runtime handles only content_filter and chat-history finalizes any done as success. Severity lowered to medium because the truncated-number path needs an unusual transport; the blank-turn path is common but not money-wrong.
entries.root_cause: Adapters forward finish_reason and streaming.ts parses it, but makeHandlers passes only usage to onDone and agent_runtime special-cases only content_filter; a done frame is always finalized as success.
entries.fix_shape: In agent_runtime next to the content_filter branch: finish 'length'/'max_tokens' -> truncation notice; finish None or zero output -> error frame (code truncated/empty_response) so the Retry row renders; raise Anthropic's chat-path max_tokens. Test: each of the three junk-stub shapes and a max_tokens finish produce a notice or error frame.

Try again or switch provider'; humanize('groq', exc(status_code=413)) -> unknown; humanize('ollama', ConnectError('All connection attempts failed')) -> 'Could not reach Ollama — check your network.' / 'Check your internet connection and try again.' || [COD-error-layer-2-4] Live: POST generativelanguage.googleapis.com …:generateContent with a bogus key -> HTTP 400 {status:'INVALID_ARGUMENT', reason:'API_KEY_INVALID', message:'API key not valid…'}; POST api.x.ai/v1/chat/completions with a bogus key -> HTTP 400 {error:'Incorrect API key provided…'}. humanize('gemini', genai ClientError(400, that body)) -> code=unknown 'Something went wrong with Google Gemini.'; humanize('xai', openai.BadRequestError(400, that body)) -> code=unknown 'Something went wrong with xAI.'. || [SURF-FAILURE-INDUCER-5] vy.py invoke copilot 'What is the price of RELIANCE?' --provider openrouter --model 'zzz-nonsense/not-a-model-9000:free' --port 52224 -> {kind:error, message:'Something went wrong with OpenRouter.', action:'Try again or switch provider in Settings.', code:'unknown', detail:"Error code: 400 - {'error': {'message': 'zzz-nonsense/not-a-model-9000:free is not a valid model ID', ...}}"}. The chat call raises ollama.ResponseError(404, 'model "qwen2.5:7b" not found, try pulling it first'); humanize maps every 404 to model_not_found. Probe: humanize('ollama', ollama.ResponseError('model "qwen3:8b" not found, try pulling it first', 404)) -> message='The requested model is not available on Ollama — pick another model.', action='Choose a different model in Settings.'.

No frontend code routes on code=model_not_found. Scope correction: 'the onboarding pull flow is never offered' is overstated. The first-run overlay auto-opens while `seen === false` and offers 'Download & use <model>' when the daemon is running and the model is missing. The dead end hits users who skipped or finished setup without pulling, or who later chose an unpulled Ollama model in the picker. Medium kept: that is still normal local-first use.
