entries.title: If the sidecar is not ready when the user sends, the chat wedges: the send promise rejects outside onError, the assistant bubble stays 'streaming' forever, Stop does nothing and later prompts queue behind it
entries.repro: State: the shared readiness probe is not resolved when the user sends, i.e. boot landed in sidecarStatus='error' (120 s budget lapsed) or Rust reported port 0. Pick a keyed provider (Anthropic/OpenAI; the keyless path pre-checks via validateProvider) and send a prompt. streamAgentInvocation/streamChat await getSidecarBaseUrl() OUTSIDE consumeSseStream's try, so after the re-armed 120 s probe the SidecarError rejects the call without ever calling handlers.onError. Proof (vitest, getSidecarBaseUrl mocked to reject): 'P1 agent: onError calls = 0 | rejected with: The data engine did not become ready in time.' and the same rejection for streamChat. In ChatSidebar the call is `await streamAgentInvocation(...)` inside handleSend with no try, invoked as `void handleSend(text)`, so the rejection is unhandled after beginAssistant already set pending:true + streamingMessageId.
entries.evidence: src/modules/chat/streaming.ts:134, src/modules/chat/streaming.ts:153 (await getSidecarBaseUrl() before consumeSseStream), src/modules/chat/streaming.ts:204-215 (the only try, which covers fetch only), src/lib/sidecar-client.ts:114-144 (re-arms a fresh 120 s probe after a failure, then throws SidecarError 503), src/modules/chat/ChatSidebar.tsx:868-886 (beginAssistant + abortRef + startRun before the call), src/modules/chat/ChatSidebar.tsx:1005-1038 (await with no try/catch), src/modules/chat/ChatSidebar.tsx:1285-1297 (onSend queues while streamingMessageId !== null; onStop only aborts the controller), src/store/chat-history.ts:141-157 (beginAssistantMessage sets pending + streamingMessageId), docs/redesign/verification/r15/census/code/evidence/error-layer-2-proof.test.ts.txt, docs/redesign/verification/r15/census/code/evidence/error-layer-2-proof-output.txt
entries.root_cause: streamChat/streamAgentInvocation await getSidecarBaseUrl() before consumeSseStream's try, so a SidecarError never reaches handlers.onError; handleSend has no try and runs as void.
entries.fix_shape: Move the base-URL await inside consumeSseStream's try (pass the path), and wrap handleSend's stream call so any rejection calls fail/finalize/endRun. Test (vitest): getSidecarBaseUrl rejecting results in onError being called once and streamingMessageId cleared.

entries.title: Router last-resort SSE guards blame the AI provider or the user's network for internal sidecar crashes (substring heuristics on str(exc), provider id never passed)
entries.repro: sidecar/.venv python: humanize(None, RuntimeError('runs_store: database connection is closed')) -> code=network 'Could not reach the AI provider — check your network.'; humanize(None, ValueError("could not parse depth 'ultra2'")) -> code=parse_error 'the AI provider returned an unreadable response.'; humanize(None, TypeError("...unexpected keyword argument 'research_depth'")) -> 'Something went wrong with the AI provider. Try again or switch provider in Settings.'; humanize(None, KeyError('connect_args')) -> code=network (substring 'connect' in the MESSAGE, not the class).
entries.evidence: sidecar/services/errors.py:207-218 ('connect'/'connection'/'timeout' matched anywhere in the message), sidecar/services/errors.py:241-245, sidecar/services/errors.py:295-300, sidecar/routers/llm.py:141-145 and sidecar/routers/agents.py:105-110 (error_frame(exc) with payload.provider in scope but not passed), sidecar/services/errors.py:59-63 (label falls to lowercase 'the AI provider', producing a sentence that starts lowercase at :247)
entries.root_cause: Adapters already humanize their own failures, so what reaches the router guard is a runtime/tool/store fault; humanize() there matches 'connect'/'timeout' anywhere in the message and labels it the provider's fault.
entries.fix_shape: Router guard emits code='internal' ('the terminal hit an internal error', detail = type + message); keyword matching on class names only. Test: RuntimeError('database connection is closed') at the router yields code internal.
entries.note: Verifier batch-8: same class, fresh case -- a pydantic validation error from a bad options.tools on the Ollama adapter is humanized as "Something went wrong with Ollama", blaming the provider for an internal/our-own construction error.

entries.title: Publish-divergence notices are matched by a prose regex that drifted from the sidecar copy: 2 of 3 notices ('kept the brief already on screen', 'reported the publish failed') are demoted to a telemetry row
entries.repro: node -e 're=/did not confirm the publish|kept the previous, richer brief/i; re.test("The panel kept the brief already on screen (AAPL) — this publish did not replace it; do not claim the new one rendered.")' -> false; same for "The brief panel reported the publish failed (AAPL)." -> false; only the no-ack line -> true. So under AUTO autonomy a kept_previous / failed publish rides to appendResearchStep (telemetry row) instead of the transcript notice chip.
entries.evidence: src/modules/chat/message-notices.ts:57 (DIVERGENCE_RE), sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py:1023-1036 (the three current copies; kept_previous reworded in R13 JARVIS 1c, :958), src/modules/chat/ChatSidebar.tsx:985-989 (branch), src/modules/chat/message-notices.test.ts:29 (pins the OLD 'kept the previous, richer brief'), sidecar/tests/test_agent_runtime.py:1390,1464 (pins the NEW 'kept the brief already on screen')
entries.root_cause: A cross-process contract is held by matching English copy; each side's test pins its own copy, so both suites stay green while the contract is broken.
entries.fix_shape: Carry a typed discriminator on the step (step_kind='notice') and branch on it; until then fix the regex and add one shared fixture of the three lines asserted by both suites.

entries.title: The chat transcript writes 'Applied: <change>' synchronously, before the async apply can fail and re-pend the change, so the transcript contradicts the review row
entries.repro: Autonomy=AUTO, agent emits a host-action tool_use whose args are incomplete: ChatSidebar.tsx:963-970 appends 'Applied: <title>' immediately after enqueue(); store/proposed-changes.ts:118-120 fires accept() asynchronously, :150-153 gets null from applyHostActionAsync, :163-167 re-pends the change with a detail. Result on screen: the transcript says 'Applied: Chart NVDA' while ProposedChangesReview.tsx:121-125 below says "Couldn't apply: … — try again." The transcript line is never corrected.
entries.evidence: src/modules/chat/ChatSidebar.tsx:940-971, src/modules/chat/ChatSidebar.tsx:572-592, src/store/proposed-changes.ts:113-122, src/store/proposed-changes.ts:148-168, src/modules/chat/ProposedChangesReview.tsx:121-125 || refuter corrections: COD-frontend-panels-agent-shell-5: Mechanism confirmed: onToolUse writes 'Applied: <title>' into the persisted chat-history step list right after enqueue(), while enqueue fires accept() without awaiting it, and accept() re-pends the change with a detail when applyHostActionAsync returns null, so the transcript can say Applied while the review row says Couldn't apply. Corrected on two points: the runtime's divergence check is fed by ackHostAction with the real applied/failed status (proposed-changes.ts:154-163), not by the transcript line, so the agent is not misled; and the failure is shown in ProposedChangesReview directly under the message. That leaves a misleading transcript line, not a silent core-flow break, so medium, not high. The enqueueSlashChange 'omits order' point is moot (no slash action is an order, and orders are being removed).
entries.root_cause: The presentation layer re-derives the auto-apply predicate at two call sites instead of reading the store's outcome; enqueue fires accept() without awaiting.
entries.fix_shape: Make enqueue/accept resolve to applied|staged|failed and write the step line from that value at both call sites. Test: a failing applyHostActionAsync under AUTO leaves no 'Applied:' line.
entries.note: Batch-7 (e81c9e7) certified: Under AUTO, a failing auto-apply writes "Couldn't apply: ..." and no "Applied:" line, and the change stays pending.

entries.title: Under ASK autonomy the model says 'I've set BDL on your chart' for a change the runtime returned as awaiting_user_review, and nothing corrects the claim
entries.repro: autonomy ask, 'Pull up Bharat Dynamics on the chart and add the RSI indicator' -> set_chart_symbol{BDL} result status awaiting_user_review ('do not claim it is done') -> model: 'I've set Bharat Dynamics (BDL) as the new symbol on your chart'; set_chart_indicators then leaks as text (never staged)
entries.evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/composer-chat/15-ask-autonomy-chart.jsonl, docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/composer-chat/15-ask-autonomy-chart.stdout.txt; sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py:174 (instruction), :1198-1215 (awaiting_user_review result)
entries.root_cause: The runtime tells the model not to claim staged actions but post-checks only publish_brief divergence, not staged host actions.
entries.fix_shape: When any tool result in the turn is awaiting_user_review, append a deterministic 'Staged for your review: ...' notice at end of stream. Test: ASK drive with set_chart_symbol yields the staged notice.

entries.title: Clearing a field in the Delegate budget editor removes that ceiling entirely and the server applies no default or validation (0/negative accepted), so a background run can have no wall-clock or spend bound
entries.repro: Switch the composer to Delegate mode, clear the "$" box in the budget row, send a task. BudgetConfig.tsx:40-45: e.target.value === '' -> n = undefined -> Number.isFinite(undefined) is false -> maxSpendUsd: undefined. lib/delegate-runs.ts:97-102 puts it in the body and JSON.stringify DROPS the key, so the sidecar receives no max_spend_usd; sidecar/services/budget_guard.py:152-156 guards every ceiling behind `if self.max_X is not None`, so absent = no ceiling. The durable background run has unlimited spend. || [COD-runs-durable-delegate-12] In the Delegate budget editor clear the 'sec' field -> onChange stores undefined -> JSON omits it -> max_wall_seconds=None -> asyncio.timeout(None) is a no-op; a stalled provider stream then holds the run in `running` forever. Clear all four -> only _MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS bounds the run. 0 / negative values are accepted and abort instantly.
entries.evidence: src/modules/chat/BudgetConfig.tsx:5-13, src/modules/chat/BudgetConfig.tsx:28-46, src/lib/delegate-runs.ts:96-103, sidecar/services/budget_guard.py:96-106, sidecar/services/budget_guard.py:152-157, sidecar/models/run.py:53-59 and :91 (all ceilings Optional, default None, no gt=0), sidecar/services/run_manager.py:258 (`budget or RunBudget()`), :145-152 (comment: 'the LLM adapters carry no per-stream timeout'; timeout(None) no-op), sidecar/services/budget_guard.py:3-4 ('unsafe to ship without a spend ceiling'), src/modules/chat/BudgetConfig.tsx:41-44 (empty input -> undefined) || refuter corrections: COD-frontend-panels-agent-shell-7: Mechanism confirmed: clearing a budget box sets that key to undefined, JSON.stringify drops it, RunBudget defaults it to None (models/run.py:55), and BudgetGuard.breach skips None ceilings, with no server-side default. Corrected: clearing only the '$' box does not make the run unbounded, because the token (120k), wall-clock (600 s) and step (12) ceilings still abort it. Truly unbounded spend needs all four boxes cleared, which is a deliberate multi-step act. Still a real hole in a component that promises 'never unbounded', so medium, not high.
entries.root_cause: BudgetConfig maps an empty box to undefined, JSON drops it, RunBudget ceilings are Optional with no default or gt=0, BudgetGuard skips None ceilings and asyncio.timeout(None) is a no-op; the trust gate depends on the client remembering to send it.
entries.fix_shape: Server-side floor in launch_run: fill each None ceiling from DEFAULT_BUDGET and add Field(gt=0); client falls back to the default on an empty box. Test: POST a run with an empty budget -> guard carries all four defaults.
entries.note: Batch-7 (e81c9e7) certified: `budget: {}` is stored as 120000 tokens / $1.0 / 600s / 12 steps; `maxSteps: 0` returns 422.

entries.title: Resume/answer re-enter a Delegate run with provider, model and api_key all None, so the 'resumable checkpoint' cannot work for any BYOK cloud run (and no UI calls resume)
entries.repro: Launch with provider=openrouter + key, let it breach (status=error), POST /runs/{id}/resume -> invoke_agent is called with provider/model/api_key all None (proved: scratch script prints `P4 resume invoke kwargs: {'provider': None, 'model': None, 'api_key': None}`), so it falls to spec.default_provider ('anthropic' for 10 bundled agents, keyless -> error; 'ollama' -> cold-loads a local model).
entries.evidence: sidecar/services/run_manager.py:401-412 (hard-coded None), sidecar/routers/runs.py:118 and :130 (routes never pass api_key/budget although the manager accepts them - test-only parameters, see sidecar/tests/test_run_manager.py:270,293), sidecar/models/run.py:144-149 (answer body has no key field), sidecar/services/runs_store.py:75 (allow-list persists only research_depth/region), sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py:524-536 (None -> agent defaults), sidecar/services/run_manager.py:399 (resume zeroes the recorded cost, so lifetime spend across resumes is understated), src/lib/delegate-runs.ts:226 (resumeDelegateRun has zero callers) || refuter corrections: COD-runs-durable-delegate-2: Mechanism fully confirmed: resume_run spawns with provider/model/api_key=None, routes never pass a key, RunAnswerRequest has no key field, provider/model are not persisted, and cost is reset to RunCost(); 10 of 13 bundled agents default to keyless anthropic. Severity lowered high->medium because no UI path reaches either resume (resumeDelegateRun has zero callers) or answer (no pause trigger, finding 10), so no user hits the failure today - it is a dead/false SC-008 claim rather than a broken core flow.
entries.root_cause: provider/model were never persisted with the run and the resume/answer routes accept no key; cost is also reset to RunCost() on resume.
entries.fix_shape: Persist provider+model in _PERSISTED_OPTION_KEYS, accept apiKey (header) on resume/answer, accumulate cost across resumes, and add a Resume control. Test: resume invokes with the persisted provider/model and the passed key.
entries.note: Batch-7 (e81c9e7) certified: Resuming a breached run keeps `provider: ollama`, `model: llama3.1:8b` (matches Ollama `/api/ps`); cost accumulates from 7,259 to 14,526 tokens over 2 steps; a dummy `X-LLM-Api-Key` sent on answer appears in no log line, DB column or `GET /runs` body.

entries.title: Resume and answer corrupt a Delegate conversation: the original prompt is replayed as the newest turn after the human's answer, and a second answer turns the first answer into the prompt
entries.repro: launch('ORIGINAL PROMPT') -> pause -> answer('ANSWER ONE'): provider receives [assistant, user 'ANSWER ONE', user 'ORIGINAL PROMPT']. pause -> answer('ANSWER TWO'): provider receives [..., user 'ORIGINAL PROMPT', assistant, user 'ANSWER TWO', user 'ANSWER ONE'] - the prompt is now the first answer (scratch proof P1a/P1b).
entries.evidence: sidecar/services/run_manager.py:126-129 (_drive_run writes history first, then the prompt, so the checkpoint no longer starts with the prompt), :369-382 (resume assumes 'first user turn = prompt'), :338-343 (answer appended as a raw dict), sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py:518-520 (history, then prompt as the last message), sidecar/services/run_manager.py:164-173 (tool RESULTS are never checkpointed, so a resumed run re-pays every tool call), sidecar/services/runs_store.py:27-28 (column documented as 'the accumulated messages list' - it is a display digest)
entries.root_cause: _drive_run writes history then the prompt, while resume_run assumes the first user turn is the prompt; the checkpoint format is known to four places with its one invariant broken by its own writer.
entries.fix_shape: Store {prompt, turns[]} explicitly; on answer send the answer as the new prompt with prior turns as history. Test: launch -> answer -> answer produces the correct provider message order.
entries.note: Batch-7 (e81c9e7) certified: Checkpoints are `{prompt, turns}` in order; for the ask_user run, the prompt is followed by `[ask_user -> ...]` then the user turn.

entries.title: The Delegate spend/token ceiling can overshoot: a breach flagged at a round boundary cannot stop the loop, so that round's tools run and the next provider request is sent and never metered
entries.repro: Faked provider that emits tool_use + done(100k tokens) every round, RunBudget(max_tokens=1000): the run aborts with 'token ceiling' but the provider was called TWICE (scratch proof prints `P5 ... provider calls after 1-round breach: 2 | cost: tokens=100000`) - round 2's request went out after the breach and its usage is not in the recorded cost.
entries.evidence: sidecar/services/run_manager.py:133-140 (callback only sets a flag), sidecar/services/run_manager.py:176-178 (the consumer can act only on the NEXT yielded event), sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py:1466-1473 (callback fires, then `break` to tool dispatch), sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py:1551-1575 (all pending tools dispatched - incl. paid search / deep research - before any event is guaranteed), sidecar/services/budget_guard.py:1-8 ('hard spend ceiling', 'aborts 100%')
entries.root_cause: _on_round_usage only sets a flag; invoke_agent breaks to tool dispatch without yielding, so the consumer can stop only on the next yielded event.
entries.fix_shape: Let the callback stop the loop (return a stop bool that invoke_agent honours before dispatch, or raise a private _BudgetBreach). Test: max_tokens=1000 with a 100k-token round -> exactly one provider call.
entries.note: Batch-7 (e81c9e7) certified: `maxTokens: 1000` with a tool-heavy prompt ends after 1 step with no tool activity, `error` "token ceiling 1000 reached (7259 used)", checkpoint `turns: []`.

entries.title: A Delegate run that completes on the round that touches a ceiling is recorded as error, hiding a finished answer
entries.repro: One-shot provider (delta + done), RunBudget(max_steps=1) -> row is status=error, detail='step ceiling 1 reached (1 taken)' while its transcript holds the complete answer (scratch proof P2). Same for a final round that crosses max_tokens / max_spend_usd.
entries.evidence: sidecar/services/budget_guard.py:162 (`>=` on an integer count: a budget of N steps aborts ON the Nth), sidecar/services/run_manager.py:183-188 (breach_reason wins even when the generator finished naturally), sidecar/services/run_manager.py:175 (`breach_reason` also carries agent error text - one variable, two meanings)
entries.root_cause: breach() uses >= on the step count and breach_reason wins over natural completion; breach_reason also carries agent error text.
entries.fix_shape: Record whether the final terminator was seen and prefer status=done with the ceiling noted; use > for steps. Test: one-shot provider with max_steps=1 ends done.
entries.note: Batch-7 (e81c9e7) certified: A one-shot answer under `maxSteps: 1` ends `done` "completed (step ceiling 1 reached (1 taken) on the final round)".

entries.title: Delegate launches an unattended, budget-spending run with no plan and no activity stream: the planner is gated off for delegate mode and the rail shows only tokens and dollars
entries.repro: Switch the composer to Delegate (Option+2), ask a compound task ('screen PSU defence names, compare the top 3, save a note') -> the run starts immediately: _planner_enabled returns False for mode 'delegate' (agent_runtime.py:110-112), so no plan is shown or approved; while it runs, the rail row shows agent name, mode, tokens and $ only (AgentsRail.tsx:94-108; cost.steps is carried but never rendered); research steps and tool actions are reduced to '[tool_use <name>]' strings inside the driver (run_manager.py:164-173) and never reach the client.
entries.evidence: sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py:110-112, sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py:1387-1413, sidecar/services/run_manager.py:164-181, src/modules/chat/AgentsRail.tsx:94-108, src/lib/delegate-runs.ts:30-38 (RunWire has no activity field), src/modules/chat/ChatSidebar.tsx:838-866; world: census/world/agent-native-ux.md W-1 (Cursor/Claude Code/Warp plan-before-execute; Linear plan as a checklist protocol object), W-7/W-8 (Linear AgentSession states incl. awaitingInput/stale; five typed activities thought/action/elicitation/response/error; 'frozen-in-time snapshots')
entries.root_cause: _planner_enabled returns True only for mode 'agent'; the driver flattens tool events to '[tool_use name]' strings and RunWire has no activity field.
entries.fix_shape: Enable the plan pre-pass for delegate with a confirm step before launch, and persist a typed activity list (tool, status, one-line result) on the run row rendered in the rail. Test: a delegate launch returns a plan and GET /runs/{id} lists activity rows.
entries.note: Batch-7 (e81c9e7) certified: On `nemotron-3-super:free`, a compound launch parks `planned` with 5 steps; `POST /runs/{id}/start` runs it to `done` with typed activity rows (compare_symbols ok, add_to_watchlist staged, set_chart_symbol staged); the activity half also ran live on Ollama.

entries.title: Conversation memory is a silent 10-message text window: after five exchanges older turns, and every prior tool result, identifier and failure, fall out of the agent's history with no meter, notice or compaction
entries.repro: In one chat space: turn 1 'I only care about FY26 guidance vs delivery for BDL, ignore the chart', then five more exchanges -> turn 7 asks 'so does that hold up?' -> the client sends only the last 10 display messages (ChatSidebar.tsx:749-753) and the runtime caps again at 10 (agent_runtime.py:482), so turn 1's constraint is gone; the UI shows nothing to say so. Per-message usage is stored (chat-history.ts:46-47, 213-216) but no component reads message.usage (grep: only the SSE parser at ChatSidebar.tsx:2027-2028). Tool results from earlier turns (fetched figures) never re-enter history at all. || [WLD-harness-context-2] Ask 6+ questions in one chat, then refer back to the first ('compare that with the pledge figure from earlier') -> turn 1 is gone from the provider request with no summary or marker. Or: turn N calls corporate_announcements and fails on BSE; turn N+1 has no trace of the failure (history carries only user/assistant prose) and retries the same dead path.
entries.evidence: src/modules/chat/ChatSidebar.tsx:749-753, sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py:469-482, src/store/chat-history.ts:46-47, src/store/chat-history.ts:213-216, src/modules/chat/ChatSidebar.tsx:2027-2028; world: census/world/agent-native-ux.md W-5 (Zed shows tokens for the active thread continuously and auto-compacts 'when approaching threshold limits'; 'the user must be able to see the window filling before it fills'), src/modules/chat/ChatSidebar.tsx:749-753 (.filter user|assistant .slice(-10)); sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py:469-482 (_coerce_history drops every non-string/tool turn and caps at 10 again), :506-521 (history spliced between preambles and prompt with no summary slot); src/store/chat-history.ts:1-12 (in-memory only); census/world/harness-context.md CHECKLIST 3, 5, 7 + 'keep the wrong turns' (S7, S12, S15 Factor 9)
entries.root_cause: The client sends only the last 10 user/assistant prose messages and _coerce_history caps again at 10 and drops tool turns; per-message usage is stored but never rendered.
entries.fix_shape: Replace FIFO deletion with a state-shaped summary slot (decisions, figures + their sources, failures) and carry tool-result identifiers across turns; show a context meter and an 'older turns summarised' marker. Test: a 7-turn thread's provider request contains the turn-1 constraint via the summary.

entries.title: No undo for an applied agent change: an accepted or AUTO-applied holding delete, position update or note replace is unrecoverable, and applied changes vanish from the review surface
entries.repro: design, verified in code: agent proposes portfolio_delete_position for a hand-entered holding (or write_note mode=replace on a symbol note) -> user clicks Accept (or AUTO applies it with no click, proposed-changes.ts:118-120) -> apply removes the holding / overwrites the note (host-actions.ts:1376-1389, 1176-1192) -> the change leaves ProposedChangesReview, which renders only status==='pending' (ProposedChangesReview.tsx:27) -> no Undo, no restorable pre-image (the stored 'before' is a prose string, host-actions.ts:790-815), no note/portfolio version history (src/store/notes.ts, src/store/portfolios.ts). The only record is a transcript line 'Applied: Remove X'.
entries.evidence: src/store/proposed-changes.ts:118-120, src/store/proposed-changes.ts:129-170, src/modules/chat/ProposedChangesReview.tsx:27, src/lib/host-actions.ts:790-815, src/lib/host-actions.ts:1176-1192, src/lib/host-actions.ts:1376-1389; world: census/world/agent-native-ux.md W-3 (Claude Code automatic checkpoints before each turn; Cursor snapshots 'restorable from the chat timeline'; Zed 'Restore Checkpoint' after every edit), W-2 (Warp: diff review is the default, auto-accept the opt-out), src/lib/host-actions.ts:545-560
entries.root_cause: accept() applies with no pre-image captured, the stored 'before' is a prose string, and the review renders only pending changes.
entries.fix_shape: Capture a typed pre-image for each data-write kind at apply time and offer Undo on applied rows for the session. Test: apply portfolio_delete_position then undo restores the holding.
entries.note: Batch-7 (e81c9e7) certified: `portfolio_delete_position` accepted, then holdings are `[]`; Undo brings back the same id, status `undone`. `remove_from_watchlist` followed by Undo restores the original list at the original index.

entries.title: With the Portfolio panel open, get_portfolio carries no position ids, so an agent update or delete lands on the first lot of that symbol rather than the lot the user meant
entries.repro: Panel open with RELIANCE x10, TCS x5 @2500, TCS x20 @3900 ('second lot'). captureTerminalState().portfolio.holdings has no `id` on any row (the closed-panel store fallback does carry ids). The catalog tells the model to 'read the current positions first with get_portfolio to learn the position_id'. applyHostActionAsync('portfolio_update_position', {position_id:'2', symbol:'TCS.NS', quantity:25}) -> 'Updated TCS.NS: ×25 @ ₹2,500': the x5 lot became x25, the x20 lot untouched. The same call also sent PUT /portfolio/positions/2 to the sidecar ledger: a numeric id the model invents addresses an unrelated ledger row (PUT /portfolio/positions/3 with a TCS body overwrote the RELIANCE ledger row, 200).
entries.evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/portfolio-notes/10-portfolio-panel-replay.json P9-agent (openPanelSnapshot vs closedPanelSnapshot, describe_update_by_symbol, after_update, net), docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/portfolio-notes/11-portfolio-routes-http.jsonl put-3-overwrite; src/modules/portfolio/PortfolioPanel.tsx:212-221 (published holdings omit id); src/modules/chat/context-provider.ts:242-258 (bus preferred), :166-187 (store fallback carries id); src/lib/host-actions.ts:545-560 (resolveHolding: id miss -> first symbol match), :1312-1317; sidecar/services/agent_tools/catalog.py:1338-1341, :1365
entries.root_cause: publishedHoldings omits id while the closed-panel store fallback includes it; resolveHolding falls back to the first same-symbol holding when the id misses.
entries.fix_shape: Publish id in publishedHoldings; resolveHolding refuses (asks) on an ambiguous symbol instead of picking the first lot; the review diff names the lot. Test: two TCS lots + update by id changes the right lot.
entries.note: Batch-6 (5e14731, commit 7f8c452) certified: get_portfolio's holdings now carry each row's id when the Portfolio panel is open (previously only the closed-panel store fallback carried ids); resolveHolding refuses a same-symbol ambiguous match (2+ lots, no id) instead of silently picking the first, naming each lot so the model can retry by position_id.

entries.title: write_screener_filters silently drops a malformed criterion and reports success for the rest, so the user's ROE filter vanishes and a looser screen runs
entries.repro: Same captured args with criteria as a real array: [{pe_ratio lt 20}, {roe gt {min:15,max:15}}, {debt_to_equity lt 0.5}] -> applyHostAction label 'Wrote 2 screener criteria — review and Run'; store criteria = pe_ratio + debt_to_equity only; a real run returns 200 rows (2,087 evaluated) with no ROE condition. entries.title: Tool-argument integrity is defended only in the OpenAI adapter; Groq and Ollama silently coerce malformed argument JSON to {} and Gemini passes args unchecked, so the model never learns its arguments were wrong
entries.repro: Groq/Ollama/Gemini model emits a truncated tool call, e.g. arguments fragment '{"symbol": "RELI' -> adapter yields LLMToolUseEvent(name='get_quote', input={}) with no error; the tool runs with no symbol and the model is never told its arguments were wrong

The stated consequence is overstated: symbol-keyed handlers validate their own required args and return {ok:False, error:'missing or non-string symbol'} to the model (price_data.py:35-37, fundamentals.py:179-181), so the model does get a self-correctable error, not a silent wrong-instrument answer; Gemini args arrive pre-parsed so no JSON-fragment truncation exists there. Residual: tools with only optional args silently run on defaults, and the error text is less specific. high -> medium.
entries.root_cause: Argument validation/repair lives inside one adapter instead of the runtime, so the three siblings do the 'never coerce to {}' thing the OpenAI adapter's comments forbid.
entries.fix_shape: Move schema validation of tool args to the runtime before dispatch (one place, catalog schema) returning an invalid-args result to the model; adapters pass raw strings through. Test: a truncated args fragment on each adapter yields an invalid-args tool result, never {}.

entries.title: Tool-arg repair makes unbounded, untimed, unmetered LLM round-trips inside the open SSE stream (one serial oneshot per failing call, each able to hang ~600 s)

entries.title: No prompt caching on the Anthropic lane, and the per-turn terminal preamble is folded into the one system string, so every round re-bills ~11.5k tokens of schemas and prompt at full price
entries.repro: design: any Anthropic BYOK turn (the default provider of 11 of the 13 first-party agents — every persona plus portfolio_advisor and strategy_critic). The adapter sends tools + one concatenated system string + messages with no cache_control breakpoint; a 4-round tool turn sends the ~11.5k-token prefix 5 times uncached. Even with a breakpoint, the system string changes every turn because the terminal preamble (focused chart, watchlist, open panels, viewport) is joined into it.
entries.evidence: sidecar/services/llm/anthropic.py:39-94 (_split_system_and_messages joins every system message into one string), :104-150 (stream_kwargs: no cache_control anywhere; grep cache_control over services/llm -> none); sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py:513-517 (persona, date, terminal preamble as three system messages in that order), :1434-1440 (tool schemas every round); sidecar/agents/*.json defaultProvider=anthropic (buffett.json:7 … strategy_critic.json:7); census/world/harness-context.md CHECKLIST 8 (S12: cached vs uncached is a 10x price difference; S7: cache_control at end of system prompt)
entries.root_cause: _split_system_and_messages joins persona, date and terminal preamble into one changing string and no cache_control breakpoint is sent; the runtime also rewrites already-sent tool results in place.
entries.fix_shape: Send system as blocks with cache_control on the stable persona+capabilities block (date/preamble uncached) and a breakpoint on the last tool result each round; stop mutating sent tool results. Test: captured request carries the breakpoints and a stable cached prefix across turns.

entries.title: With two chart panels and the second focused, the context preamble labels charts[0] 'Focused chart' and contradicts the deixis line in the same system message

The frontend builds `charts` by iterating Object.entries(bySource) -- bus insertion order (src/modules/chat/context-provider.ts:225-236) -- and resolves focusedSymbol from the chart whose panelId === focusedPanel (context-provider.ts:276-278). The sidecar then renders 'Focused chart: <charts[0].symbol> (<its timeframe>, <its indicators>)' and, four lines later, 'When the user says "this" or "it", they mean <focusedSymbol>'. entries.title: market_overview swallows a total news-feed failure into headlines:[] with ok:true, so the model tells the user there are no notable headlines when the feed is down

entries.title: Three hand-written MCP tools (list_agents/list_workflows/list_runs) turn a failing in-process route into an empty list, so an external client is told 'no agents' instead of 'broken'
entries.repro: design + code path. mcp_server.py:168-180 list_agents catches httpx.HTTPError and returns {'agents': []}; :297-313 list_workflows and :350-364 list_runs do the same. The same branch is reachable from _internal_client's own unbound fallback at :94 (base_url='http://127.0.0.1:0'), whose comment claims it 'exists so an early failure produces a useful error'. Meanwhile :244, :252 and :334 call raise_for_status() bare so a 404 escapes the tool as a raw httpx error.
entries.evidence: sidecar/services/mcp_server.py:178, sidecar/services/mcp_server.py:311, sidecar/services/mcp_server.py:362, sidecar/services/mcp_server.py:94, sidecar/services/mcp_server.py:244, sidecar/services/mcp_server.py:252, sidecar/services/mcp_server.py:334, sidecar/services/mcp_server.py:120 || refuter corrections: COD-mcp-servers-3: The swallow-to-empty is real (list_agents/list_workflows/list_runs map any httpx.HTTPError to an empty list), but the trigger is mis-stated: in production bind_app is always called so the tools use the in-process ASGITransport and the 127.0.0.1:0 fallback is unreachable; the actual path is a 5xx from the in-process route -> raise_for_status HTTPStatusError (an HTTPError) -> confident empty list. The three bare raise_for_status sites do not escape as raw transport errors either - FastMCP/lowlevel server convert a raising tool into an isError=True result. A rare in-process 5xx is a medium, not high, silent degradation.
entries.root_cause: They catch httpx.HTTPError (including raise_for_status on a 5xx) and return []; the file carries three incompatible error policies.
entries.fix_shape: Return {ok:false, error} on any HTTPError (the policy already used at :116-122) for all hand-written tools. Test: a 500 from /agents yields ok:false.

entries.title: The fundamentals agent tool discards ProviderError.kind and re-derives it by substring, so a real not_found (instrument does not exist) is reported as provider_error ('our feed's gap')
entries.repro: ProviderError("Yahoo has no company record for 'KSE.NS'", kind='not_found') -> _classify_reason('provider error: ...') returns 'provider_error' (verified). Same for ProviderError("yfinance returned a non-company (fund-id) record for '509470.BO'", kind='not_found').
entries.evidence: sidecar/services/agent_tools/fundamentals.py:67-68, sidecar/services/agent_tools/fundamentals.py:44-51, sidecar/services/agent_tools/fundamentals.py:33-41, sidecar/services/yfinance_provider.py:334-342, sidecar/tests/test_fundamentals_tool.py:90-101 || refuter corrections: COD-fundamentals-profile-4: Real and reproduced: _fetch_once stringifies the ProviderError and drops .kind (agent_tools/fundamentals.py:67-68). _classify_reason then returns 'provider_error' for both yfinance not_found messages (yfinance_provider.py:334-342) and for the registry's own kind=not_found 'no provider returned usable' error (provider_registry.py:435-438). entries.title: News sentiment scoring and symbol tagging live in the HTTP route, so the agent and MCP news tool return unscored, untagged items while claiming to mirror GET /news; raw watchlist symbols like BTC/USDT also tag nothing
entries.repro: Call the `news` agent tool. news_tool.py:46 calls news_provider.fetch_news directly and returns item.model_dump() at news_tool.py:55 with no enrichment; every NewsItem therefore carries sentiment=None, sentiment_label=None, symbols=[] (defaults at models/news.py:24-26). The GET /news route does the enrichment itself at news.py:115-130 (sentiment.score_text + _tag_symbols). Second half: _tag_symbols' regex (news.py:72) is \b-anchored and needs the literal symbol string, so a raw watchlist symbol like 'BTC/USDT' never matches a headline saying 'Bitcoin'/'BTC'; because `requested` is non-empty the route then drops every untagged item (news.py:120-121) and returns an empty list. The frontend defends this by projecting through toNewsSymbol (NewsFeedPanel.tsx:170, BTC/USDT -> BTC); the agent path has no such projection.
entries.evidence: sidecar/routers/news.py:115, sidecar/routers/news.py:72, sidecar/routers/news.py:120, sidecar/services/agent_tools/news_tool.py:4, sidecar/services/agent_tools/news_tool.py:46, sidecar/models/news.py:24, src/modules/news/NewsFeedPanel.tsx:170
entries.root_cause: Enrichment belongs to the service but sits in the router, so the second consumer silently degrades; _tag_symbols needs the literal symbol string.
entries.fix_shape: Move scoring + tagging into news_provider (one enrich step) used by both route and tool, and normalise symbols before tagging. Test: news tool items carry sentiment and symbols; symbols=BTC/USDT returns items.

entries.title: There is no way to add a user-chosen MCP server: only openbb-mcp and sec-edgar-mcp are wired, with no config surface, route or UI
entries.repro: Try to point Vysted at any third-party MCP server (e.g. https://mcp.kite.trade/mcp, an Upstox or screener.in server). There is no config surface, no route, no UI.
entries.evidence: grep -riE 'mcp_servers|mcpServers|add_mcp|external_mcp|custom_mcp|register_mcp' over sidecar/ src/ src-tauri/src/ types/ returns ZERO hits. The two subprocesses are hardcoded in Rust: src-tauri/src/openbb_mcp.rs, src-tauri/src/sec_edgar_mcp.rs. sidecar/routers/mcp.py exposes only /mcp/status (:28) and /openbb-mcp/status (:44). World inventory of servers Vysted cannot consume: Zerodha official (https://github.com/zerodha/kite-mcp-server), Upstox x2 (https://glama.ai/mcp/servers/adibhattar95/upstox-mcp-server), Angel One SmartAPI, Dhan, Groww, multi-broker (https://lobehub.com/mcp/sharuniyer-indian-broker-mcp), ~8 screener.in scrapers (https://github.com/ronyv89/screener-mcp). || refuter corrections: WLD-T-5: The core claim holds: the product has no config, route or UI to add a user-chosen MCP server, and only openbb-mcp and sec-edgar-mcp are wired. Three corrections. (1) The 'universal tool layer' promise in the constitution and spec is MCP-as-SERVER, where one catalog is projected to external clients; nothing promises consuming user-added servers, so there is no positioning contradiction. (2) A generic stdio/http McpClient already exists (mcp_client.py:218), so the missing piece is only a config surface. (3) Most of the cited example servers are broker servers, which are now out of scope. Downgraded high -> medium.
entries.root_cause: A generic stdio/http McpClient exists (mcp_client.py:218) but nothing exposes it; subprocesses are hardcoded in Rust.
entries.fix_shape: Config surface (servers list in the workspace/settings) + Rust spawn for stdio servers + read-only declaration enforced by the existing wrapper audit. Tier-4: adds a user-controlled subprocess/tool layer to the core architecture, so the operator decides scope.
entries.note: blocked_tier4 (batch-10 PLAN.md §4 deferred list): adds a user-controlled subprocess/tool layer to the core architecture, so the operator decides scope (see DECISIONS_FOR_OPERATOR.md 2.12).

entries.title: Registered kill-switch chord is Ctrl+Cmd+Shift+K (all three modifiers AND-ed), not the documented CmdOrCtrl+Shift+K, so the emergency chord never matches while an OS-wide chord is grabbed for a dead event
entries.repro: [COD-safety-audit-2] Read src-tauri/src/kill_switch.rs:35-38: Modifiers::SHIFT | Modifiers::SUPER | Modifiers::CONTROL is a bitflag AND-requirement. The crate's own CmdOrCtrl parse sets SUPER on macOS OR CONTROL elsewhere, never both (~/.cargo/registry/src/*/global-hotkey-0.7.0/src/hotkey.rs:212-217). Pressing Cmd+Shift+K (mac) or Ctrl+Shift+K (win/linux) therefore never matches the handler's `shortcut != &kill_switch_shortcut()` guard.
entries.evidence: [COD-safety-audit-2] src-tauri/src/kill_switch.rs:34-39 (the OR'd modifiers), :20,:30,:75 (docs + log line claim CmdOrCtrl+Shift+K); src/modules/safety/DisclaimerFlow.tsx:45 (TOS tells the user Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+K); docs/SAFETY_ARCHITECTURE.md:119,240; no Rust test references kill_switch_shortcut (grep src-tauri/src) -- refuter admitted_with_correction (high->medium): The bug is real: Shortcut::new(SHIFT|SUPER|CONTROL) registers Ctrl+Cmd+Shift+K and HotKey::matches is an exact equality on modifiers, whereas the crate's CmdOrCtrl parse sets SUPER on macOS or CONTROL elsewhere, never both. Downgraded high->medium: today it has no functional consequence because nothing listens for the emitted event (-1), so the only live effect is an OS-wide chord grabbed for a dead event. Mechanism scope: the kill switch gates ONLY broker order placement - its sole subscriber is BrokerAdapter.__init__ (sidecar/services/broker_base.py:103) and its sole is_fired readers are propose/confirm (broker_base.py:251,345); no workflow, agent run or other control-plane action subscribes or checks it (grep of non-test sidecar), so the whole mechanism goes with trading.
entries.root_cause: Shortcut::new(SHIFT|SUPER|CONTROL) requires all three modifiers; HotKey::matches is exact equality, whereas CmdOrCtrl means SUPER on macOS or CONTROL elsewhere.
entries.fix_shape: Refuters established the kill switch gates ONLY broker order placement (sole subscriber BrokerAdapter.__init__, sidecar/services/broker_base.py:103; sole is_fired readers the propose/confirm gates, broker_base.py:251,345) and the audit log has only trading writers. Operator decides (Tier-4, §6.5): if the 23 Sep trading removal deletes the kill switch + audit log with trading, this entry closes with that commit; if the mechanism is kept, apply: cfg-gate SUPER (macOS) vs CONTROL (else) or parse "CmdOrCtrl+Shift+K", plus a Rust unit test asserting equality with the parsed string.
entries.closure_reason: kill_switch.rs and its OS-wide shortcut were deleted whole; the chord bug has no surviving code to affect.

entries.title: write_text_atomic / write_bytes_atomic accept any absolute path from the webview with no confinement, and CSP is null, so any webview script can write arbitrary bytes anywhere the user can write
entries.repro: [COD-rust-core-5] design — invoke('write_bytes_atomic', { path: '<any absolute path>', contents: [...] }) from any script in the webview writes those bytes there; the command validates nothing beyond dest.parent() and then create_dir_all's it.
entries.evidence: [COD-rust-core-5] src-tauri/src/lib.rs:287-310 (write_text_atomic) and :318-342 (write_bytes_atomic) — no path validation; src-tauri/src/lib.rs:410-411 (both in the production invoke_handler); src-tauri/tauri.conf.json app.security.csp = null; the guard lives in callers and only in some of them: src/modules/notes/notes-persistence.ts:68 strips [/\\] from the scope, src/lib/export-artifact.ts:76-88 interpolates subdir + filename straight in; docs/research/phase-10/hunt-rust-tauri.md 'SECURITY HARDENING — csp: null' reported the CSP half and it is unfixed at 2d99cda -- refuter admitted_with_correction (high->medium): The missing boundary is real: write_text_atomic/write_bytes_atomic take any path and only create_dir_all the parent (lib.rs:287-342), they are in the release invoke_handler (lib.rs:410-411), app commands are unrestricted (no AppManifest in build.rs), and CSP is null. Corrected on two particulars: (1) 'one caller already forgot' is wrong in effect - export-artifact.ts saveTextArtifact interpolates subdir/filename unsanitised, but its only callers (NotesPanel.tsx:225,236,247) pass the constant 'notes' and a base name sanitised at NotesPanel.tsx:220; (2) the plugin threat model cited does not exist today - plugins are static bundled imports (plugin-runtime.ts:26-28, marketplace.ts:8-41), not runtime-loaded third-party JS, and the finder itself found no injection sink. Defense-in-depth gap with no live vector: medium, not high.
entries.root_cause: Path confinement was pushed up into callers (notes-persistence sanitises, export-artifact interpolates) instead of held by the command; no CSP backstop. No live injection vector today (no innerHTML sinks, plugins are static imports).
entries.fix_shape: One private write_atomic(path, bytes) that canonicalises the parent and rejects anything outside app_data_dir(); both commands become one line over it (collapses the write_atomic duplication entry). Rust test: a path outside app_data_dir is refused. The CSP half touches tauri.conf.json (Tier-1) -> operator; the lib.rs half can proceed independently.
entries.note: blocked_tier4 (batch-10 PLAN.md §4 deferred list): the CSP half edits src-tauri/tauri.conf.json (Tier-1) (see DECISIONS_FOR_OPERATOR.md 2.13).

entries.title: Plugin Manager enable/disable toggle lies: disable stops the instance in memory only (back after restart, panels/commands/agents never leave) and enable of a Marketplace-disabled plugin is a no-op
entries.repro: [COD-plugins-1] Open the Plugin Manager panel -> flip any active plugin's toggle off -> restart the app. The plugin is active again. Before restarting: its panels/slash commands are still in cmd+K and its agents still in the chat roster.
entries.evidence: [COD-plugins-1] src/components/PluginManagerPanel.tsx:171-185 (calls runtime.unloadPlugin directly), src/lib/plugin-runtime.ts:278-295 (unloadPlugin touches no persistence), src/store/marketplace.ts:176-191 (the sibling path calls disablePlugin + unbridgePluginModule + syncPluginAgents(false) + disconnectBroker), src/lib/plugin-bootstrap.ts:262-264 (boot re-reads plugins.db, which still says enabled:true) -- refuter admitted_with_correction (high->medium): Real: PluginRow.handleToggle calls runtime.loadPlugin/unloadPlugin directly; unloadPlugin persists nothing, so boot re-reads enabled:true and reloads it, and no unbridge/agent-sync runs. The reverse direction is also dead: toggling ON a Marketplace-disabled plugin is a no-op because loadPlugin honours persisted enabled:false. Severity corrected high->medium: the designated lifecycle surface (Marketplace store enable/disable) is correct; this is a second, lying control on a secondary panel, not a broken core flow.
entries.root_cause: The panel calls the runtime primitives (loadPlugin/unloadPlugin) while the Marketplace store calls the policies (disablePlugin + unbridge + syncPluginAgents + persistence).
entries.fix_shape: Route PluginRow.handleToggle through useMarketplaceStore.enable/disable; structural: move persist+bridge+agent-sync into PluginRuntime.enable/disable so every caller is thin. Pin with a test that toggling off persists enabled:false and unbridges the module.

entries.title: 'Is this plugin on?' lives in two independent stores (plugins.db enabled and workspace enabledModules['plugin:<id>']) that only one of three code paths keeps in sync; restoring an older named workspace hides the panels of a plugin re-enabled since
entries.repro: [COD-plugins-12] design (drift hazard, reachable via COD-plugins-1): plugins.db `enabled` and the workspace blob's enabledModules['plugin:<id>'] are written by different callers; disable via the Plugin Manager writes neither, disable via the runtime writes only the first, unbridgePluginModule writes only the second.
entries.evidence: [COD-plugins-12] sidecar/services/plugins_store.py:38-44 (plugins.db enabled column), src/lib/workspace.ts:50,263 (workspace.enabledModules -> setEnabledMap replaces the map wholesale on restore), src/lib/plugin-runtime.ts:344-348 (disablePlugin writes only plugins.db), src/lib/plugin-bootstrap.ts:193-194 (unbridgePluginModule writes only the module map), src/store/marketplace.ts:182-183 (the only caller that writes both). Four sites encode the never-persisted default and disagree: plugin-runtime.ts:221, plugin-runtime.ts:310, plugin-bootstrap.ts:262-263, store/marketplace.ts:109-110/123-125 -- refuter admitted (medium->medium): Holds: plugins.db enabled and the workspace blob's enabledModules['plugin:<id>'] are independent; disablePlugin writes only the former, unbridgePluginModule only the latter, and workspace restore replaces the whole enabled map (so an older named workspace carrying plugin:x=false hides panels of a plugin re-enabled since). The never-persisted default is spelled at four sites with two answers.
entries.root_cause: No single owner for the enabled fact; the never-persisted default is spelled at four sites with two different answers (true vs row.entry.preinstalled).
entries.fix_shape: One lifecycle owner writes both, or derive the module-enabled flag from runtime state instead of persisting it in the workspace blob; one shared default. Pin with a test restoring a workspace blob with plugin:x=false over a re-enabled plugin.

entries.title: Saving a BYOK secret for an already-active plugin never re-runs initialize(), so PluginConfig.secrets stays stale until restart (and a green test locks the no-op)
entries.repro: [COD-plugins-3] Marketplace -> Configure any plugin that is already active (e.g. vysted-news, preinstalled+enabled) -> save a key. The keychain write lands and grantedSecretIds is persisted, but initialize() is never called again, so the running instance keeps the secrets map it got at boot (empty).
entries.evidence: [COD-plugins-3] src/store/marketplace.ts:238-244 (comment: 'Reload so the plugin resolves the new secrets via PluginConfig.secrets' -> calls runtime.enablePlugin), src/lib/plugin-runtime.ts:339-342 (enablePlugin -> patchConfig -> loadPlugin), src/lib/plugin-runtime.ts:199-202 (loadPlugin returns early when state is 'active'), src/lib/plugin-runtime.test.ts:171-177 (green test locks the no-op: initialize called once after two loadPlugin calls), types/plugin.ts:41-42 (PluginConfig.secrets is the contract's designated credential channel) -- refuter admitted_with_correction (high->medium): Mechanism holds: configure() calls enablePlugin -> patchConfig -> loadPlugin, which returns early for an active record, so initialize() never re-runs and PluginConfig.secrets stays stale; the green test locks that idempotence. Severity corrected high->medium because it is latent: no bundled plugin reads config.secrets for a credential (only plugins/example reports the key ids), vysted-news reads its key out-of-band, and the broker consumers are being removed.
entries.root_cause: configure() calls enablePlugin -> patchConfig -> loadPlugin, which returns early for an active record; the comment claims a reload.
entries.fix_shape: Add a real runtime.reloadPlugin() (unload then load) and call it from configure(); update the test that asserts initialize() is called once to assert it re-runs after configure. Latent: no bundled plugin reads config.secrets for a credential yet.

entries.title: Plugin data contribution is declaration-only: getDataSources() output only feeds a count in the Plugin Manager subtitle, VystedPlugin.subscribe has no host call site, so DataSource.realtime cannot be honoured and a data plugin cannot serve one quote
entries.repro: [INT-blueprint-48-5] Write a plugin with `contributesData: true` and a DataSource; it loads, and the only effect anywhere in the app is the count in the plugin-manager subtitle (`${dataSources.length} data sources`, src/components/PluginManagerPanel.tsx:42). No panel, store or sidecar route resolves a read through a plugin-contributed source. The bundled reference plugin says so in its own header: 'The actual data flows through the sidecar's provider_registry (this plugin is a thin declaration of the source...)' (plugins/yfinance/index.ts:1-11). Likewise `VystedPlugin.subscribe` (types/plugin.ts:251) has no host call site in src/ and no implementor in plugins/, so `DataSource.realtime: true` (types/plugin.ts:84) cannot be honoured.
entries.evidence: [INT-blueprint-48-5] types/plugin.ts:76-87,236,251; src/lib/plugin-runtime.ts:419-425; src/store/plugins.ts:62,86; src/components/PluginManagerPanel.tsx:28,42; plugins/yfinance/index.ts:1-11; plugins/openbb-mcp/index.ts:168 -- refuter admitted (medium->medium): Holds. getDataSources() output goes only into the plugins store (plugin-runtime.ts:422, store/plugins.ts:62,86), and its only reader is the PluginManagerPanel count (PluginManagerPanel.tsx:28,42). Nothing in src/ calls `VystedPlugin.subscribe`: the runtime's own `subscribe` (plugin-runtime.ts:525) is a UI-listener API. So `DataSource.realtime` (types/plugin.ts:86) cannot be honoured, and yfinance/index.ts:1-11 admits the plugin is a declaration only. This does not reopen the plugin system's existence; it is an inert contract slice.
entries.root_cause: The data slice of the contract was never wired to a resolution seam; actual data flows only through the sidecar provider_registry (plugins/yfinance/index.ts:1-11 admits it).
entries.fix_shape: Operator choice (contract honesty is Tier-4): either a resolution seam (provider_registry entry backed by a plugin-declared sidecar route) or document DataSource as a declaration and mark realtime/subscribe reserved in types/plugin.ts + PLUGIN_DEVELOPMENT.md. Pin with a test that a declared source is either resolvable or flagged not-runnable.
entries.note: blocked_tier4 (batch-10 PLAN.md §4 deferred list): contract honesty on types/plugin.ts (Tier-1) (see DECISIONS_FOR_OPERATOR.md 2.14).

entries.title: The Notify Desktop workflow node never produces an OS notification: the bridge reads useWorkflowStore, which no production code writes to
entries.repro: [COD-workflow-engine-5] Run a workflow containing action.notify_desktop from the node editor -> NodeEditorPanel consumes SSE with its own consumeSse + local setRunState and never calls useWorkflowStore.appendEvent -> pendingNotifications stays empty -> useDesktopNotificationBridge (mounted in page.tsx:43) never fires.
entries.evidence: [COD-workflow-engine-5] src/store/workflow.ts:173-192,203-220,240-311 (the only intent capture + a second full SSE client); grep: no production caller of runWorkflow/appendEvent outside src/store/workflow.ts (only src/lib/desktop-notification.ts reads the slice); src/modules/node-editor/NodeEditorPanel.tsx:386-431,937-976 (separate SSE parser); src/app/page.tsx:43; sidecar/services/workflow_nodes/builtin.py:325-344 -- refuter admitted (medium->medium): No production code calls useWorkflowStore.appendEvent or runWorkflow: the only consumer of the store is the notification bridge (src/lib/desktop-notification.ts), while NodeEditorPanel runs its own fetch + consumeSse + local setRunState. The bridge mounted in page.tsx therefore never receives an intent, so the Notify Desktop node never produces an OS notification.
entries.root_cause: Two SSE clients / run-state models for one wire; NodeEditorPanel runs its own consumeSse + local state while the notification bridge listens to the dead store (376 lines, unit-tested in isolation).
entries.fix_shape: NodeEditorPanel dispatches every server event through useWorkflowStore.appendEvent (or calls the intent capture directly); delete the store's unused runWorkflow SSE client and dead clearRun/clearAll. Pin with a NodeEditorPanel test that a notify_desktop node-complete event enqueues a notification.

entries.title: transform.code has two evaluators with different semantics: the editor (mathjs) and the agent/MCP path (Python ast) disagree on round(2.5), '^' and ternaries for the same saved workflow
entries.repro: [COD-workflow-engine-6] round(2.5): mathjs 3 vs server 2; 2^3: mathjs 8 vs server 'disallowed syntax: BinOp'; 'a > 1 ? 1 : 0': mathjs 1 vs server parse error (both measured). A workflow authored and tested in the editor then run by the agent via MCP run_workflow yields a different value or fails.
entries.evidence: [COD-workflow-engine-6] sidecar/services/workflow_nodes/code_node.py:20-45,97 (Python round = banker's rounding, '^' unsupported, no ternary); src/modules/node-editor/code-node.ts:1-27 (mathjs); stale comments claiming no server handler exists: src/modules/node-editor/code-node.ts:26-27, src/modules/node-editor/code-node-run.ts:12-15; now-obsolete restriction: code-node-run.ts:63-74; sidecar/services/mcp_server.py:258-285 -- refuter admitted (medium->medium): The server lane really is a separate Python-ast evaluator with different semantics (banker's rounding, '^' parsed as BitXor and rejected, no ternary), and the client comments claiming no server handler exists are stale since code_node.register() is called from register_all. entries.title: Quant workflow nodes run CPU-bound pricing synchronously on the sidecar event loop (Monte Carlo up to 10M paths, binomial up to 100k steps), freezing every sidecar route for the duration
entries.repro: [COD-workflow-engine-8] A workflow with quant.price_option {method: 'monte-carlo', monte_carlo_paths: 10000000} (MAX_MC_PATHS) or binomial_steps up to 100000 -> options.price runs inline in the async handler, freezing the whole sidecar for the duration.
entries.evidence: [COD-workflow-engine-8] sidecar/services/workflow_nodes/quant_nodes.py:46-52,57-63,68-74,79-85 (sync calls, no to_thread); sidecar/models/quant.py:33-34 (MAX_BINOMIAL_STEPS=100_000, MAX_MC_PATHS=10_000_000); contrast sidecar/services/workflow_nodes/builtin.py:62-64,87-89,121 (to_thread) and sidecar/routers/quant.py:36-37 (sync def -> threadpool) -- refuter admitted (medium->medium): All four quant adapters call options.price / greeks / bonds / yield_curve synchronously inside async handlers, while the builtin adapters use asyncio.to_thread and the HTTP /quant routes are sync defs (threadpool). Parameters up to MAX_BINOMIAL_STEPS=100000 (binomial prices ~9 trees for FD greeks) and MAX_MC_PATHS=10M are accepted as valid, so a user-permitted config stalls the whole sidecar loop.
entries.root_cause: The four quant adapters call options/greeks/bonds/yield_curve inline in async handlers, unlike the builtin adapters (to_thread) and the /quant HTTP routes (threadpool).
entries.fix_shape: asyncio.to_thread around each quant call (four one-line changes), landing with or after the QuantLib evaluation-date lock (else the date race becomes reachable here); ideally the engine runs every handler off-loop under a per-node timeout. Pin with a test that a long pricing does not block a concurrent /health.
entries.note: Batch-7 (e81c9e7) certified: Frozen batch-7 binary: a 20k-step American binomial prices while `/health` stays fast (worst 0.224s under EOF, 0.014s under TERM); stdin EOF exits 0 and SIGTERM exits -15 with 4 processes before and 0 leftover after both. entries.title: Workflow engine has no per-node or per-run timeout and schedules in gather-barrier waves, so a slow node stalls unrelated dependants and a hung handler keeps the run (and the MCP run_workflow call) open forever
entries.repro: [COD-workflow-engine-9] Sources A (flow.sleep 300 s or a hung provider fetch) and B (fast); C depends only on B -> C does not start until A finishes because each wave is awaited with asyncio.gather. A handler that never returns keeps the run (and the MCP run_workflow tool call) open indefinitely.
entries.evidence: [COD-workflow-engine-9] sidecar/services/workflow_engine.py:3-5 (docstring: 'runs downstream nodes when their inputs are available'), :210-282 (ready-set recomputed only after the whole wave's gather), :366-367 (await handler with no wait_for); sidecar/services/mcp_server.py:282-283 (no timeout around run_workflow) -- refuter admitted (medium->medium): The scheduler recomputes the ready set only after asyncio.gather of the whole wave, so a slow node delays unrelated dependants, and the handler call has no wait_for; the MCP run_workflow tool awaits the engine with no timeout either. Only flow.sleep has a bound (300 s).
entries.root_cause: The ready set is recomputed only after asyncio.gather of the whole wave; handlers are awaited without wait_for; the docstring says the opposite.
entries.fix_shape: Schedule with asyncio.wait(FIRST_COMPLETED) so each completion releases its dependants, and wrap each handler in asyncio.wait_for(node_timeout) producing node-error; pin with an A(slow)/B(fast)/C<-B test asserting C starts before A ends.

entries.title: Backtest engine replaces an existing position on a second buy: cash is debited for every buy but only the last lot is held, so a flat market reports -3.0% total return and orphaned entries never reach the metrics

Result: 4 trade rows recorded, cash correctly debited 4 x 1001 = 4004, but portfolio.positions['AAA'] holds 10 shares not 40 -> final equity 96996 and metrics.totalReturn = -0.03004 on a market that never moved. The three orphaned entry rows keep pnl=None forever, so tradeCount/winRate never see them.
entries.evidence: [COD-backtest-3] sidecar/services/backtest_engine.py:343 (`portfolio.positions[intent.symbol] = _OpenPosition(...)` — assignment, not merge), sidecar/services/backtest_engine.py:324 (comment directly above reads `# New long position OR add to existing`), sidecar/services/backtest_engine.py:114-118 (equity marks only the surviving position) -- refuter admitted_with_correction (high->medium): Mechanism confirmed (buy assigns a fresh _OpenPosition, orphaning the earlier one while cash stays debited, under a comment claiming 'add to existing'), but it is unreachable in the shipped product: register_strategy is only called by register_all for four strategies, all of which gate entries on has_position, and plugins have no backtest-strategy registration path. Latent maintainer trap, not a core flow that breaks today -> medium.

entries.evidence: [COD-backtest-4] sidecar/services/backtest_engine.py:362-365 (position looked up, then `portfolio.cash += abs(intent.quantity) * fill_price` with no reconciliation against position.quantity), sidecar/services/backtest_engine.py:371 (pnl computed on abs(intent.quantity)), sidecar/services/backtest_engine.py:385 (`portfolio.positions.pop(...)` regardless of size), sidecar/services/backtest_engine.py:368-370 (comment parks the partial-close case as a 'documented limitation') -- refuter admitted_with_correction (high->medium): Mechanism confirmed (sell credits abs(intent.quantity) with no reconciliation against position.quantity, then pops the whole position), but, as with COD-backtest-3, every registered strategy exits with quantity=-held, so no shipped path (UI, custom DSL, agent tool) can over-sell. entries.title: snapshot_structured's 'never raises' promise is not held by its own asyncio.gather: one cross-check without its own try/except breaks every research path
entries.repro: design - fast.py:377-385 gathers seven cross-checks without return_exceptions; wrappers call should_cross_check outside any try. Add a cross-check that raises -> FAST, DEEP, ULTRA and tier-B all raise out of snapshot_structured (only DEEP has a caller-side except).

entries.root_cause: The no-raise guarantee is delegated to each helper's own except (dividend_history, market_cap_witness, range_check) instead of the gather that owns the promise.
entries.fix_shape: asyncio.gather(..., return_exceptions=True) + coerce BaseException to None before the folds. Test: monkeypatch one cross-check to raise and assert snapshot_structured returns a result with that leg absent.

entries.title: Hardware-fit has no Windows branch: every Windows machine is reported as exactly 8 GiB RAM / 4.4 GiB budget (presented as measured), so the onboarding local-model recommendation is scored against a constant; dedicated VRAM is never detected on Windows or Linux
entries.repro: [HYG-3] cd sidecar && ./.venv/bin/python -c "import platform; from services import hardware_fit as h; platform.system=lambda:'Windows'; print(h.detect_device(force=True).to_dict())" -> ramGib 8.0, gpuBudgetGib 4.4 regardless of the machine; GET /system/local-model-recommendation then picks/rejects candidates on that constant (a 4 GB laptop is over-recommended, a 32 GB RTX box steered to cloud keys)
entries.evidence: [HYG-3] sidecar/services/hardware_fit.py:203-219 (Darwin -> _detect_macos, Linux -> _detect_linux, else _detect_fallback), sidecar/services/hardware_fit.py:182-197 (_detect_fallback: ram = 8 * _GIB hardcoded), sidecar/services/hardware_fit.py:124-132 (non-Apple: 55% of RAM, dedicated VRAM never detected on Windows or Linux), sidecar/services/hardware_fit.py:86-95 (to_dict emits ramGib with no estimated/provenance flag), sidecar/routers/system.py:106-140 -- refuter admitted (medium->medium): detect_device routes anything not Darwin/Linux to _detect_fallback, which hardcodes ram = 8 GiB and a 55% CPU budget; to_dict emits it as ramGib with no estimated flag, and /system/local-model-recommendation picks the onboarding model from it. psutil is not installed, so there is no other RAM source on Windows. Linux reads /proc/meminfo correctly but, like Windows, never detects dedicated VRAM. Re-checked 23 Sep: sidecar/services/hardware_fit.py:182-186 `ram = 8 * _GIB`, :209-216 Darwin/Linux/else-fallback routing. hardware_fit.py is owned by market-data-providers-1 in CODE_PARTITION.
entries.root_cause: detect_device routes every non-Darwin/non-Linux OS to _detect_fallback, which hardcodes 8 GiB; to_dict carries no estimated/provenance flag; psutil is not installed.
entries.fix_shape: Add _detect_windows via ctypes GlobalMemoryStatusEx (~15 lines, no new dependency) and an `estimated: bool` on DeviceProfile.to_dict that the onboarding UI surfaces for fallback profiles; unit-test with a monkeypatched platform.system + ctypes stub asserting real RAM is read and fallback profiles are flagged estimated. VRAM detection (nvidia-smi/DXGI) is a separate follow-up.

entries.title: The deterministic layout modes (Fundamental / Technical / Macro / Compare / Reset) exist only in the macOS native menu; Windows/Linux can reach them only via '/layout', which goes through the gated, additive, viewport-downgraded fitLayoutTemplate path the menu bridge was written to avoid
entries.repro: [HYG-4] On Windows/Linux: install_layout_menu is #[cfg(target_os = "macos")], so vysted://menu-layout is never emitted and applyLayoutMode (its sole caller is menu-bridge.ts:33) is unreachable; the command palette exposes no layout modes; '/layout research-cockpit' enqueues arrange_layout through the proposed-changes gate and the fit-downgraded path, and its ids differ from the menu labels
entries.evidence: [HYG-4] src-tauri/src/lib.rs:344-350 (#[cfg(target_os = "macos")] install_layout_menu, doc: 'Windows/Linux keep their existing chrome untouched'), src-tauri/src/lib.rs:495-500, src/lib/menu-bridge.ts:4-13 and :33 (sole applyLayoutMode caller), src/modules/chat/ChatSidebar.tsx:667-672 (/layout -> enqueueSlashChange('arrange_layout')), src/lib/host-actions.ts:1038-1047 (fitLayoutTemplate) -- refuter admitted (medium->medium): install_layout_menu and its call are both #[cfg(target_os = "macos")], menu-bridge.ts is the only caller of applyLayoutMode, and the command palette exposes panels/agents/actions/symbols but no layout modes. Off-Mac the only route is /layout, which enqueues arrange_layout through the gate and the additive fit-downgraded path, and its argument names (research-cockpit, single-focus) differ from the menu labels (Fundamental, Technical). The Mac-only scope is a documented choice (lib.rs:344-347), but it still leaves Windows/Linux without the deterministic modes. Re-checked 23 Sep: src-tauri/src/lib.rs:343-350 doc + cfg gate. Related but distinct: R15-AGENT-055 (same template id means a different layout per entry point).
entries.root_cause: The layout modes were added as a macOS-only native menu (documented Mac-first choice, lib.rs:344-347) with no platform-neutral command surface.
entries.fix_shape: Register the five modes as command-palette commands that call applyLayoutMode / resetToDefaultLayout directly; make the macOS menu dispatch those same commands. Pin with a vitest asserting the palette registry contains every menu-bridge mode id and that invoking one calls applyLayoutMode.

Any later change upstream is invisible: pressing Load with 'AAPL' again sets the same string so React bails and the effect never re-runs; the Retry button calls the same cached accessor, which short-circuits on the cache. No control in the panel can re-fetch, and no timestamp is rendered. Same for the earnings drill-down caches (history/surprises/estimates). || COD-market-data-providers-2-8: GET /earnings/{sym}/history twice within 24h -> the second call is served entirely from data_cache with no field on the wire saying when it was fetched. entries.root_cause: getX accessors return cached payloads unconditionally (no fetchedAt, no eviction), Load/Retry hit the same cache; EarningsHistory/Surprises/Upcoming envelopes have no as_of.
entries.fix_shape: Have data_cache return fetched_at and stamp as_of on each envelope; store {payload, fetchedAt} in the stores with a TTL, render an as-of chip and a Refresh (NewsFeedPanel refreshNonce precedent). Pin with a store TTL test.

entries.title: News fabricates now() as the publication time for undated items and sorts newest-first, so an undated headline is presented as the freshest story
entries.repro: design. _parse_struct_time returns _utcnow() when the feed entry has no published_parsed/updated_parsed or the value is malformed; _parse_iso does the same for NewsAPI's publishedAt. fetch_news then does `unique.sort(key=lambda item: item.published_at, reverse=True)`. An RSS item with no date therefore sorts to position 0 and renders with the current timestamp, above genuinely recent stories.
entries.evidence: COD-market-data-providers-1-15: sidecar/services/news_provider.py:151, sidecar/services/news_provider.py:161, sidecar/services/news_provider.py:395, sidecar/services/news_provider.py:204 || refuter (COD-market-data-providers-1-15, admitted): Confirmed: _parse_struct_time and _parse_iso both return _utcnow() for a missing or malformed date, published_at is a required datetime in the model, and fetch_news sorts newest-first, so an undated item sorts to the top stamped 'now'. No live instance appeared in the current RELIANCE.NS feed (0 of 50 items stamped within 120 s of now), but the code path holds. || refuter severity_final: COD-market-data-providers-1-15=medium
entries.root_cause: _parse_struct_time/_parse_iso return _utcnow() for missing/malformed dates; published_at is required.
entries.fix_shape: Make published_at optional, leave it None when unparseable, sort nulls last and render 'date unknown'; pin with an undated RSS item.

entries.title: A cold-cache BSE range request silently returns at most 8 daily bars as if that were the year, and the registry never tries the lane that has the full history
entries.repro: design. _assemble_history walks trading days newest-first with `downloads_left = _MAX_COLD_DOWNLOADS` (8); once spent, every further missing day is skipped. On a cold cache a range='1y' request therefore returns at most 8 daily bars, wrapped in an ordinary OHLCVSeries(symbol, timeframe='1d', bars, provider='bse') -- no coverage field, no partial marker, no warning. The chart renders 8 points as if that were the year.
entries.evidence: COD-market-data-providers-1-16: sidecar/services/bse_provider.py:87, sidecar/services/bse_provider.py:437, sidecar/services/bse_provider.py:402, sidecar/services/bse_provider.py:406 || refuter (COD-market-data-providers-1-16, admitted): Confirmed: _MAX_COLD_DOWNLOADS=8 bounds newest-first downloads per call, the result is a plain OHLCVSeries with no coverage or partial field, the gate checks only the last bar, and non-empty bars end the registry walk before yfinance. No background BSE bhavcopy warmer exists (only the NSE bhavcopy lane), so deep history fills only at about 8 days per chart request. || refuter severity_final: COD-market-data-providers-1-16=medium
entries.root_cause: _MAX_COLD_DOWNLOADS=8 bounds downloads per call; OHLCVSeries has no coverage field; non-empty bars end the registry walk.
entries.fix_shape: Add a coverage/partial field (or raise when the span is materially short so the registry falls through); pin with a cold 1y request.
entries.note: Batch-10 (f407107) not certified: Left open by the writers (D-B10-8, one leg): the registry fall-through is not delivered. Observed: cold 1y BSE-only history (ICONIKSPEV.BO) served 246 bars, partial false - the <=8-bar case did not reproduce today, but nothing certifies the flagged fall-through. || Batch-11 (4097dac) certified: Cold `/history/KARNAVATI.BO?range=1y` served bse with 256 bars (2025-09-10 to 2026-09-24), a complete lane. entries.title: The bundled trading-holiday tables end on 2026-12-25 with no regenerator or expiry test, and already miss 2026 BSE non-session days, so freshness labels drift
entries.repro: design. locale._NSE_HOLIDAYS's latest entry is '2026-12-25' and _US_HOLIDAYS's is '2026-12-25' (today is 2026-09-19). After that date _is_trading_day returns True for every holiday, so most_recent_session walks back to a non-session day and trading_sessions_between over-counts the lag; is_rejectably_stale then rejects a value that is in fact as fresh as the exchange allows. There is no scripts/ or services/resolver_masters/-style regenerator for these sets and no test asserting the table extends past today.

entries.title: The live-lookup LRU caches a successful empty search forever, so a stock listed after the first miss stays unresolvable for that query until the app restarts
entries.repro: First resolve of an unknown name falls to _live_lookup, which caches the result -- INCLUDING a successful empty search -- under (query, region) with no expiry (only a 128-entry LRU bound). entries.evidence: COD-resolver-10: sidecar/services/symbol_resolver.py:124, sidecar/services/symbol_resolver.py:990, sidecar/services/symbol_resolver.py:1033, sidecar/services/symbol_resolver.py:982 || refuter (COD-resolver-10, admitted): Holds: _live_lookup caches the result, including an empty successful search, under (query, region) with only a 128-entry LRU bound and no timestamp, so a negative result persists for the sidecar's lifetime. entries.root_cause: _live_lookup caches (query, region) -> rows including [] with only a 128-entry bound; the live rung is the only path to post-snapshot listings.

entries.title: Tool-arg repair accepts a JSON-schema echo from the model as valid tool args instead of retrying
entries.repro: During the tool-arg repair round (the retry path that runs when a model's tool call has invalid JSON args), a model response that merely echoes the tool's JSON schema back (rather than filling in real argument values) was accepted as if it were valid args, instead of being rejected and retried or surfaced as a failed call.
entries.evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/stage-c/batch-5/VERDICTS.md, Issues found outside the entries #9 (verifier batch-5)
entries.root_cause: The repair round's args validator checks JSON-shape validity but not whether the payload is the tool's own schema echoed back rather than a filled instance.
entries.fix_shape: Reject a repair response whose payload structurally matches the tool's input schema (keys are the schema's property names mapped to type-name placeholders, not real values) and retry or fall back to the invalid-args sentinel used elsewhere in the repair path; pin with a test that feeds the repair round a schema-echo response and asserts it is rejected, not executed.
entries.note: Batch-6 (5e14731) certified: services/llm/openai.py OpenAIProvider._repair_tool_args/_validate_tool_args now reject a repair reply that is the JSON Schema itself echoed back (plain, fenced, or prose-wrapped). Live: 8/8 vulnerable no-required-key tools now reject the echo (0 accepted post-fix); legit args still pass. Closes the hole batch-5's verifier flagged as issue #9.
