entries.title: A sidecar spawn failure is indistinguishable from a slow boot: the documented SidecarPort==0 'disconnected' sentinel is honoured nowhere, so a missing or denied binary ends in a 120 s blind spinner and a message that names nothing
entries.repro: Rename the bundled sidecar binary and launch -> get_sidecar_port still returns the picked live-looking port; the frontend probes /health for 120 s and then shows 'The data engine did not become ready in time.' The real cause is only on stderr (which a packaged app never shows; see the diagnostics entry).
entries.evidence: src-tauri/src/lib.rs:440-441 (SidecarPort managed once, before the spawn), src-tauri/src/lib.rs:206-222 (every spawn-failure arm eprintln!s and returns without updating state), src-tauri/src/lib.rs:201-204,272-279 (doc: '0 means no sidecar bound ... the frontend treats that as disconnected'), src/lib/sidecar-client.ts:96-98 (port interpolated with no zero check), src/lib/sidecar-client.ts:124-141 (120_000 ms deadline, generic SidecarError(503)); port-0 half also observed in COD-error-layer-12 (folded into R15-LIFECYCLE-027); docs/research/phase-10/hunt-rust-tauri.md BUG 3 (reported, unfixed); refuter admitted medium
entries.root_cause: The sentinel exists only in prose: no producer sets it on failure and no consumer tests it; SidecarPort is a bare u16 set before the spawn.
entries.fix_shape: Replace SidecarPort(u16) with a SidecarStatus { port, state: Starting|Ready|Failed(reason) } set from start_main_sidecar's failure arms and the port-wait thread; the renderer short-circuits on Failed and renders the reason. Pin with a Rust unit test that a spawn-failure arm yields Failed(reason) and a vitest that a Failed status throws immediately with the reason instead of probing.

entries.title: sidecarStatus is a one-shot boot latch: nothing re-probes, so the header stays green 'Connected' over a dead engine, boot-time 'error' has no retry short of reload, and the retry hook's 're-arm on reconnect' fires at most once per app lifetime
entries.repro: grep -rn 'connectSidecar\|sidecarStatus:' src plugins -> the only caller is src/app/page.tsx:52 (mount effect), the only writers src/store/app.ts:25,29,32. Kill the sidecar after boot -> the chip keeps bg-positive 'Connected' while every panel and the chat fail with 'Load failed'. Let boot hit the 120 s budget -> status 'error' with no control that calls connectSidecar again.
entries.evidence: src/store/app.ts:24-34, src/app/page.tsx:45-52, src/lib/use-sidecar-retry.ts:19-22,113-135, src/components/StatusChrome.tsx:88-106,173,203-210,217-220, src-tauri/src/lib.rs:226-238 (child Terminated event dropped); refuter admitted medium
entries.root_cause: The status is written only by the boot-time connect; no heartbeat, focus re-probe, or failure-path write exists, while two consumers were designed against a live status.
entries.fix_shape: Make the error layer the writer: sidecarGet/consumeSseStream set sidecarStatus='error' (and null readyPromise) on a connection-level failure and 'connected' on any success; add click-to-reconnect on the chip calling connectSidecar(); optionally a 15-30 s /health heartbeat. Pin with a vitest that a connection-refused sidecarGet flips status to 'error' and a later success flips it back and re-runs a hooked load.

entries.title: 'Durable' Delegate runs are row-deep: no startup reconciliation and a checkpoint written only at exit, so a restart leaves zombie `running` rows and a hard kill leaves a run that cannot be resumed
entries.repro: Launch a run, call run_manager.shutdown() (what the lifespan does) -> the row stays status=running forever. On a crash / kill -9 / power loss the row is running with checkpoint_json NULL -> POST /runs/{id}/resume -> 404 'no checkpoint to resume from'. A webview that outlived the sidecar shows a forever-pulsing row with frozen cost.
entries.evidence: sidecar/services/run_manager.py:185-192,210-218 (checkpoint only on terminal exits; CancelledError path writes no status), :421-438 (shutdown), sidecar/app.py:136-155 (no startup sweep; the 'FIRST' comment at :149 is wrong), sidecar/services/runs_store.py:6-8; refuter admitted medium
entries.root_cause: Durability covers only the terminal row write; nothing reconciles 'running' rows at startup and the checkpoint is not written per round.
entries.fix_shape: At lifespan startup: UPDATE runs SET status='error', detail='interrupted by sidecar restart' WHERE status='running'; write the checkpoint inside _on_round_usage (which already writes cost). Pin with a test that inserts a running row, runs the startup hook, and asserts status=error; and a test that a run cancelled mid-round has a non-null checkpoint and resumes.
entries.note: Batch-7 (e81c9e7) certified: A run killed mid-flight (stdin EOF) while `running`, 1 step, 7,277 tokens; checkpoint already non-null (written at the round, not at exit). On restart, `GET /runs/{id}` reads `error` "interrupted by sidecar restart"; it resumes (200) and then cancels (200, `cancelled`).

entries.title: Delegate resume drops the user's provider/model and silently runs on the agent default (live: Ollama swapped llama3.1:8b for Qwen2.5 7B), and the paused/answer state is unreachable
entries.repro: Launch a delegate run with ollama llama3.1:8b and max_tokens 2000 -> error 'token ceiling 2000 reached (10126 used)' -> POST /runs/{id}/resume -> Ollama log 07:46:58 loads 'Qwen2.5 7B Instruct' (evicting llama). POST /runs/{B}/answer on any run -> 409 'not awaiting an answer'; no code path ever pauses a run.
entries.evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/composer-chat/30-delegate-launch.txt, docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/composer-chat/31-delegate-lifecycle.txt, sidecar/services/run_manager.py:260-269 (launch persists options+region only), :301 (pause_run: no caller outside tests), :402-407 (resume spawns with provider=None, model=None), sidecar/routers/runs.py:127-130; CROSS-CLUSTER: live confirmation of the same defects already merged as R15-AGENT-035 (COD-runs-durable-delegate-2) and R15-CODE-AGENT-011 (COD-runs-durable-delegate-10) - fold into those at register build; refuter admitted medium
entries.root_cause: The run row never persists provider/model, the resume route takes none, and pause_run has no production caller.
entries.fix_shape: Persist provider/model on the run row at launch and pass them on resume; wire pause_run to an ask_user tool or remove the paused/answer UI. Pin with a test that launch -> resume invokes the agent with the launch-time provider/model.
entries.note: Batch-7 (e81c9e7) certified: Resuming a breached run keeps `provider: ollama`, `model: llama3.1:8b` (matches Ollama `/api/ps`); cost accumulates from 7,259 to 14,526 tokens over 2 steps; a dummy `X-LLM-Api-Key` sent on answer appears in no log line, DB column or `GET /runs` body.

entries.title: A malformed or missing agent JSON silently shrinks the roster: warning log only (nothing at all for a missing agents dir), HTTP 200, no runtime surface
entries.repro: Schema-violate any file in sidecar/agents/ (e.g. a defaultProvider the enum omits) -> _discover_specs logs 'agent <file>: schema violation ...' and continues; _specs is built once at import. GET /agents returns 200 with 12 entries instead of 13. A missing agents dir returns {} with no log at all (the packaged-app 'agents/ silently unavailable for 3 releases' shape).
entries.evidence: sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py:237-238 (missing dir -> {} silently), :250, :256, :280 (built once at import), sidecar/routers/agents.py:68, sidecar/tests/test_agent_runtime.py:95 (CI count is the only detector); refuter admitted medium
entries.root_cause: Partial-load resilience with no report: skipped files and their reasons are discarded after a log line, and the packaged app has no log (see R15-LIFECYCLE-008).
entries.fix_shape: Keep the skipped filenames + reasons in a module-level list and expose them on GET /agents (and /health) as a `degraded` field; log an ERROR when the agents dir is missing; have the smoke test assert /agents count > 0 and degraded == []. Pin with a test that drops a bad agent JSON into a temp agents dir and asserts the degraded field names it.

entries.title: Backtest run history is in-memory and capped at 32, so a restart or the 33rd run makes backtest_summary forget a run the user is still looking at, and the documented 'newest first' list order is wrong
entries.repro: Put three results; backtest_store.list_runs() returns them oldest-first (and get() reorders by LRU) while the route documents 'newest first'. Restart the sidecar or run a 33rd backtest -> backtest_summary(run_id=<older run>) returns 'no cached backtest with run_id=...', so the Strategy Critic cannot critique a run still on screen.
entries.evidence: sidecar/services/backtest_store.py:23 (DEFAULT_CAPACITY = 32), :31 (plain OrderedDict, no disk), :41-48, sidecar/routers/backtest.py:176; refuter admitted medium (in-memory was a disclosed v0.5.0 choice; the Critic consequence stands)
entries.root_cause: Results live only in a 32-entry process-memory LRU; list() returns OrderedDict order.
entries.fix_shape: Write results as JSON under <data-dir>/backtests keyed by run_id (load on miss), and return the list newest-first. Pin with a test that a result survives a store re-instantiation and that list order is newest-first after a get().

entries.title: Kill-switch halt state lives only in process memory: a sidecar restart silently un-halts, and reset leaves adapters latched read-only while status says not fired
entries.repro: Fire the switch, restart the sidecar -> GET /safety/kill-switch/status -> fired:false with no acknowledgement and no audit row. Separately: fire -> reset -> status fired:false, but every adapter still raises 'adapter is in read-only mode' because _on_kill_switch latched _read_only and reset() never broadcasts.
entries.evidence: sidecar/services/kill_switch.py:54-56 (three instance attrs), :146-152 (reset touches only the bus), :198 (per-process singleton), sidecar/routers/safety.py:129-131, sidecar/services/broker_base.py:103,251,345,441; related audit gap R15-CODE-PLATFORM-008 (COD-safety-audit-5); refuter admitted medium, noting the kill switch gates ONLY broker order placement, so the whole mechanism goes with the 23 Sep trading removal
entries.root_cause: Fired state is not derived from the durable append-only audit store, and reset does not undo the adapter latch.
entries.fix_shape: OPERATOR DECISION FIRST (tier4, §6.5): if the trading removal deletes the kill switch with order placement, close this with it; otherwise derive fired state at boot from the last kill-switch audit row (after R15-CODE-PLATFORM-008 adds that row) and broadcast reset to un-latch adapters. Pin with a test that fire -> new KillSwitch instance -> status fired:true.
entries.closure_reason: The kill-switch bus and its halt state were deleted whole; there is nothing left to un-halt.

entries.title: Screener enrichment swallows every exception as 'field missing' at DEBUG and stalls its own progress bar on failure, so a broken adapter looks like a slow upstream
entries.repro: An adapter bug that raises AttributeError inside get_fundamentals during phase E -> every survivor reports missing_field:<f>, nothing above DEBUG is logged, and 'enriching fundamentals n/m' freezes because emit is reached only on the success path.
entries.evidence: sidecar/services/screener.py:984-993 (except (TimeoutError, Exception); DEBUG log; failure branch increments done without emit); refuter admitted medium
entries.root_cause: A catch-all except (TimeoutError is already an Exception) conflates expected upstream failures with code bugs, and progress emission lives only on the success path.
entries.fix_shape: Catch (TimeoutError, ProviderError) for the expected cases, log anything else at WARNING, and move done += 1 / emit(...) into a finally. Pin with a test whose stub adapter raises AttributeError and asserts a WARNING plus progress reaching m/m.

entries.title: The web_search hot path documented as an 'instant in-process read, no network probe' awaits a full docker derivation (up to one ~15 s docker-version timeout on a wedged daemon) on the first search of every process, and a concurrent first search reads a stale None
entries.repro: Code read: web_search.py:88 calls manager.ready_base_url_detected(), whose first call per process awaits refresh() -> detect() ('docker version', 15 s budget) + docker inspect + docker port + a 5 s health probe. _hot_path_detected is set True BEFORE the await, so a concurrent first search floors to keyless while the derivation is in flight.
entries.evidence: sidecar/services/agent_tools/web_search.py:10-13,85-88 (both comments promise no probe), sidecar/services/searxng_manager.py:91,97,337-353,412-446 (derivation), :348-349 (flag set before await), :361-371 (code 124 -> early return bounds the stall); refuter admitted_with_correction medium ('tens of seconds' overstated; at most one ~15 s timeout)
entries.root_cause: A lazy one-shot derivation was put on the hot path while the comments describe the intended eager design.
entries.fix_shape: Run the one-shot derivation in the app lifespan startup (background) and keep the hot path on the pure ready_base_url() read; if it must stay lazy, set the flag after the await under self._lock. Correct both comments. Pin with a test that web_search's first call performs no subprocess when the lifespan derivation has run.

entries.title: One failed rename-master fetch at boot turns the NSE rename lane off for the rest of the IST day, silently: a renamed scrip answers with its dead identity and its current ticker resolves to an unrelated US company
entries.repro: Clean profile boot on :52225: log 'nse_symbol_change: request failed ()' then 'no file and no recent cache - rename lane is a no-op' (the URL answered 200 in 1.35 s a minute later). GET /resolve?q=GUJGASLTD -> 'Gujarat Gas Limited', former_name null; GET /resolve?q=GUJENERGY -> needs_disambiguation led by US 'UR-ENERGY INC'. Same query on a sidecar whose fetch succeeded -> GUJENERGY with 'renamed ... effective 2026-07-01'. Further /resolve calls never retry until IST midnight (mock-transport proof: attempts stays 1).
entries.evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/lifecycle/L1-stranger/http-log.jsonl R01,R02, lifecycle/L1-stranger/sidecar-log-nonrequest.txt, lifecycle/L1-stranger/rename-gate-proof.txt, sidecar/services/nse_symbol_change.py:379-382,417-427,430-437,450-451, sidecar/routers/resolve.py:91,140, sidecar/services/symbol_resolver.py:793-799; refuter admitted medium
entries.root_cause: _refresh_guarded stamps _refreshed_on = today in a finally regardless of outcome, so a failure counts as today's refresh; the warning logs str(exc), which is empty for httpx timeouts.
entries.fix_shape: Set _refreshed_on only on success or a successful stale-cache hydrate; retry a failure with bounded backoff; log type(exc).__name__; expose rename_lane: unavailable on /resolve while the map is empty. Pin with a mock-transport test: first fetch ConnectTimeout, second schedule_refresh after the backoff -> attempts == 2 and the map loaded.

entries.title: At boot the sidecar starts a US-only S&P 500 warm loop every ~40 s whatever the region, spending the shared Yahoo circuit on 506 US symbols on an India-first install
entries.repro: Clean keyless IN profile on :52225, no user requests for ~5 min: /system/provider-health yahoo open at t=27 s (throttles 16), 4 opens by 357 s; log 'screener warm: rate-limited' backoff 64 -> 110 -> 227 s. At T+11 min POST /screener/run {universe:'sp500'} -> evaluated 0, skipped 506 'rate_limited'; POST {universe:'nifty50'} (the IN default) cold -> 44.8 s. Confound: other isolated sidecars on the same IP and the India warm worker were also on Yahoo, so the circuit timing is not attributable to this loop alone; the region-blindness and boot-time start stand on the code.
entries.evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/lifecycle/L1-stranger/idle-boot-sampler.jsonl, lifecycle/L1-stranger/sidecar-log-nonrequest.txt, lifecycle/L1-stranger/http-log.jsonl P00-P04, sidecar/app.py:127-134, sidecar/services/screener.py:107-110,147-148,1208,1295 (_WARM_UNIVERSES = ('sp500',)); refuter admitted medium
entries.root_cause: _WARM_UNIVERSES is a constant ('sp500',) and start_warm_precompute runs unconditionally in the lifespan, on the same circuit user requests use.
entries.fix_shape: Warm the region's default universe (nifty50 for IN), start the first cycle after a grace period or the first UI request, and keep background warming from opening the circuit user requests share (a separate budget or a lower-priority weight). Pin with a test that an IN-region start_warm_precompute schedules nifty50, not sp500.

entries.title: A dead or moved NSE endpoint is invisible: /health keeps naming nse_direct as primary, provider-health tracks only Yahoo, and an .NS chart silently switches to BSE bars (last-bar volume 10.7M -> 0.56M)
entries.repro: Own sidecar :52226 behind a loopback proxy refusing *.nseindia.com: GET /quotes/RELIANCE.NS -> provider bse; GET /history/RELIANCE.NS?range=3mo -> provider bse, last-bar volume 560,999 vs 10,684,376; GET /health byte-identical to base; GET /system/provider-health -> yahoo only. Same with the NSE API path moved (404): /health unchanged, one WARNING per request, retried every call.
entries.evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/lifecycle/L2-rot/http-log.jsonl (profiles base/deadhost/moved, tags Q1/Y1/H1/H2/P1), sidecar/services/provider_registry.py:362-364 (per-request WARNING, no counter), :552-570 (/health from importability), sidecar/services/nse_provider.py:139-146 (available = curl_cffi imports), :323-341 (breaker counts 401/403 only), sidecar/services/provider_health.py:49 (YAHOO only), src/modules/chart/ChartPanel.tsx:1420-1421; refuter admitted medium (the per-surface 'via bse' chip does flip)
entries.root_cause: Provider availability is importability, not liveness; fall-throughs are logged but never counted, and provider_health tracks one family.
entries.fix_shape: Count fall-throughs per (provider, model_key) in _resolve_sync/_resolve_async, expose them on /system/provider-health, derive /health's primary from recent success, and show one quiet chrome notice ('NSE data unreachable - serving BSE') above a threshold. Pin with a test that N consecutive nse_direct ProviderErrors surface on /system/provider-health.

entries.title: A moved NSE bhavcopy archive path is read as a week of holidays: every past weekday's 404 is cached as an empty 'holiday' marker with no log, the UDiFF-primary 404 never tries the live legacy fallback, and the IN EOD freshness lane silently dies
entries.repro: In-process on a fresh cache: UDiFF and legacy URLs moved -> fetch_latest() makes 6 requests, all 404 -> None, cache now holds {'empty': true} for 22, 21, 18, 17, 16 Sep. Only the primary moved -> 'missing' returned before the legacy sec_bhavdata_full fallback (200 / 2,921 rows for 22 Sep) is ever requested. The only signal is 'no bhavcopy found within 7 days'; the live 'moved' sidecar logged nothing. The symbol-change master fails the same way (404 -> 30-day stale 'network down' -> inert).
entries.evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/lifecycle/L2-rot/30-parser-drift.txt (C1-C3, D1), sidecar/services/nse_bhavcopy.py:101 (7-day TTL), :345-348 (any 404 -> 'missing', no log, before the fallback), :388-394 (past-date missing -> _EMPTY_MARKER), sidecar/services/fundamentals_warm.py:254-265, sidecar/services/nse_symbol_change.py:380-386,418-426; refuter admitted_with_correction medium (poisoning is bounded by the 7-day TTL; sharper: the fallback is never tried on a primary 404)
entries.root_cause: 404 is overloaded as 'holiday or not yet published', so an endpoint move is indistinguishable from a holiday and is cached as one; a primary 404 short-circuits the fallback.
entries.fix_shape: Try the legacy fallback on a primary 404; only write the holiday marker when the date is on the NSE holiday calendar (or the next trading day's file exists); log a WARNING naming the URL after N consecutive non-holiday weekday 404s. Pin with a test where the primary 404s and the fallback returns rows -> fetch_latest returns the fallback data and no empty marker is written.

entries.title: No React error boundary anywhere: one panel's render throw blanks the whole cockpit (portfolio and chat included) with no message or recovery, and the stack goes to a console a release build cannot open
entries.repro: Design (NEEDS-GUI to show visually): src/main.tsx:17 createRoot(...).render(<StrictMode><Page/></StrictMode>) passes no onUncaughtError/onCaughtError; grep -rn 'componentDidCatch|ErrorBoundary' src -> 0 non-test hits; dockview portals every panel into the same root. React's documented default: 'if your application throws an error during rendering, React will remove its UI from the screen' (https://react.dev/reference/react/Component). A relaunch restores the same autosave and can re-crash.
entries.evidence: src/main.tsx:17-21, src/components/PanelHost.tsx (DockviewReact components={components}, no per-panel wrapper), src-tauri/Cargo.toml:25 (no devtools); refuter admitted medium
entries.root_cause: No error boundary is installed at the panel host or root, so any render throw unmounts the entire tree.
entries.fix_shape: Wrap each dockview panel component (at PanelHost's component map) in an error boundary rendering 'this panel crashed - reload panel / copy error', and pass onUncaughtError to createRoot to write the stack to the diagnostics log. Pin with a vitest mounting PanelHost with a throwing panel and asserting sibling panels still render.

entries.title: No persistent store records a schema version (user_version 0 on all 8 SQLite DBs; no top-level workspace blob version) and nothing backs up the data dir before a new build touches it, so the first non-additive schema change will crash or silently drop data
entries.repro: Copy the 19-Sep 0.8.0 data dir, boot current source on it, sqlite3 <db> 'PRAGMA user_version' for audit_log, custom_agents, data_cache, delegate_runs, fundamentals_cache, plugins, portfolio, workflows -> 0 for every one, before and after boot. Clean today only because 0.8.0 -> HEAD changed no schema. 2,678 screener:* rows orphaned in data_cache since 5142aa1.
entries.evidence: $ISO/seat-l4-upgrade/evidence/pre-boot-schema.txt + post-boot-schema.txt, additive guards only at sidecar/services/fundamentals_store.py:172-182, sidecar/services/runs_store.py:94-102, sidecar/services/plugins_store.py:53-67; CREATE-IF-NOT-EXISTS only at sidecar/services/portfolio_db.py:26-35, agents_store.py:23 ('no schema migrations'), workflow_store.py:26-34, data_cache.py:59-65, models/audit_log.py:21; src/lib/workspace.ts:174 (only MODEL_OVERRIDES_VERSION); refuter admitted medium
entries.root_cause: Each store hand-rolls 'add a nullable column' guards; there is no version marker, migration chain, pre-upgrade backup or downgrade detection.
entries.fix_shape: One shared sidecar helper migrate(conn, steps) keyed on PRAGMA user_version used by all 8 stores (audit_log's append-only triggers untouched); a top-level schemaVersion on SerializedWorkspace with a migrate chain in deserializeWorkspace; a one-time copy of the data dir to backups/<old-version>/ when the stored app version differs from the running one. Pin with a test that a store at user_version 0 is migrated to N and a second boot is a no-op.
entries.note: audit_log.db is moot: deleted whole (a122dbf6 feat(d81)). Core finding stays open: no DB carries a schema version and nothing backs up the data dir before a build touches it, across the 7 surviving databases (custom_agents, data_cache, delegate_runs, fundamentals_cache, plugins, portfolio, workflows). || Batch-11 (4097dac) certified: Booted a copy of the iso data dir whose data_cache build marker was set to `0.7.9-prior`. Log: "data dir backed up to .../backups/0.7.9-prior before the upgrade". The backup holds every db, notes, workspaces and searxng, with dev-keystore.json kept at mode 600. `meta.build` is now 0.8.0. All seven stores went from user_version 0 to 1 on first touch: data_cache, fundamentals_cache and workflows at boot, portfolio and delegate_runs and plugins and custom_agents on their routes. Fresh cases: a workflows.db copy set to user_version 7 comes back from `schema_version.migrate` as 7 with the "newer than this build's 1; left untouched" warning; a fresh DB migrates to 1 and a second call is a no-op. vitest: the v0 workspace blob round-trips with schemaVersion, and a newer blob is not downgraded.

entries.title: A custom agent saved on the v0.8.0 tag silently loses its 'macro' tool: the id was renamed with no alias or row migration, every adapter drops unknown ids without a log, and re-saving the agent 422s
entries.repro: The tag's agents_store.create_agent(custom:macro-hawk, tools=['price_data','macro','news']) -> boot current source -> GET /custom-agents returns the tools unchanged -> schemas.openai_tools(spec.tools) -> ['price_data','news'] ('macro' not in TOOL_SCHEMAS) -> PUT /custom-agents/custom:macro-hawk with the same tools -> 422 "unknown tool ids: ['macro']". The system prompt still says 'Always check the macro series first'.
entries.evidence: $ISO/seat-l4-upgrade/evidence/v080tag-agent-tools.txt, git show v0.8.0:sidecar/models/custom_agent.py:30-38, commit 0e248f9 (ids now macro_series/macro_search), sidecar/services/agent_tools/schemas.py:50-51 (_known() filters silently), sidecar/models/custom_agent.py:55-63, sidecar/services/agent_tools/catalog.py:94-96 (Capability.aliases has no reader); distinct from COD-frontend-panels-agent-shell-2 (builder strip); refuter admitted medium

entries.title: Under light realistic load the sidecar burns ~60% of a CPU core continuously, 99% of it on the event-loop thread and mostly between requests (a clean idle sidecar sits at 0-0.8%)
entries.repro: L6 soak (source sidecar :52229, copy of the operator data dir, region IN, keyless, soak.py: 8 cheap GETs per 60 s cycle, portfolio CRUD every 10th, one free-model invoke every 15th). ps -p <pid> -o etime,utime,time: 8:10.43 CPU at etime 13:41 -> 10:53.62 at 18:13 = 163 s CPU in 272 s wall (60%), 92% user; ps -M puts 10:49.65 of 10:53.62 on the main (asyncio loop) thread; requests fill ~60 s of the window, so >=100 s of CPU fell between them.
entries.evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/lifecycle/L6-longsession.md section 5, <scratch>/vysted-iso/soak/soak-mem.jsonl, docs/redesign/verification/r15/lifecycle/L1-stranger/idle-boot-sampler.jsonl (baseline), sidecar/app.py:127-134 (lifespan starts screener warm, fundamentals_warm, nse_symbol_change refresh), sidecar/services/fundamentals_warm.py:199,301,373, sidecar/main.py:142; partial contributor found by the refuter: sidecar/services/provider_registry.py:406-407 calls sync provider functions on the loop inside async routes (fundamentals.py:89, quotes.py:53/65); refuter admitted medium (subsystem assignment provisional until profiled)
entries.root_cause: unknown (no profiler attached in the census stage); sync provider calls on the loop explain request-time CPU only.
entries.fix_shape: First `py-spy dump`/`sample <pid> 10` of the loop thread during an idle gap to attribute; then move the hot path off the loop (asyncio.to_thread for the sync provider calls in provider_registry and any spinning background loop). Pin with a soak assertion that idle-between-cycles loop CPU stays under a bound (e.g. < 5% over 5 min).
entries.closure_evidence: 4097dac merge(r15): stage C batch 11 - 18 certified fixes at 9985b00e
entries.note: Batch-11 (4097dac) certified: Source sidecar, 5-minute idle window: process CPU went from 31.68 s to 41.57 s, so 3.3% process-wide. The last ~40 s of that window overlapped the start of the eval, so true idle is lower. A 5 s `sample` of the loop thread shows 3694/3703 samples in `uv__io_poll`/kevent (loop 99.8% idle); the 12 worker threads are parked on locks. Grep: `_resolve_async` runs accessors via `asyncio.to_thread` (provider_registry.py). The commit body records the profile attribution (fundamentals_warm re-crawling fresh rows inline).

entries.title: Sidecar staleness gate ignores .json.gz, so regenerating the bundled Indian fundamentals seed does not rebuild the binary and assertFresh still passes: a local release ships the previous seed snapshot
entries.repro: node -e "console.log(/\.(py|txt|toml|cfg|ini|json|csv)$/i.test('india_fundamentals_seed.json.gz'))" -> false. Regenerate sidecar/services/screener_universes/india_fundamentals_seed.json.gz (regenerate_fundamentals_seed.py touches no .py) -> node scripts/ensure-all-sidecars.mjs -> '[ensure-sidecar] vysted-sidecar-<triple> present and fresh - skipping build.' -> node scripts/smoke-test-sidecars.mjs freshness gate also green -> the bundled binary carries the old seed.
entries.evidence: scripts/sidecar-staleness.mjs:41 (SOURCE_EXT regex, lead re-verified at HEAD), :62, :94, :108; scripts/ensure-sidecar.mjs:81-86 (fresh -> skip), :179-189 (--add-data bundles services/screener_universes wholesale); scripts/smoke-test-sidecars.mjs:886; sidecar/services/fundamentals_seed.py:37. entries.root_cause: 'What is build input' is encoded twice in different shapes - an --add-data path list in ensure-sidecar.mjs and a file-extension allow-list in sidecar-staleness.mjs - and they have drifted (\.json$ does not match .json.gz).

entries.title: A cut-off answer is shown as complete: the Anthropic adapter hard-caps every call at 4096 output tokens and no layer (oneshot, runtime, UI) acts on a max_tokens/length finish_reason, so a truncated deep-research synthesis renders as final
entries.repro: Deep-research synthesis or a long agent answer on Anthropic -> adapter sends max_tokens=4096 (no caller sets it) -> stream stops mid-sentence with stop_reason 'max_tokens' -> LLMDoneEvent.finish_reason='max_tokens' -> oneshot.complete returns the partial text; agent_runtime only inspects 'content_filter'; streaming.ts decodes finishReason with no consumer.

entries.root_cause: DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS=4096 is the only value ever sent; finish_reason is carried end to end but never acted on.
entries.fix_shape: Raise the Anthropic default to the model's documented output ceiling from the registry; have oneshot.complete and the runtime flag finish_reason in {'max_tokens','length'} as a visible 'answer truncated' note on the brief/message. entries.title: Command-palette action and panel rows never show their keyboard shortcut: about 0% carry one, against SC-009's >=90% (the only <kbd> is a literal 'Enter' on the Ask-agent row)

entries.title: FR-038's preference depth does not exist: no provider/model fallback order, no palette-behaviour options and no starter-cockpit composition. The settings were killed in R9 as theatre, and the behaviour behind them was never built
entries.repro: Open Settings: AI Providers offers a single default pick (llm-providers.ts:127-136) and no ordered fallback list. There is no palette section and no starter-cockpit picker (default-layout.ts is a constant). A failing default provider therefore never falls through to a second configured one.
entries.evidence: spec.md:909-914 (FR-038 MUST); SettingsPanel.tsx section list :410-1872; src/store/settings.ts:10-15,51-68,165-166 (providerPreferenceOrder, palette*, starterCockpitPanelIds, panelDefaults deliberately dropped); R9_DEFECT_CATALOGUE.md:40-44 ('resurrect only WITH a consuming picker'); layout autosave/restore partly covers starter composition (SettingsPanel.tsx:1630-1632,1704). Panel defaults are R15-UI-048. Refuter: admitted_with_correction, high to medium.
entries.root_cause: R9 removed the settings fields because nothing consumed them, correctly, but the consuming behaviour (a provider fallback chain, palette ranking/scoping options) was never built, so the MUST remains unmet.
entries.fix_shape: Build the behaviour first, then the control. An ordered provider list in llm-providers with a fallback in the chat send path on a classified provider failure (auth/quota/unreachable), plus a drag-to-reorder list over the existing provider rows. Also a 'start with' picker (last session vs a named layout) feeding the launch restore. Pin it with a store test where a first-provider failure routes to the second.
entries.closure_evidence: 4097dac merge(r15): stage C batch 11 - 18 certified fixes at 9985b00e
entries.note: Batch-11 (4097dac) certified: vitest: `orderedProviders` order. The fallback fires on a first-provider auth failure and the notice names both providers. It does not fire after answer text or on a content error. Start layout covers last session, a named layout, and a missing layout (keeps the session). Each palette option changes order or scope. The settings round-trip rejects garbled values. `PROVIDER_FAILURE_CODES` (auth, provider_402, insufficient_credit, network, ollama_not_running, provider_5xx) all exist in sidecar/services/errors.py; quota maps to insufficient_credit. The live free-lane run emitted `provider_5xx`, which is exactly the frame the fallback keys on. GUI feel (drag reorder, notice chip) is still unexercised in a real window.

entries.root_cause: Indicator builders are not parameterised (period/anchor fixed), and the only live preset source ignores timeframe; the timeframe-aware preset module was never wired.

Pin with a sidecar test: (equity,5m) -> ema:9,ema:21; (crypto,1d) -> ema:50,ema:200,vwap:week.

entries.title: run_custom_backtest advertises readOnlyHint=true on the external MCP surface while it writes to the in-process backtest result cache
entries.repro: External MCP client lists tools -> run_custom_backtest carries annotations.readOnlyHint=true -> client auto-approves it as a read -> the call persists a BacktestResult into the shared backtest_store. Declared safety hint is false.
entries.evidence: sidecar/services/agent_tools/catalog.py:905, sidecar/services/agent_tools/run_custom_backtest.py:116, sidecar/services/mcp_server.py:153, sidecar/services/agent_tools/catalog.py:14 || refuter corrections: COD-agent-tools-catalog-ledger-1: Mechanism is real: run_custom_backtest is catalogued read_only=True and the MCP projection maps that flag straight to readOnlyHint, while the handler calls backtest_store.put(result). But the 'write' is to a bounded 32-entry in-process LRU result cache (no persistence, no money, no order path), so the only side effect an auto-approving client can cause is evicting an older cached run id; that is a hint-accuracy polish issue, not a critical safety boundary.
entries.root_cause: One read_only flag conflates 'no order path' (§6.5 gate) with 'no side effects' (MCP hint); the write is a bounded 32-entry LRU, so impact is hint accuracy.
entries.fix_shape: Set read_only=False on the entry or split the flag into no_order_path and no_side_effects. Test: the MCP listing marks run_custom_backtest not read-only.
entries.note: triage@e032be7: still_reproduces, confidence 5, one catalog flag + a parity assertion; backtest is simulated, not trading, evidence docs/redesign/verification/r15/stage-c/lows-triage/LOWS_TRIAGE.json#R15-AGENT-066

entries.title: MCP projection is derived from tool kind alone plus one hand-listed exclusion, with no per-entry axis for session-scoped or account-scoped reads (it excludes backtest_summary but projects its writer run_custom_backtest)
entries.repro: design. The rule projects every read_handler except one hand-listed id, so broker_portfolio (real positions, equity, buying power), web_search and research (which spend the user's BYOK Exa/Perplexity credits) are on the external MCP surface purely by virtue of their kind.

entries.title: Nine agent-tool handlers each re-implement the validate/try/except/cap/envelope block, and one copy has already drifted: earnings_upcoming's int() parse is unguarded so a bad days arg returns a raw Python error instead of the range message
entries.repro: earnings_upcoming({'days':'seven'}) -> int('seven') raises ValueError out of the handler -> _dispatch_tool's generic catch returns "tool 'earnings_upcoming' raised: invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'seven'" instead of the tool's own "days must be in [1, 60]". Verified by executing the expression. || [COD-market-data-providers-2-10] design. The agent-tool error-envelope contract ({'ok': False, 'error': ...} + row cap + ProviderError-vs-Exception split) exists in nine copies; a change to how tool failures are surfaced to the model means nine edits.
entries.evidence: sidecar/services/agent_tools/earnings_tools.py:31, sidecar/services/agent_tools/earnings_tools.py:32, sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py:669, sidecar/services/agent_tools/macro_tools.py:71, sidecar/services/agent_tools/news_tool.py:36, sidecar/services/agent_tools/sec_tools.py:49, sidecar/services/agent_tools/analyst_tools.py:32-49, :52-69, :72-89; sidecar/services/agent_tools/earnings_tools.py:29-61, :64-81, :84-98; sidecar/services/agent_tools/sec_tools.py:34-74, :77-110, :113-152; plus sidecar/services/agent_tools/compare_symbols.py:69 and :84 and market_overview.py:90 writing 'except (ProviderError, Exception)' -- a tuple whose first member is unreachable || refuter corrections: COD-agent-tools-catalog-ledger-9: Real: earnings_tools.py:31 int() is unguarded, unlike its siblings. Scope is narrower than stated: the OpenAI-family adapter validates tool args against the catalog schema (days is type integer) and repairs or returns an invalid-args error before dispatch, so the escape only happens on the Anthropic/Gemini/Groq/Ollama lanes, and there the runtime catch-all still returns ok:false naming the bad literal, which the model can act on. Low. | COD-market-data-providers-2-10: Repetition confirmed across analyst_tools/earnings_tools/sec_tools, and 'except (ProviderError, Exception)' has a redundant first member at the cited lines. Corrected: in the nine data handlers the ProviderError/Exception split is NOT one blanket catch — the two branches emit different messages ('provider error' vs 'unexpected error'), which is deliberate; the redundant-tuple sites are the degrade-to-None paths in compare_symbols/market_overview. Short handlers, no present defect -> low.
entries.root_cause: Shallow per-tool copies of the error-envelope contract; drift is inevitable and has happened once.
entries.fix_shape: Extract register_data_tool(id, fetch, shape) covering the analyst/earnings/sec handlers with arg coercion + envelope in one place. Test: earnings_upcoming({'days':'seven'}) returns the range message.

entries.title: _resolve_model falls back to the agent's default model even when the provider was overridden, so a non-UI caller (workflow node, durable run) passing a provider without a model sends copilot's 'qwen2.5:7b' to e.g. Anthropic
entries.repro: PROVEN: get_agent('copilot').default_provider == 'ollama', default_model == 'qwen2.5:7b', and _planner_enabled('ollama','agent') is False -- the shipped default for the primary agent is the lane the runtime itself classifies as too unreliable for the visible planner (and MEMORY.md records qwen-7b tool-use as inconsistent). Separately, _resolve_model returns the literal 'gpt-4.1-mini' whenever model_registry.default_model_for(provider) is None, so a provider absent from the registry sends an OpenAI model id to (e.g.) Anthropic.
entries.evidence: sidecar/agents/copilot.json:59, sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py:90, sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py:110, sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py:536 || refuter corrections: COD-agent-runtime-14: Both stated mechanisms are mostly wrong: the UI deliberately ignores copilot's ollama pin (GENERIC_AGENT_IDS, documented as boilerplate) and always sends a provider+model from the user's selection store, and the 'gpt-4.1-mini' fallback is unreachable for any LLMProviderId because the registry covers the closed set. The real residual defect is adjacent: _resolve_model falls back to spec.default_model even when the provider was overridden, so a non-UI caller passing provider without model (workflow node config, durable run) sends copilot's 'qwen2.5:7b' to e.g. Anthropic.
entries.root_cause: Model fallback ignores whether the provider was overridden; the UI always sends both so only API/workflow callers hit it.
entries.fix_shape: When provider is overridden without a model, use model_registry.default_model_for(provider); raise a stated error if none. Test: invoke(provider='anthropic', model=None) resolves an Anthropic model.
entries.note: triage@e032be7: still_reproduces, confidence 5, pass the resolved provider into _resolve_model, evidence docs/redesign/verification/r15/stage-c/lows-triage/LOWS_TRIAGE.json#R15-AGENT-073

entries.title: The Delegate spend ceiling is priced against the requested provider string, so a run launched without a provider (and every resume) is metered at the $5/M default
entries.repro: Launch without `provider` on an agent whose default is anthropic/claude-opus (registry 30 $/M) -> guard prices at 5 $/M, so a $1 ceiling admits ~$6 of estimated spend; on ollama (0 $/M) it bills phantom dollars and can abort a free run. Scratch proof P5 shows spend_usd=0.5 for 100k tokens with provider ''.
entries.evidence: sidecar/services/run_manager.py:116 (`provider_str = str(provider or '')`), :136, sidecar/services/budget_guard.py:68-79 (unknown provider -> DEFAULT_RATE_PER_M), sidecar/config/model_registry.json:77-80,104 (default 5.0; opus 30.0; ollama 0.0), sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py:1467 (callback receives resolved_model but not the resolved provider), sidecar/services/run_manager.py:406-407 (resume always passes provider=None) || refuter corrections: COD-runs-durable-delegate-11: Mechanism confirmed: the guard is priced with str(provider or '') and an empty provider falls to the 5 $/M default, and the callback receives the resolved model but not the resolved provider. Severity medium->low: the UI always sends a resolved provider (providerOverride ?? agent preference ?? defaultProviderId), there is no MCP launch tool, and resume is unreachable from the UI, so only raw-HTTP launches that omit provider are mispriced.
entries.root_cause: on_round_usage receives the resolved model but not the resolved provider.
entries.fix_shape: Pass provider_id through on_round_usage and price with it. Test: an omitted-provider run on an opus default prices at the opus rate.
entries.note: Batch-7 (e81c9e7) certified: A launch that omits the provider (Ollama default) with `llama3.1:8b` prices 7,234 tokens at `spend_usd: 0.0`; before the fix the $5/M default would give $0.036.

entries.title: With openrouter/auto the adapter never reads which model actually answered, so the UI keeps showing 'openrouter/auto' and cost is priced at the provider-wide rate
entries.repro: Pick OpenRouter + 'openrouter/auto' in the HUD (it is in the curated list) and ask a valuation question -> OpenRouter routes to a model of its choosing; the stream's chunk.model names it, but the adapter reads only choices/usage, LLMDoneEvent has no model field, and the UI keeps showing 'openrouter/auto'. The BudgetGuard/spend estimate prices the round against the literal 'openrouter/auto' string.
entries.evidence: sidecar/config/model_registry.json:71 and src/store/model-selection.ts:59, src/store/llm-providers.ts:110 (openrouter/auto curated); sidecar/services/llm/openai.py:750-830 (stream loop never reads chunk.model), :830 (LLMDoneEvent(usage, finish_reason) only); sidecar/models/llm.py:213-217 (done event: usage + finish_reason, no served model); sidecar/services/budget_guard.py:60-78 (price by requested model substring -> DEFAULT_RATE_PER_M); census/world/harness-context.md CHECKLIST 20 (S20: 'The response includes the model field showing which model was actually used') || refuter corrections: WLD-harness-context-6: The served-model gap holds. openrouter/auto is in all three curated lists, openai.py's stream loop reads only choices and usage (never chunk.model), and LLMDoneEvent has no model field, so the UI cannot show what actually answered. Corrected: pricing is not the $5/M default. price_per_million('openrouter','openrouter/auto') returns $2.0/M from the provider-wide ('openrouter','') PRICE_TABLE key, so the cost is a mis-estimate either way, not a 2.5x inflation. Lowered to low: this is a disclosure/estimate gap on one opt-in curated slug, not a data defect.
entries.root_cause: The stream loop reads only choices/usage and LLMDoneEvent has no model field.
entries.fix_shape: Capture chunk.model, add optional served_model to LLMDoneEvent (+ types mirror), show it when it differs and price with it. Test: a stub returning model 'x/y' surfaces served_model.

entries.title: Ollama silently retries a round without tools on a client-side tools-construction error, with no log or event
entries.repro: Ollama daemon returns a transient 500 (or any error) on the tools-enabled chat call -> adapter swallows the exception with no log, reopens the stream WITHOUT tools, and the model answers from training data instead of calling get_quote; the stream looks completely normal to the user
entries.evidence: sidecar/services/llm/ollama.py:139-149, sidecar/services/llm/ollama.py:150-169 || refuter corrections: COD-llm-adapters-2: The repro mechanism is wrong: ollama.AsyncClient.chat(stream=True) returns a lazy async generator and makes no HTTP request at await time, so a 500/connection error/'model does not support tools' surfaces during iteration and is humanized into an LLMErrorEvent (ollama.py:228-237), never a silent tool-less retry. The bare `except Exception: stream = None` (no log) only catches client-side construction errors (e.g. a Tool.model_validate failure on a malformed schema); a TypeError from an unknown kwarg recurs on the retry and surfaces as an error. Residual: a swallowed, unlogged exception, and the retry-without-tools fallback is effectively dead for its documented purpose. high -> low.
entries.root_cause: A bare except Exception: stream = None around the tools-enabled call; network/HTTP errors surface later during iteration, so only construction errors are swallowed.
entries.fix_shape: Narrow the except to the specific validation error and log + emit a notice when tools are dropped. Test: a Tool.model_validate failure logs and yields a notice.

entries.title: Walk-forward slices share their boundary date, so each boundary bar is traded in two slices while the UI strip presents them as disjoint periods
entries.repro: [COD-backtest-11] sidecar/.venv/bin/python -c 'from services.backtest_engine import _slice_dates; print(_slice_dates("2024-01-01","2024-01-11",2))' -> [('2024-01-01','2024-01-06'), ('2024-01-06','2024-01-11')]. The slice filter is `slice_start <= b.timestamp <= slice_end`, so every bar dated 2024-01-06 is replayed in both slices; with 10 slices, nine bars are double-counted across the strip.

entries.root_cause: _slice_dates returns contiguous boundaries and the slice filter is inclusive on both ends.
entries.fix_shape: Half-open filter (slice_start <= ts < slice_end, inclusive only on the last slice); pin with a test that each bar lands in exactly one slice.

entries.title: Chat SSE consumer relabels consumer exceptions as 'unparseable SSE frame', and a stream that ends without a done/error frame leaves the message streaming, the run 'running' and the brief in_flight forever
entries.repro: [COD-error-layer-11] design: handlers.onEvent(event) is inside the same try as JSON.parse (streaming.ts:263-271). A throw in ChatSidebar's onToolUse/enqueueChange or in feedBriefLifecycle (called from normalizeEvent) is caught, relabelled `unparseable SSE frame: <consumer message>`, routed to onError -> the assistant message is failed and the run ended as 'error' while the stream keeps delivering frames to a settled message. SECOND HALF (design): consumeSseStream returns normally when reader.read() reports done (streaming.ts:225-244) whether or not a terminal frame was seen; ChatSidebar settles a turn ONLY in onDone/onError (ChatSidebar.tsx:890-939) and does nothing after `await streamAgentInvocation(...)` (:1005-1038). Any server path that closes the generator without `done` leaves the message 'streaming', the rail run 'running', abortRef held and the brief panel in_flight, forever.
entries.evidence: [COD-error-layer-11] src/modules/chat/streaming.ts:263-271, src/modules/chat/streaming.ts:302-305 (store side effect inside normalizeEvent), src/modules/chat/ChatSidebar.tsx:890-912, src/modules/chat/streaming.ts:225-249 (no sawTerminal tracking), src/modules/chat/ChatSidebar.tsx:914-939,1005-1038, src/modules/chat/streaming.test.ts (10 tests; none for non-ok, malformed frame, consumer throw, or EOF-without-done) -- refuter admitted (low->low): Holds on both halves: dispatchFrame wraps JSON.parse, normalizeEvent (which calls feedBriefLifecycle) and handlers.onEvent in one try and relabels any throw 'unparseable SSE frame: …'; consumeSseStream returns normally on reader done without tracking a terminal frame, and ChatSidebar settles only in onDone/onError with nothing after the await.
entries.root_cause: dispatchFrame wraps JSON.parse, normalizeEvent (which mutates the brief store) and handlers.onEvent in one try; consumeSseStream does not track a terminal frame and ChatSidebar settles only in onDone/onError.
entries.fix_shape: try only around JSON.parse/normalizeEvent, call onEvent outside it, move feedBriefLifecycle out of normalizeEvent; track sawTerminal and call onError('The stream ended before the answer finished.') after the read loop if false. Pin with streaming.test.ts cases for consumer throw and EOF-without-done.

entries.title: LLMProvider.stream_chat is declared 'async def -> AsyncIterator' (a coroutine) while all five adapters and all three callers treat it as an async generator
entries.repro: [INT-deferred-0-4] sidecar/services/llm/base.py:83-90 declares '@abstractmethod async def stream_chat(...) -> AsyncIterator[LLMStreamEvent]'. Every concrete adapter (anthropic.py:103, gemini.py:99, groq.py:101, ollama.py:126, openai.py:656) is an async-generator function (contains 'yield' directly in its async def body). The only call site, sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py:1434, does 'async for event in adapter.stream_chat(...)' with no 'await' before it -- correct for an async generator, but inconsistent with what the ABC's 'async def' signature would imply (call, then await the coroutine to get the iterator).
entries.evidence: [INT-deferred-0-4] sidecar/services/llm/base.py:83-90, sidecar/services/llm/anthropic.py:103, sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py:1434 -- refuter admitted_with_correction (medium->low): The mismatch is real: base.py:85-108 is an abstract 'async def' whose body is just 'raise NotImplementedError' (no yield), so it declares a coroutine, while all five adapters are async generators. Two corrections. There are three call sites, not one: agent_runtime.py:1434, native_search.py:242 and oneshot.py:79, and all of them iterate without await. Severity also drops to low, because no type checker runs anywhere (no mypy/pyright config or CI step), so nothing enforces the ABC. Nothing changes at runtime; this is a one-word annotation fix.

entries.title: Boot path bridges a plugin's panels and commands without checking that loadPlugin succeeded, so an errored plugin still contributes UI
entries.repro: [COD-plugins-5] Make any bundled plugin's initialize() throw (or drift its manifest version from its instance version, which checkCompatibility rejects) -> restart. The Plugin Manager renders the row red 'error' while its panels and slash commands are live in cmd+K.
entries.evidence: [COD-plugins-5] src/lib/plugin-bootstrap.ts:264-270 (`await runtime.loadPlugin(plugin)` return value discarded, then appendModules unconditionally), vs the three guarded siblings src/store/marketplace.ts:147, :165, :241 (`if (snap.state === 'active')`), src/lib/plugin-runtime.ts:356-365 (documents the FR-054/SC-015 'contributes nothing' promise), src/lib/plugin-runtime.test.ts:516 ('an incompatible plugin contributes nothing' -- asserted at the runtime level only) -- refuter admitted_with_correction (medium->low): Core claim holds: the boot loop discards loadPlugin's snapshot and appendModules unconditionally (modules default enabled), unlike the three guarded store paths. Mechanism corrected: the cited hardcoded versions at marketplace.ts:91/125/140 are MarketplaceEntry.version, which checkCompatibility never reads, and manifest/instance version drift for bundled rows is CI-guarded by marketplace.test.ts:44; the reachable first-party path is a transient persistence.load failure at boot (config-load error) or an initialize() throw. Severity medium->low: plugins are compiled in, and after broker removal only vysted-example contributes commands and none contribute panels.
entries.root_cause: The boot loop discards loadPlugin's snapshot, unlike the three guarded store paths.
entries.fix_shape: const snap = await runtime.loadPlugin(plugin); bridge only if snap.state === 'active'; pin with a bootstrap test where initialize() throws.

entries.title: moduleForPlugin re-implements capability negotiation without the runtime's try/catch, so a throwing getPanels()/getCommands() rejects bootstrapPlugins() mid-loop
entries.repro: [COD-plugins-6] A plugin whose getPanels() or getCommands() throws: runtime.collectPanels() contains it and emits `errored`, but moduleForPlugin lets it propagate -> the unguarded call at plugin-bootstrap.ts:266 rejects bootstrapPlugins() and the plugin layer never finishes booting. Same throw also breaks bridge/unbridge on disable.
entries.evidence: [COD-plugins-6] src/lib/plugin-bootstrap.ts:135-138 (flag -> optional getter, no try/catch) vs src/lib/plugin-runtime.ts:389-416 (callIfFlagged: flag check + getter-exists check + `errored` emit + try/catch), unguarded callers at src/lib/plugin-bootstrap.ts:183, :198, :266 -- refuter admitted_with_correction (medium->low): Real duplication: moduleForPlugin calls getPanels/getCommands with no try/catch or missing-getter errored event, while callIfFlagged has both; a throw at plugin-bootstrap.ts:266 would reject bootstrapPlugins mid-loop (page.tsx only .then()s it). Severity medium->low: every plugin is compiled in, and post-trading-removal the only panel/command contributor is plugins/example with a static getCommands array, so the throw path is latent.
entries.root_cause: The flag->getter rule is written twice; the copy lacks callIfFlagged's guard and errored event.
entries.fix_shape: Source panels/commands from runtime.collectPanels()/collectCommands() filtered by plugin id (or export callIfFlagged); collapse the five collect* bodies to one collect<T>. Pin with a throwing-getter test.

entries.title: Removing a credentialed non-broker plugin (e.g. vysted-news) never deletes its plugin-secret keychain entry, and the legacy vysted-search-exa secret has no cleanup
entries.repro: [INT-deferred-84-5] install a search-tier backend with a key (e.g. Exa) -> disable or remove it -> plugin-secret:<id> keychain entry is never deleted, only manual Keychain Access cleanup removes it
entries.evidence: [INT-deferred-84-5] src/store/marketplace.ts:175-204 -- refuter admitted_with_correction (medium->low): The mechanism is real, but the subject and scope are wrong. No 'search-tier plugin' exists: the Exa/R7-R8 search lanes are dead (search-headers.ts:27-30) and the marketplace catalog has no search entry. entries.title: The 'atomic, crash-safe' note/export write never fsyncs (File::flush is a no-op), so the SC-032 survives-a-crash claim does not hold for the .md mirror
entries.repro: [COD-rust-core-7] design — write_text_atomic does File::create -> write_all -> flush() -> rename with no sync_all on the file or the parent directory; on power loss the renamed file can appear with zero or partial content.
entries.evidence: [COD-rust-core-7] src-tauri/src/lib.rs:303-309 (text) and :336-341 (bytes): `f.write_all(...)`, `f.flush()`, then `std::fs::rename`; std::fs::File's Write::flush is a documented no-op (File is unbuffered — it never fsyncs); doc comment src-tauri/src/lib.rs:281-286 claims 'the kernel rename(2) is atomic (SC-032: survives a crash mid-save)' -- refuter admitted_with_correction (medium->low): Real: both commands do File::create -> write_all -> flush -> rename with no sync_all on the file or directory (lib.rs:303-309, :336-341); File::flush does not fsync, so the SC-032 'survives a crash' comment (lib.rs:281-286) overclaims. Downgraded: the .md file is a mirror, not the note's primary store - notes-persistence.ts documents the workspace blob as 'the primary durable store' and the .md write as non-fatal (notes-persistence.ts:52,72-76), so a power-loss truncation of the mirror does not lose the note.
entries.root_cause: rename(2) is atomic for the directory entry, not the data; no sync_all on file or parent.
entries.fix_shape: f.sync_all()? before rename and (unix) sync the parent dir after, in the single write_atomic helper.
entries.note: triage@e032be7: still_reproduces, confidence 5, f.sync_all()? before rename plus a parent-dir sync on unix, in the shared helper 055 introduces, evidence docs/redesign/verification/r15/stage-c/lows-triage/evidence/R15-CODE-PLATFORM-054/

entries.title: Dev keychain migration swallows a failed read and still sets migrated=true, so that secret is never retried and the report says success
entries.repro: [COD-rust-core-11] Dev build, first boot, one account's keychain read errors on both passes (denied dialog / locked keychain) -> that secret is never copied, `migrated: true` is written, and the keychain is never read again by design. The report says already_done on every later boot.
entries.evidence: [COD-rust-core-11] src-tauri/src/keychain.rs:286-292 (pass 2: `resolved.insert(account.clone(), read(account).unwrap_or(None))` — the error is discarded); src-tauri/src/keychain.rs:197 (`store.migrated = true` runs unconditionally after the loop); src-tauri/src/keychain.rs:180-186 and :258-264 (both guards then short-circuit forever); src-tauri/src/keychain.rs:50-58 (MigrateReport has backend/migrated/already_done — no failed list, no error count); src-tauri/src/keychain.rs:189-190 (the comment acknowledges the skip: 'the user re-adds it via Settings' — but nothing tells the user WHICH) -- refuter admitted_with_correction (medium->low): The logic defect is real: pass 2 converts a read error to None (keychain.rs:287-289), migrate_at then sets migrated=true unconditionally (keychain.rs:197-198), both guards short-circuit forever after (keychain.rs:180-186, :258-264), and MigrateReport has no failed list (keychain.rs:49-58). Corrected: the whole path is cfg(debug_assertions) (keychain.rs:92, :353-361) - no shipped user runs it - and nothing is 'forfeited': the secret stays in the OS keychain and the frontend treats migration as best-effort with Settings re-entry as the fallback (src/lib/keychain.ts:141-151). Dev-only edge: low.
entries.root_cause: Pass 2 converts a read error to None and the flag is set unconditionally; MigrateReport has no failed list. Debug-only path.
entries.fix_shape: Set migrated only when no read errored, or add failed: Vec<String> to MigrateReport and leave the flag unset; pin with a Rust unit test using an erroring reader.

entries.title: All three Rust child-kill closures hold the MutexGuard through the whole if-let body instead of releasing it after .take()
entries.repro: [INT-deferred-0-6] src-tauri/src/lib.rs:510 (main sidecar exit handler), src-tauri/src/openbb_mcp.rs:188, src-tauri/src/sec_edgar_mcp.rs:185 each still write 'if let Some(child) = state.0.lock().unwrap().take() { let _ = child.kill(); }' -- the MutexGuard temporary from '.lock().unwrap()' lives for the whole if-let block (the clippy::significant_drop_in_scrutinee shape), not just for the .take() call.
entries.evidence: [INT-deferred-0-6] src-tauri/src/lib.rs:508-513, src-tauri/src/openbb_mcp.rs:186-192, src-tauri/src/sec_edgar_mcp.rs:183-189 -- refuter admitted_with_correction (medium->low): The pattern is present at all three sites (lib.rs:510, openbb_mcp.rs:188, sec_edgar_mcp.rs:185), and on edition 2021 (Cargo.toml:6) the guard does live through the if-let body. The claimed consequence does not hold, though. Each of these mutexes is locked in exactly one place, the kill path itself; grep finds no other lock() on SidecarProcess, OpenbbMcpProcess or SecEdgarMcpProcess. So no concurrent locker can be blocked. child.kill() only sends a signal and never re-enters the mutex, so there is no deadlock either. significant_drop_in_scrutinee is a nursery lint that clippy -D warnings does not enable. This is lint hygiene with zero behavioural effect: lowered from medium to low.
entries.root_cause: Edition-2021 temporary lifetime in an if-let scrutinee; no behavioural effect today (each mutex locked only here).
entries.fix_shape: let child = state.0.lock().unwrap().take(); if let Some(child) = child { ... } at the three sites.
entries.note: triage@e032be7: still_reproduces, confidence 5, three-line mechanical change, evidence docs/redesign/verification/r15/stage-c/lows-triage/evidence/R15-CODE-PLATFORM-059/

entries.evidence: [COD-scripts-build-9] scripts/sidecar-staleness.mjs:63 (const m = statSync(full).mtimeMs — bare), vs :51-55 (readdirSync guarded, 'unreadable / missing dir contributes nothing') and :79-85 (the extraFiles stat guarded, 'missing extra file contributes nothing'), consumed at scripts/ensure-sidecar.mjs:81 -- refuter admitted_with_correction (low->low): The statSync at :63 is unguarded while :51-55 and :79-85 are guarded, which is real. The headline repro is wrong: readdirSync(withFileTypes) returns a symlink Dirent whose isFile() is false, so a dangling symlink is skipped and nothing crashes (verified). All that remains is a TOCTOU window where a SOURCE_EXT file outside IGNORE_DIRS is deleted between readdir and stat, which is rare because the cache dirs are already pruned. Side note: symlinked real sources are ignored for staleness for the same reason.
entries.root_cause: The hot-path stat lacks the try/catch applied six lines away; dangling symlinks are skipped (refuter), leaving only a TOCTOU window.
entries.fix_shape: Wrap the stat at :63-65 in the same 'contributes nothing' try/catch; covered by the staleness test file.
entries.note: triage@e032be7: still_reproduces, confidence 4, one-line guard, evidence docs/redesign/verification/r15/stage-c/lows-triage/evidence/R15-CODE-PLATFORM-061/

entries.title: The BSE probe in smoke-test-sidecars has an unreachable catch, and _httpGetOk's blanket swallow discards the 404-vs-offline distinction the probe exists to report
entries.repro: [COD-scripts-build-11] design — _httpGetOk has `catch { return false }` over the whole fetch, so the try/catch wrapping `await _httpGetOk(url, 4000)` can never enter its handler.
entries.evidence: [COD-scripts-build-11] scripts/smoke-test-sidecars.mjs:382-398 (try { const ok = await _httpGetOk(url, 4000) ... } catch (err) { console.warn('probe errored') }), scripts/smoke-test-sidecars.mjs:334-345 (_httpGetOk: catch { return false }) -- refuter admitted (low->low): Confirmed. _httpGetOk wraps the fetch in try/catch returning false and clears its timer in finally, so the awaited promise cannot reject and the catch at :393-398 is dead. The status/error distinction the probe's own comment asks for is thrown away at :341.
entries.root_cause: _httpGetOk returns false on any failure.
entries.fix_shape: _httpGetOk returns {ok, status, error}; the warning names the actual outcome; delete the dead catch.
entries.note: triage@e032be7: still_reproduces, confidence 5, script-local change, evidence docs/redesign/verification/r15/stage-c/lows-triage/evidence/R15-CODE-PLATFORM-062/

entries.title: Screenshot generator scripts depend on an undeclared Pillow and silently collapse all three font sizes into load_default() on macOS/Linux
entries.repro: [COD-scripts-build-13] sidecar/.venv/bin/python scripts/render_phase_6_e_screenshots.py -> ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'PIL' (Pillow is in none of the four requirements files). With Pillow installed on macOS/Linux: load_font tries only the two C:/Windows/Fonts paths, both raise OSError, and returns ImageFont.load_default(), which ignores `size` — so fnt_small/fnt_med/fnt_lg are the same bitmap font and the 1920x1080 / 2560x1440 'pair' is one render at two canvas sizes.
entries.evidence: [COD-scripts-build-13] scripts/render_phase_6_e_screenshots.py:20 (from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont), :37-48 (load_font: candidates = ["C:/Windows/Fonts/consola.ttf", "C:/Windows/Fonts/cour.ttf"]; except OSError: continue; return ImageFont.load_default()), :55-57 (three distinct sizes requested), scripts/render_phase_6_sc_screenshots.py:39-47 and :88-96 (same pattern), sidecar/requirements.txt + sidecar/requirements-dev.txt + sidecar/openbb_mcp_subprocess/requirements.txt + sidecar/sec_edgar_mcp_subprocess/requirements.txt (grep -i pillow: no hits) -- refuter admitted (low->low): Confirmed. Pillow is in none of the four requirements files and the sidecar venv has no PIL. load_font tries only two C:/Windows/Fonts paths, then falls back to ImageFont.load_default() with no size argument, so every requested size collapses to one default font on macOS/Linux. These are dead v0.6.0-era scripts, and deleting them under COD-scripts-build-5 closes this too.
entries.root_cause: Windows-only font paths with a swallowed OSError fallback.
entries.fix_shape: Delete both dead v0.6.0-era scripts and their mock PNGs; if kept, declare Pillow and raise when no truetype font resolves.
entries.note: triage@e032be7: still_reproduces, confidence 5, dead v0.6.0 tooling; deletion is the fix, evidence docs/redesign/verification/r15/stage-c/lows-triage/evidence/R15-CODE-PLATFORM-064/

entries.title: POST /workflow/run swallows spec-validation errors: the SSE stream closes with zero frames and the editor shows a guessed cause instead of the real reason
entries.repro: [COD-workflow-engine-4] Run a spec containing an unregistered node type (e.g. a plugin-contributed node) or a dangling edge -> _validate_spec raises before run-start (proof: 'events emitted: []') -> routers/workflow.py:55-58 logs and ends the stream -> the editor shows its generic 'stream ended without a terminal frame … e.g. a node type with no server-side handler' guess.
entries.evidence: [COD-workflow-engine-4] sidecar/routers/workflow.py:50-60 (comment at :57 'The engine emits run-error on validation failures already' is false); sidecar/services/workflow_engine.py:191 (_validate_spec before any _emit); siblings that do it right: sidecar/routers/llm.py:144-145 and sidecar/routers/agents.py:109-110 (yield an error frame), sidecar/services/mcp_server.py:282-285 (returns the WorkflowEngineError text); workarounds: src/modules/node-editor/NodeEditorPanel.tsx:374-379,435-441 and src/modules/node-editor/code-node-run.ts:76-90 (client re-implements cycle detection because of this) -- refuter admitted_with_correction (medium->low): Mechanism is real: _validate_spec raises before run-start, the router's except only logs, and the comment at routers/workflow.py:57 is false (zero events emitted). Downgraded because the failure is not silent: NodeEditorPanel already turns a no-terminal-frame stream into a run error with a likely-cause message and pre-empts cycles client-side, and the MCP run_workflow path returns the exact WorkflowEngineError text; what is lost is only the precise reason string in the editor.
entries.root_cause: _validate_spec raises before run-start and the router only logs (its comment claims the engine emits run-error).
entries.fix_shape: On WorkflowEngineError yield a run-error event carrying str(exc); delete the client-side 'no terminal frame' guesswork and duplicated Kahn cycle check; pin with a router test asserting a run-error frame for a dangling edge.
entries.note: triage@e032be7: still_reproduces, confidence 5, except WorkflowEngineError: yield run-error(str(exc)); client guess text can then go, evidence docs/redesign/verification/r15/stage-c/lows-triage/evidence/R15-CODE-PLATFORM-065/

entries.title: The server code node admits unbounded ** and list * and evaluates synchronously on the event loop (7**10**7 blocked the sidecar 8.2 s), reachable via MCP run_workflow
entries.repro: [COD-workflow-engine-7] evaluate_code({}, {'expression': '7**(10**7)'}) took 8.226 s on the event loop (7**10**6: 0.2 s; growth is super-linear, 7**10**8 is minutes). '[0]*10**9' is also admitted (ast.List + BinOp Mult). Reachable by an agent through MCP run_workflow/save_workflow.
entries.evidence: [COD-workflow-engine-7] sidecar/services/workflow_nodes/code_node.py:5-6 ('Safe by construction'), :20-27 (ast.Pow, ast.Mult unbounded), :62-63, :84-85, :89-100 (sync evaluation inside an async handler, no to_thread, no size guard) -- refuter admitted_with_correction (medium->low): Real: ast.Pow and ast.Mult are unbounded and evaluation runs synchronously inside the async handler on the event loop (7**10**6 took 0.21 s here; larger exponents grow super-linearly). Downgraded: it needs a pathological expression authored by the local user or their own agent in a single-user local app, and the node editor evaluates code nodes client-side, so only the MCP/agent path reaches it - not something hit in normal use.
entries.root_cause: 'Safe by construction' covers code execution, not CPU/memory exhaustion.
entries.fix_shape: Bound Pow exponents, reject Mult on list/str operands, evaluate via asyncio.to_thread with a timeout; pin with a test that 7**(10**7) is rejected fast.
entries.note: triage@e032be7: still_reproduces, confidence 5, exponent/size guard in _eval plus to_thread wrapper, evidence docs/redesign/verification/r15/stage-c/lows-triage/evidence/R15-CODE-PLATFORM-066/

entries.title: Atomic-rename writers have no Windows sharing-violation retry: a Defender/indexer handle on the workspace file turns autosave into an unhandled 500, and the Rust note/export writers leak '<name>.tmp.<pid>' when the rename fails
entries.repro: [HYG-7] On Windows, os.replace / std::fs::rename (MoveFileExW REPLACE_EXISTING) fails with WinError 5/32 while the destination is open without FILE_SHARE_DELETE (AV scan, indexer, concurrent read) -> POST /workspace returns 500 (routers/workspace.py:53-60 catches only WorkspaceNameError), losing that autosave; write_text_atomic/write_bytes_atomic reject and leave the temp file
entries.evidence: [HYG-7] sidecar/services/workspace_store.py:85-94 (os.replace, no retry; the tmp is cleaned in finally), sidecar/routers/workspace.py:53-60 (catches only WorkspaceNameError), src-tauri/src/lib.rs:297-309 and :328-341 (std::fs::rename, no retry, no tmp cleanup on error) -- refuter admitted (low->low): save_workspace calls os.replace once with no retry (it does clean its temp in finally), and the POST route catches only WorkspaceNameError, so a Windows PermissionError from a concurrent reader or scanner becomes a 500. Both Rust atomic writers rename once and return early on error with no temp cleanup, which leaks '<name>.tmp.<pid>'. Rare but real on Windows. Re-checked 23 Sep: sidecar/services/workspace_store.py:85-94 single os.replace (temp cleaned in finally); src-tauri/src/lib.rs:341 bare std::fs::rename(&tmp_path, dest). Related, distinct: R15-CODE-PLATFORM-055 (the two Rust writers are duplicated), R15-CODE-PLATFORM-054 (no fsync).
entries.root_cause: Single-shot rename with no retry on transient Windows sharing violations; Rust writers return early on rename error without removing the temp.
entries.fix_shape: Retry the replace 3-5x with ~50 ms backoff on PermissionError / ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION in save_workspace and in one shared Rust atomic-write helper, removing the temp on final failure; map a final failure to a typed 503 not a bare 500. Pytest monkeypatching os.replace to raise PermissionError twice then succeed.
entries.note: triage@e032be7: still_reproduces, confidence 4, 3-5 retries with ~50 ms backoff in save_workspace; one shared Rust atomic-write helper that removes the temp on rename error, evidence docs/redesign/verification/r15/stage-c/lows-triage/evidence/R15-CROSS-PLATFORM-007/

entries.title: MCP supervisors mutate the process environment (std::env::set_var/remove_var) from two parallel setup threads while GTK/WebKit and runtime threads may call libc getenv, which is undefined behaviour on POSIX
entries.repro: [HYG-8] design: lib.rs:470-485 spawns openbb_mcp::spawn and sec_edgar_mcp::spawn in parallel; each calls set_var/remove_var (openbb_mcp.rs:59-60,95-96; sec_edgar_mcp.rs:58-59,95-96) on edition 2021 where it is not unsafe; a concurrent non-std getenv (glibc, GTK/WebKitGTK) can read a reallocating environ -> rare boot crash on Linux/macOS; Windows unaffected
entries.evidence: [HYG-8] src-tauri/src/lib.rs:470-485 (parallel threads), src-tauri/src/openbb_mcp.rs:58-60,95-96, src-tauri/src/sec_edgar_mcp.rs:57-59,95-96, src-tauri/Cargo.toml:6 (edition = "2021") -- refuter admitted_with_correction (low->low): The global env mutation is real: openbb_mcp.rs and sec_edgar_mcp.rs call set_var/remove_var from two threads spawned in parallel during setup, on edition 2021 where the call is not unsafe. Correction: the two MCP threads racing each other is not the hazard, because std's env functions are synchronised with each other. The Rust docs say the hazard is concurrent reads through non-std getenv (glibc, GTK/WebKit, libc internals). That narrows the risk to C-level readers running at setup time on Linux/macOS; Windows is safe. The fix shape (pass the ports with .env(...) on the sidecar Command) stands. Re-checked 23 Sep: set_var/remove_var at the cited lines.
entries.root_cause: Global env is used as the channel to hand MCP ports to the main sidecar spawned afterwards.
entries.fix_shape: Drop the env mutation; pass VYSTED_*_MCP_PORT/HOST via .env(...) on the main sidecar Command in start_main_sidecar, reading ports from the managed OpenbbMcpPort/SecEdgarMcpPort state (0 -> omit). Pin with a grep test (no std::env::set_var/remove_var under src-tauri/src) and a unit test that the sidecar command env carries the ports.
entries.note: Verifier batch-8: confirmed live in the batch-8 boot-order change -- openbb_mcp::start/sec_edgar_mcp::start now call std::env::set_var while the main event loop is live (previously the main thread was blocked in join). setenv/getenv are not thread-safe on macOS; low-probability but present since the LIFECYCLE-001 boot-order fix. || triage@e032be7: still_reproduces, confidence 5, changes the port hand-off channel in the Rust boot path; needs a cargo build the triage lanes cannot run, evidence docs/redesign/verification/r15/stage-c/lows-triage/evidence/R15-CROSS-PLATFORM-008/

The 140 s blocking itself is R15-CODE-PLATFORM-057; this entry owns the Linux no-provider path and non-secret flags in the secret store.
entries.root_cause: Linux has only the sync-secret-service backend and os_keychain passes non-NoEntry errors through; app-meta flags (onboarding, ToS timestamps) are stored as keychain items.
entries.fix_shape: Move non-secret app-meta flags out of the keychain into the workspace blob or a data-dir file; cfg-gate the migrate wait to target_os="macos"; surface a typed 'secret store unavailable' state in KeyEntryDialog instead of a raw invoke rejection. entries.title: Keyless-search SERP parsers (DDG, Brave, Mojeek) are tested only against inline fixtures and nothing detects live markup drift; a drifted parser returns an empty SUCCESS that records breaker success and reads 'no results', so the fallback tier dies silently exactly when DDG is throttled
entries.repro: design: sidecar/tests/test_brave_backend.py / test_mojeek_backend.py assert against inline HTML fixtures only; no scheduled workflow re-fetches a live query (.github/workflows has build.yml, lint.yml, test.yml, no schedule). If Brave's markup changes, brave.parse yields 0 rows -> keyless.py:162-176 calls breaker.record_success(), notes 'no results' and rotates; tier_status stays healthy and the engine is never benched.
entries.evidence: sidecar/services/search/keyless.py:53 (ENGINE_CHAIN = ddg, brave, mojeek), sidecar/services/search/keyless.py:162-176 (record_success before/regardless of a zero-row parse; 'no results' note), sidecar/tests/test_brave_backend.py:19,67 (inline fixture), sidecar/services/search/brave.py:8-13 (layered selectors degrade fields before rows); docs/redesign/verification/R7_RUN_REPORT.md:41. refuter (INT-deferred-42-9, admitted_with_correction, severity_final low): drift does not by itself zero the default tier (DDG primary, zero-row parse rotates), but the empty-success accounting hides it; the same fixture-only gap applies to the DDG parser. Related, same accounting seam but a different trigger (CAPTCHA page): R15-RESEARCH-022.
entries.root_cause: Parser correctness is pinned only by frozen fixtures, and keyless.py treats a 200 that parses to zero rows as a healthy engine (record_success + 'no results'), so markup drift is indistinguishable from an empty query.
entries.fix_shape: Treat a zero-row parse of a non-empty 200 page on a known-good canary query as a parse failure (record_failure, note 'parser drift') and expose it in tier_status; add an opt-in live smoke script (scripts/, run manually or by a non-CI cron — no CI workflow change) that runs one fixed query through each of ddg/brave/mojeek and fails on zero rows or missing url/title. Pin the accounting with a unit test feeding a drifted-markup page and asserting the breaker counts a failure.
entries.note: triage@e032be7: still_reproduces, confidence 4, Residual is the empty-success accounting + fixture-only pinning; the CAPTCHA half is closed by R15-RESEARCH-022., evidence docs/redesign/verification/r15/stage-c/lows-triage/LOWS_TRIAGE.json#R15-DATA-111
