entries.title: No timeout or AbortSignal anywhere in the shared sidecar client: one hung /health probe holds the shared readyPromise past its 120 s budget, a hung route is an eternal spinner, and the boot-time plugin path fetches every plugin's config twice, serially, with no ceiling
entries.repro: Design: resolveAndAwaitReady awaits fetch('/health') with no signal and checks the deadline only after it settles; sidecarGet/sidecarPost take no signal. Point the host at a socket that accepts but never answers -> bootstrapPlugins never resolves (the plugin layer stalls; app startup does not, since bootstrap is fire-and-forget). installed+enabled plugins get persistence.load twice (bootstrap then loadPlugin), serially.
entries.evidence: src/lib/sidecar-client.ts:125-144,154-158,194-196,226-234, src/lib/plugin-bootstrap.ts:90-97,252-271, src/lib/plugin-runtime.ts:218-232; contrast plugins/openbb-mcp/index.ts:90-92 (AbortController + 2 s); refuters: COD-error-layer-12 admitted low, COD-plugins-11 admitted_with_correction low (fire-and-forget, 5 loaded rows, loopback). The port-0 half of COD-error-layer-12 is R15-LIFECYCLE-010.
entries.root_cause: The shared client has no timeout primitive, and plugin bootstrap re-derives state loadPlugin re-fetches.
entries.fix_shape: signal: AbortSignal.timeout(5_000) on the health probe; an optional signal param with a generous default timeout on sidecarGet/sidecarPost; pass the already-loaded PluginPersistedConfig into loadPlugin. Pin with a vitest that a never-resolving fetch mock makes resolveAndAwaitReady reject by the deadline.
entries.note: Verifier batch-8: live-confirmed the same mechanism from the outside -- after a transport failure sidecarFetch nulls readyPromise, so the *next* call re-runs the full 120 s /health probe before failing: call 1 took 3 ms, call 2 took 120,238 ms. Inside Tauri a crash now short-circuits this via Terminated (LIFECYCLE-010/UI-014), but a hung-not-exited engine still hits the full 120 s wait every time. || triage@e032be7: still_reproduces, confidence 4, health probe needs signal: AbortSignal.timeout; a default timeout on sidecarRequest; pass persisted into loadPlugin, evidence docs/redesign/verification/r15/stage-c/lows-triage/LOWS_TRIAGE.json#R15-LIFECYCLE-027

entries.fix_shape: Carry a last_error field on the snapshot and let refresh() re-derive the state. Pin with a test: state error + a healthy container -> refresh() -> ready with last_error still reported.

entries.title: A bare TCP connect is logged as 'Python sidecar healthy' and used to publish the MCP discovery file
entries.repro: Design: wait_for_port_timeout returns true for any process accepting on 127.0.0.1:<port>; pick_free_port drops the listener before the child binds, and the port is picked before the up-to-90 s MCP join, so a foreign listener in that window makes the core publish its address.
entries.evidence: src-tauri/src/lib.rs:30-33, :46-55, :260-265, :440, src-tauri/src/openbb_mcp.rs:178, docs/research/phase-10/hunt-rust-tauri.md BUG 5; refuter admitted_with_correction low (frontend gates on its own GET /health, so only the log line and discovery file are affected)
entries.root_cause: The evidence (a TCP handshake) cannot support the conclusion the caller states.
entries.fix_shape: Replace the bare connect with a GET /health matching a known field before logging healthy / writing the discovery file. Pin with a Rust test that a plain TCP listener does not pass the check.
entries.note: triage@e032be7: still_reproduces, confidence 5, hand-rolled HTTP over std TcpStream to avoid a new crate; only the main sidecar changes, evidence docs/redesign/verification/r15/stage-c/lows-triage/evidence/R15-LIFECYCLE-038/

entries.title: The smoke-test PID ledger is a fixed-path multi-writer file with an unconditional clear: a concurrent run's pre-flight tree-kills the other run's live sidecars and interleaved writes lose rows

entries.evidence: scripts/smoke-test-sidecars.mjs:118-119, :122-150, :160-189, :323; refuter admitted_with_correction low (consequence corrected to a spurious failure of the other run)

entries.note: triage@e032be7: still_reproduces, confidence 4, script-local; needs an owner-pid field and a glob, evidence docs/redesign/verification/r15/stage-c/lows-triage/evidence/R15-LIFECYCLE-039/

entries.root_cause: The two tuning constants live in different modules and their coincidence collapses 'consecutive bad searches' into 'one bad search'.

entries.note: Batch-7 (e81c9e7) certified: One search that fails both attempts (2 engine calls) leaves the breaker `closed` with 1 failure; a second failed search opens it.

entries.title: adr_ratio.lookup does not cache an exception miss, so a hanging or unreachable EDGAR stalls every fundamentals/financial_statements call for that symbol
entries.repro: adr_ratio.lookup() catches Exception from _fetch() (adr_ratio.py:141-145) and returns None on the exception path without caching a miss (data_cache.set is only reached on the non-exception path, line 146). _TIMEOUT is 60s per EDGAR HTTP request and _fetch makes up to two sequential requests, so an unreachable or slow EDGAR is re-fetched in full (up to ~120s) on every fundamentals/financial_statements call for that symbol, instead of being cached as a miss for _MISS_TTL the way a clean 'no data' result is.
entries.evidence: sidecar/services/adr_ratio.py:131-147 (lookup/_fetch); docs/redesign/verification/r15/stage-c/batch-15/PLAN.md (adr_ratio.lookup design: 'caches hits for 30 d and misses for 24 h ... and never' re-fetches a cached miss)
entries.root_cause: lookup()'s except branch returns early without calling data_cache.set(f'{key}:miss', {}), so only a clean not-found result (a successful fetch that finds no ratio) is cached as a miss; a network/timeout exception is retried in full on every call.
entries.fix_shape: Cache the miss on the exception path too (data_cache.set(f'{key}:miss', {}) before returning None in the except branch); pin with a test that makes _fetch raise and asserts a second lookup() call for the same symbol does not re-invoke _fetch.
entries.note: batch-16: filed from the lead's review of batch-15's adr_ratio.py (services/adr_ratio.py:141-146): the except branch never caches, so a hanging/unreachable EDGAR (60s timeout per request) is retried in full on every call rather than cached as a miss for _MISS_TTL.

entries.title: The chat history's '[tool steps: …]' trailer lives inside the assistant `content` string, so llama3.1:8b echoes it back as if it were its own prose
entries.repro: Turn 1: POST /copilot (or vy.py invoke copilot) with prompt "What is AAPL's market cap?", provider ollama, model llama3.1:8b, autonomy ask — the agent calls `fundamentals` and answers "The market cap of AAPL is $4.90T.". Client-side, chat-history.ts's `historyForSend` calls `withTrailer` on that stored assistant turn, producing content "The market cap of AAPL is $4.90T.\n\n[tool steps: Using fundamentals]" (readToolLabel's default-case label for the fundamentals tool). Turn 2: send that history plus prompt "Which tool gave you that market cap figure? Show exactly what it returned." against the same session/port. The model's turn-2 answer streams the trailer text verbatim back inside its prose.
entries.evidence:
docs/redesign/verification/r15/stage-c/batch-17/verifier-evidence/followup-aapl-2-t2.txt:11-15 (ASSISTANT TEXT: "The market cap of AAPL is $4.90T.

[tool steps: Using fundamentals]

This result was returned by the fundamentals tool…"); followup-aapl-2-history.json:8 (turn-1 content sent as history already carries the trailer: "The market cap of AAPL is $4.90T.

[tool steps: Using fundamentals]"); VERDICTS.md:95-96 ("llama3.1:8b echoed the client's history trailer … into its own answer text").
entries.root_cause: chat-history.ts `withTrailer` (used by `historyForSend`, ~line 300) appends the bracketed "[tool steps: …]" bookkeeping line straight into the assistant turn's `content` string that goes out over the wire as ordinary chat-history prose — there is no separate metadata channel or role for it, and no client-side stripping before the next model call. The label text itself comes from `readToolLabel` in ChatSidebar.tsx (default case: `Using ${name}`). From the model's point of view the trailer is indistinguishable from the rest of its own prior answer, so a model that reads its own history back (llama3.1:8b, asked to "show exactly what it returned") can and does reproduce it.
entries.fix_shape: src/store/chat-history.ts: stop folding the trailer into the `content` sent as history — either omit it from `historyForSend`'s payload entirely (the tool-call record is already reconstructable from `toolSteps`/the agent runtime's own trace, so the model does not need it echoed back), or carry it as a distinct system-role history line (e.g. a separate `{role:"system", content:"prior turn used tools: …"}` entry) instead of appending it inside the assistant `content` a chat model treats as quotable prose.

entries.title: Background India fundamentals warming passes bare screener-universe symbols to the correctness gate, which never strips yfinance's Emerge (SME) '-SM' infix, so every NSE Emerge symbol fails as a symbol mismatch
entries.repro: With config.get_region() == "IN", let the boot-started `fundamentals_warm` deep crawler (services/fundamentals_warm.py `_crawl_batch`/`_one`, started beside `screener.start_warm_precompute`) run a cycle over the india-all universe; or directly call `await provider_registry.get_fundamentals("INSPIRE")` (or IPHL, ISHAN — any NSE Emerge/SME-listed symbol) with region IN. yfinance_provider resolves the bare symbol to Yahoo's `INSPIRE-SM.NS` form and returns `Fundamentals(symbol="INSPIRE-SM.NS", …)`; provider_registry's `_fundamentals_validator` calls `correctness_gate.validate_fundamentals(result, "INSPIRE", "IN")`, which raises `CorrectnessError: … symbol mismatch`. The crawler's `except Exception` handler (fundamentals_warm.py) logs it at debug level and calls `mark_info_failure`, so the symbol never populates and silently rotates out for `TTL_INFO_RETRY_SECONDS` — deterministically, every cycle, since the mismatch is not transient.
entries.evidence: VERDICTS.md:97-99 ("During the MSFT run, the sidecar log showed a sweep of fundamentals calls for *-SM.NS symbols (INSPIRE-SM.NS, IPHL-SM.NS, ISHAN-SM.NS) that failed the correctness gate. This looks like background warming, not the agent."); no raw sidecar-log excerpt for this sweep was saved under verifier-evidence/ (sidecar-guard-lines.log:1 holds only the unrelated SIFY citation-guard line) — the mechanism below was traced by reading the code the remark implicates, per the filing brief's step 2.
entries.root_cause: correctness_gate.py's `_SUFFIX_RE` (line 59, `[.\-](NS|BO|BSE)$`) and `_match_key` (lines 116-128) strip only the exchange suffix (`.NS`/`.BO`/`.BSE`); they do not strip yfinance's Emerge-only `-SM` infix (added by `yfinance_provider._yahoo_symbol`, lines 155-157, for any `symbol_resolver.is_nse_emerge` name). `fundamentals_warm.py`'s deep crawler (line 363, `provider_registry.get_fundamentals(symbol)`) passes the bare india-all universe symbol (e.g. "INSPIRE") as `requested_symbol` straight through to `correctness_gate.validate_fundamentals`. `symbols_match("INSPIRE", "INSPIRE-SM.NS")` normalises the two sides to "INSPIRE" and "INSPIRESM" respectively — they do not match — so every SME/Emerge listing's fundamentals is rejected as a wrong-instrument result and never reaches the fundamentals store, regardless of how many times the crawler retries.
entries.fix_shape: sidecar/services/correctness_gate.py `_match_key`: also strip a trailing `-SM` (or `[\s_-]?SM`) infix before the exchange suffix comparison, the same way the sector-lookup already does ad hoc in yfinance_provider.py:772-773 (`bare.endswith("-SM")`) — centralise that stripping in `_match_key` so every caller (quotes, series, fundamentals) benefits, and pin it with a `symbols_match("INSPIRE", "INSPIRE-SM.NS") is True` case in test_correctness_gate.py.

entries.root_cause: Model behaviour: llama3.1:8b does not reliably honor an explicit in-prompt 'without calling any tool' instruction; the runtime dispatches whatever tool call the model emits without checking the turn's own prompt for a no-tool constraint.
entries.fix_shape: Not a guard/formatting fix. If pursued: have the runtime detect an explicit no-tool instruction in the user's turn and refuse/flag any tool call the model attempts that turn, rather than relying on the model to self-restrain; the write still lands behind the existing proposed-changes review gate either way. Pin with a scripted-provider test asserting no tool call is dispatched when the prompt carries an explicit no-tool instruction.

entries.title: The all-errored fabrication guard's replacement prose renders inside the original code fence, leaving a ```json block that contains a sentence instead of JSON
entries.repro:
Offline probe f-named-colon-fenced-json (batch-19 verifier-evidence/probe-fresh.out): every tool call in the turn errored; the model wrote 'After calling `fundamentals` for TATAMOTORS.NS, I got:

```json
{...fabricated...}
```'. The guard replaces the fabricated dump text but leaves the surrounding ```json fence in place, so the stream reads 'I got:

```json
The fundamentals tool returned no data for this in this turn.
```'. No figure leaks; cosmetic only.
entries.evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/stage-c/batch-19/VERDICTS.md 'Issues found' (cosmetic bullet); docs/redesign/verification/r15/stage-c/batch-19/verifier-evidence/probe-fresh.out:2
entries.root_cause: When the all-errored guard rewrites a sentence/paragraph it identifies as a fabricated dump, it does not also strip the enclosing ``` fence markers the model emitted around the original dump, so the replacement prose is left rendered as a fenced code block.
entries.fix_shape: When the guard replaces an all-errored dump, also strip any enclosing fence the original dump opened so the replacement renders as plain prose, not a code block. Pin with a test asserting the replacement text carries no fence markers.
entries.note:
batch-21 (not_certified, source batch-20/VERDICTS.json): The literal repro holds: f-named-colon-fenced-json now yields the note as prose with no ``` (b19v_probe/b20w_probe), and a fresh chunked ```text fence also renders as prose. The fix_shape ('strip any enclosing fence the original dump opened') and the acceptance ('the replacement carries no fence markers') fail on a fresh fence of the same class. For a CommonMark tilde fence, all-errored fundamentals, 'Here is the output:

~~~json
{"pe": 8.4, "roe": 0.214}
~~~

Hope that helps.' becomes 'The fundamentals tool returned no data for this in this turn.

~~~

Hope that helps.' (verifier-evidence/fresh.out v036-tilde-fence). The orphan closing ~~~ opens an unclosed code block that swallows the following prose. Cause: _FENCE_OPEN/_FENCE_CLOSE (agent_runtime.py:2084-2085) recognise backtick fences only. Base renders the note inside the ~~~json fence, so this is no regression. || batch-22 (not_certified, source batch-21/VERDICTS.json): The formatting claim holds for every CLOSED fence tried. The replacement renders as prose with no fence marker for: batch-20 v036-tilde-fence; fresh chunked ~~~~ with an info string; a ```` fence nesting ```json; a ~~~ closed by a longer ~~~~~; an indented ~~~ block; a mixed-turn ~~~ fence on an errored subject. An ok-result ~~~ block streams intact. Not certified, because the change that makes tildes fences also makes an UNCLOSED tilde fence invisible to the guard, so the fabricated dump inside it is neither replaced nor unfenced. All-errored fundamentals with 'Output:

~~~json
{"pe": 31.7}
' streams whole on this branch; base 4d9a7324 replaced it with the note. This is a regression on a fresh case of the fence class the entry fixes (verifier-evidence/unclosed.out, fresh2.out f036-unclosed-tilde). Cause: _fence_body (agent_runtime.py, unchanged) drops lines[-1] as the closer even when _seg_at found none (_Seg.closed False at end of stream). CommonMark closes an open fence at end of document. || batch-23 (not certified, cross-round fence, source batch-22/VERDICTS.md): same-round fences hold, but a fence opened one round earlier (a streamed ``` before a native tool call) stays open when the next round's replaced note renders, leaving the note inside an orphaned code block. Reproduces offline for ``` and ~~~; unchanged on base, not a regression.

entries.title: The fabrication guard grounds a stated figure by VALUE only, so an older bar buried in the same price_data payload counts as grounded for the current-price sentence
entries.repro: batch-22 verifier live c-short-ok: llama3.1:8b stated 'SBI (SBIN.NS) is ₹1082.0' as the current price; the running app's /quotes/SBIN.NS and screener.in both read ₹983.00 (25 Sep close). 1082.0 is a distinct, older bar value present elsewhere in the same price_data tool payload, so the guard's value-membership check treats the sentence as grounded even though it answers the wrong field (current price) with a stale one.
entries.evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/stage-c/batch-22/VERDICTS.md 'Issues (outside these entries; not in the diff)' item 2
entries.root_cause: The grounding check asks only whether a stated number appears anywhere in the turn's tool payloads, not whether it appears in the specific field the sentence claims to answer (e.g. current/last price vs a historical bar).
entries.fix_shape: Ground by field, not just value: resolve which payload field a price sentence claims (current/last vs a labelled historical point) and check membership against that field specifically; pin with a fixture whose payload carries two distinct numeric values for the same symbol (current price and an older bar) and assert only the current-price value grounds.

entries.title: Research brief citation-integrity net matches only a bare [n]; grouped markers [2, 3] and prose pseudo-citations [New findings] ship unresolved as literal text
entries.repro: Gate round 2 owner drive rc1-drive-research-briefs:2 at 4c6dfe8c, re-proved by the fresh verifier (rc1-verifier:3, r15/rc1/verifier/g2/fixloop-briefs2-citecheck.txt): MARKER_RE in citecheck.py:39 finds nothing in '[2, 3]' and brief-ingest.ts:396 renders '[New findings]' as literal text; a brief whose synthesis carries a grouped marker or a bracketed prose fragment passes the net with unresolved citations.
entries.evidence: docs/redesign/verification/R15_GATE_RC1.md (item 10), docs/redesign/verification/r15/rc1/findings/rc1-verifier.json (rc1-verifier:3), r15/rc1/fix-r1/PLAN.md, r15/rc1/fix-r2/RECHECK.md
entries.root_cause: sidecar/services/research/citecheck.py:39 MARKER_RE is a single-integer bracket grammar; src/lib/brief-ingest.ts:396 mirrors it, so any bracket the grammar rejects is neither resolved nor stripped and ships verbatim.
entries.fix_shape: One shared marker grammar on both sides of the wire: a bracket group is a citation iff every comma/en-dash separated token is an integer (with optional ranges); grouped markers resolve each index; a bracket whose content is not an integer list is prose and is neither resolved nor counted as a citation but IS flagged by the net as an unresolved pseudo-citation when it looks like one (capitalised words, no digits) — the brief fails the integrity check rather than shipping it. The two fix rounds of gate round 2 (Sonnet, r15/rc1/fix-r1 + fix-r2 on worktree-agent-rc1-4c6dfe8-fix-int@81fbfe91) patched the regex only and the recheck still reproduced live through both nets; the next attempt is a root-cause fix on Opus with a fresh case the fix was not written against.
entries.note: Filed by the lead 26 Sep after gate round 2 from the gate verifier finding (fresh-verifier concurrence on the four-area rule: rc1-verifier:3). Certification failures so far: 2 (gate round 2 fix rounds r1 and r2, recheck reproduced) — a third stops it for the operator.; batch-26 adjudication: stage-c batch-25 VERDICTS not_certified — The corpus and the planned fresh cases pass with byte-identical parity. But the implemented grammar ('a citation if ANY comma/semicolon token is an integer') departs from the register fix_shape ('a citation iff EVERY token is an integer'), and it manufactures citations out of numeric prose brackets. 'Shares outstanding [1,234 mn] at year end.' becomes '...[1] at year end.' on BOTH sides, a silent fabricated citation. 'A price target of [Rs 1,200] was set.' becomes 'A price target of was set.' (backend), erasing the figure. The plan's own rule 5 (a mid-sentence bracket is prose, left untouched) does not hold for them. Reverted at 3a674e7c; stays open at three certification failures (operator decision). Batch-26 lead adjudication (20:14 IST 26 Sep): THIRD certification failure at batch-25 — stops here for the operator under the three-failure rule; status blocked_tier4, DECISIONS_FOR_OPERATOR.md section 4.14 (the attempt 1288ec19 was reverted at 3a674e7c; the release line carries the original narrow-[n] behaviour; recommendation: one operator-approved Opus attempt with the every-token-integer grammar, else documented limitation). || rc1 gate round-3 verifier concurrence (rc1-verifier:9, batch-27 adjudication): rc1-drive-research-briefs:1 is the same citation-integrity-net class (grouped/prose markers ship unresolved). Concurred as the same known limitation, not a new defect; no fix round; DECISIONS_FOR_OPERATOR.md 4.14.

entries.title: Cold resolver-masters load under concurrent first resolves starves the shared to_thread pool, delaying unrelated work by ~9.4s even when yf.Search answers instantly
entries.repro: 12 concurrent first-resolve queries against a cold resolver-masters cache, with yf.Search stubbed to answer instantly, still leave an unrelated to_thread call waiting ~9.4s (batch-26 verifier, worktree-agent-batch-26-int@2e1950fe, sat-timed.py stub)
entries.evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/stage-c/batch-26/VERDICTS.md 'Issues noticed' item 1 (R15-AGENT-010 verification): the cold resolver-masters load runs on the shared default to_thread pool and saturates it independent of the Yahoo network leg AGENT-010 fixed
entries.root_cause: The resolver-masters cold load is scheduled on the same shared default to_thread executor as every other blocking call, so 12-way concurrent first resolves monopolise the pool regardless of how fast the network leg itself returns.
entries.fix_shape: Move the resolver-masters cold load off the shared default to_thread pool (a dedicated executor, or an eager warm-on-boot load) so concurrent first resolves cannot starve unrelated to_thread work. Test: with the masters cache cold and yf.Search stubbed instant, an unrelated to_thread call under 12-way concurrency completes without the pool-wait delay.

entries.title: The proposed-change review card and its applied label price a US lot in the session region's currency, not the listing's: {MSFT, 4, 480 USD} under an IN session reads 'Add 4 MSFT @ ₹480 to the portfolio'
entries.repro: Under region IN, an agent-staged portfolio_add_position {MSFT, 4, 480} (user said "480 dollars") shows on the review card and its applied label as "Add 4 MSFT @ ₹480 to the portfolio"; an order-attempt write reads "Add 10 AAPL @ ₹0". The ledger value itself is correct (480 USD); only the text the user reads and accepts is wrong.
entries.evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/rc1/round-3/GATE8.md 'rc1-gate8:1' (new_defect, low); docs/redesign/verification/r15/rc1/round-3/gate8.json:139; src/lib/host-actions.ts:657 (formatPrice), :1366-1383 (describeIntent), :1868 (applied label) all call currencySign(region) instead of the position's own listing currency, against D57 (cost basis is in the listing currency; the panel itself renders it with the quote's currency)
entries.root_cause: formatPrice signs every staged/applied price with the session region's currency symbol (currencySign(region)) instead of the position's listing currency, so a USD lot staged in an IN session is labelled in rupees while the stored value stays correctly denominated in USD.
entries.fix_shape: Have formatPrice (and describeIntent's callers) take the position's own currency (already resolved for the ledger write) instead of the session region, so the review-card and applied-label text always matches the value's real currency. Test: staging {MSFT, 4, 480} in an IN session renders "$480", not "₹480".

entries.title: Missing/invalid API key on OpenAI, Groq or another eagerly-validating provider surfaced the router's generic 'internal error, restart Vysted' frame instead of a humanized 'add your API key' message, on both /agents/{id}/invoke and /llm/chat
entries.repro: vy.py invoke copilot "hi" --provider openai --model gpt-4o-mini --mode agent --autonomy ask --no-key -> SSE {kind:error, message:'The terminal hit an internal error.', action:'... restart Vysted.', code:'internal'}; reproduced identically for provider=groq and via a direct /llm/chat curl for provider=openai. Anthropic on the same route correctly humanizes because its SDK defers key validation to request time.
entries.evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/rc1/round-3/findings/rc1-drive-composer-chat.json:1 (register_id null at the time of filing); docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/composer-chat/rc1/round-3/cc-20-err-nokey-openai.jsonl; fixed by ac0d8617 (fix(rc1): humanize no-key adapter errors to auth), merged 5ff9be04 and 5903f373; re-verified closed live per docs/redesign/verification/R15_GATE_RC1.md item 10 ('my re-run gives code auth, "No … API key is set"')
entries.root_cause: OpenAI's/Groq's SDK client constructor (self._client(api_key)) raises immediately on a missing key, before the adapter's own try/except in stream_chat, so the exception never reaches humanize() and instead falls through to the router's last-resort guard, which (per R15-AGENT-030's fix) unconditionally emits the generic internal-error frame rather than trying humanize(provider_id, exc) first.
entries.fix_shape: Already delivered: construct the SDK client inside the adapter's own try/except (or catch the constructor's exception explicitly) so a missing/invalid key still reaches humanize() before the router's last-resort guard. Test: a no-key OpenAI/Groq invoke gets code 'auth', not 'internal'.
